item.content:encoded:
Field Level Media

24 Sep 2026, 07:55 GMT+10

(Photo credit: Brad Penner)
Ryan McMahon hit a third-inning grand slam and tied a career high with five RBIs, while Ben Rice hit a pair of solo homers as the host New York Yankees rolled to a 9-2 victory over the Tampa Bay Rays on Wednesday night.
McMahon drove in five runs for the fourth time in his career and started his big night with a two-strike single off Tampa Bay spot starter Mason Englert (0-4) for a 2-0 lead in the second.
After George Lombard Jr. started the third with a homer to right-center field, McMahon lifted a full-count offering down the right field line for a 7-0 lead.
It was the third baseman's third career grand slam, and McMahon went deep after Anthony Volpe took ground balls at third before the game.
Rice homered on the first pitch of the contest from Englert to become the 13th Yankee with 40 homers in a season. After hitting his fourth career leadoff homer, Rice homered again into the right field seats for an 8-1 lead in the fourth.
Rice had his fifth career multi-homer game and became the seventh player to reach 40 homers this season. Rice also added a single and reached base four times.
The Yankees (91-67) won for the 10th time in 15 games. Rookie Spencer Jones doubled and scored on McMahon's RBI single in the second, while Heliot Ramos chipped in a sacrifice fly.
New York's Gerrit Cole (10-9) allowed two runs on three hits in 5 2/3 innings in a postseason tuneup. Cole struck out eight, walked three and reached double-digit victories for the 10th time in his career.
Jonny DeLuca hit an RBI double, and Cedric Mullins homered for the Rays (96-62), who fell three games behind Milwaukee for the best record in baseball.
After clinching their fifth AL East title on Tuesday, the Rays rested AL hits leader Yandy Diaz and played Junior Caminero for five innings.
Englert allowed eight runs on nine hits over 3 2/3 innings after Ian Seymour was originally slated to start for Tampa Bay. Seymour is expected to pitch in Thursday's series finale.
--Field Level Media

item.title: [nydailynews.com] Giancarlo Stanton, Carlos Lagrange, Game 1 starter among Yankees’ many playoff puzzle pieces
item.dc:creator: Gary Phillips
item.description: The postseason is right around the corner, and the Yankees have more question marks than The Riddler’s suit. item.content:encoded:
The postseason is right around the corner, and the Yankees have more question marks than The Riddler’s suit.
That’s not necessarily a bad thing, at least in some instances, as Aaron Boone revealed that some unexpected players could factor into the team’s postseason plans on Wednesday. While the Bombers don’t expect to have Aaron Judge (right calf strain) when they host the Wild Card series, which begins Sept. 29, Boone didn’t rule out a few faces who haven’t been seen in a while.
“There’s a lot to shake out and unfold over the next four or five days,” the manager said before the Yankees played the division-winning Rays on Wednesday. “Hopefully, we have a lot of options to choose from.”
THE RETURN OF STANTON (AND GRISHAM)?
Giancarlo Stanton, out since April 24 due to three separate calf strains (two right, one left), and Trent Grisham, sidelined by his second right hamstring strain of the season, took live at-bats in Somerset on Wednesday. Both ran the bases, and Boone said Stanton homered while getting six or seven at-bats.
“They’re knocking on the door,” Boone said, but he wasn’t sure if Stanton, a decorated postseason performer, could be ready for the Wild Card round.
The manager previously said that Grisham could be in play, though he wasn’t expected to be activated before the final five games of the regular season.
Asked what he would need to see from Stanton after a five-month layoff, Boone earnestly said, “I’m not sure.”
“I don’t know that answer,” he continued. “Obviously, there’ll be conversations with him. Does he fit on the roster? Is it realistic? All those things, and I can’t answer that right now.”
With the Yankees already log-jammed with first-base/DH types — Stanton can’t play the outfield anymore — Boone added that the former MVP would probably be used as a pinch-hitter, if anything. While not a big role, Stanton’s right-handed bat could be helpful off the bench if the Yankees face the lefty-heavy Red Sox, their likeliest opponent, in the Wild Card round.
Grisham, meanwhile, would give the Yankees an interesting choice in center field with Spencer Jones handling the position in his absence. Jones has outperformed Grisham at the plate, but both are shaky defenders, and the latter has postseason experience that the rookie does not.
LAGRANGE TO DEBUT?
“He’s in the conversation for something,” Boone said of flamethrowing pitching prospect Carlos Lagrange, who threw live batting practice on Wednesday.
But the skipper noted that a lot of “unknown” comes with righty, who has yet to make his major league debut, only recently returned from a shoulder sprain, and has just eight relief appearances under his belt this season. If the Yankees were to use Lagrange and his 100-plus-mph fastball, it would be out of the bullpen.
Asked why the Yankees don’t just promote Lagrange now, Boone said that they still have to cover innings over the last few games of the regular season. They would also have to clear space for him on the 40-man and active rosters.
While Lagrange is 23 and Stanton is 36, both are in similar positions in that they offer the Yankees an intriguing combination of upside, mystery and risk. Asked how Boone might personally weigh all that as the Yankees prepare to make their postseason roster, he said the club will “make the best decision possible” “if those guys are truly pushing into the conversation.”
“Carlos is in the stay ready [phase]. G [got] at-bats today,” Boone said. “All, at least, putting them on the outskirts of the conversation, if nothing else.”
WHO STARTS GAME 1?
Cam Schlittler is the clear frontrunner to win the American League Cy Young Award. So he’s obviously going to start Game 1 of the Wild Card round, right?
“Not necessarily,” Boone said. “We’ll see. Whoever goes Game 1 or Game 2 doesn’t affect the next series. Whoever goes Game 1 or Game 2 can pitch Game 2 and Game 5 in the next series, for example. We’ll decide what makes the most sense, just matching up how we want to go with it. But Cam would certainly be one of those first two games.”
Gerrit Cole, who totaled two earned runs, three walks and eight strikeouts over 5.2 innings and 105 pitches on Wednesday against the Rays, is currently lined up for Game 1 of the Wild Card round on extra rest. The 2023 Cy Young winner, now 22 starts removed from Tommy John surgery, has struggled to get swing-and-miss this season. He’s also faltered against the Red Sox throughout his career. With Max Fried and Carlos Rodón also in the rotation, the case can be made that Cole has been the Yankees’ fourth-best starter lately.
Schlittler, who dominated Boston in last year’s Wild Card series, would be on regular rest if tabbed for Game 1. He is scheduled to make his final start of the regular season on Thursday.
VOLPE AT THIRD? MCMAHON OFF THE ROSTER?
With the lefty-swinging Ryan McMahon putting the finishing touches on an abysmal offensive season and taking a step back defensively, the righty-hitting Anthony Volpe did some pregame work at third base on Wednesday. Boone expects the shortstop turned second baseman to play the hot corner in one or two games before the regular season ends.
“Good to go,” Volpe, who played a few games at third in the minors this year, said of his comfort level at the position.
Meanwhile, José Caballero, another righty, has already gotten some starts at third over McMahon against right-handed pitching. If Volpe shows that he can handle third, it could increase the odds of the Yankees leaving McMahon off their Wild Card roster.
Boone said that he still sees McMahon as a “top-shelf” defender, but he entered Wednesday’s game with -2 Defensive Runs Saved and one Out Above Average, numbers well below career norms. Couple that with a 73 wRC+, and the $16 million man has not been a quality player, though he did hit a grand slam on Wednesday.
“I understand he’s had a couple misplays here along the way, but I want him in the game and the ball hit to him in a big spot,” Boone said. “Offensively, it’s been a struggle, especially in the second half and lately getting it going. But through his struggles that he’s had offensively, he’s gotten a lot of big hits for us, too, along the way.”
On the subject of third base, Boone also said that he hasn’t given much thought to Jazz Chisholm Jr. trying the position again. However, he’s not ruling it out.
WHAT ABOUT OTHER INJURED ARMS?
Fernando Cruz made a rather adamant appearance in the Yankees’ clubhouse on Wednesday. The reliever, out with a partially torn UCL, repeatedly said that he refused to “accept” the diagnosis.
“I had real good inflammation, real stiffness and irritation,” said Cruz, who isn’t considering surgery right now. “People can say it’s a partial tear, but in my heart, it’s not a partial tear.”
While it seems rather improbable that Cruz will pitch again this season, he said that that is his goal, and Boone didn’t rule out the possibility. The righty threw a touch-and-feel bullpen three days ago, and he plans to throw another bullpen on Thursday.
Meanwhile, Clarke Schmidt felt better playing catch on Wednesday than he did on Tuesday after experiencing some biceps cramping over the weekend. However, if the recently returned Tommy John patient is not a viable option by Thursday, “then we’ll probably go a different way,” Boone said, referring to the Yankees’ postseason roster plans.
Finally, Ryan Weathers isn’t expected to throw live batting practice until sometime during the Wild Card series, so he won’t be an option.
With Weathers ruled out and Schmidt’s status uncertain, it will be interesting to see how the Yankees fill out their Wild Card bullpen. On a related note, Boone said that he sees “no scenario” in which the team carries 13 pitchers for the series. They may not even roster 12, he said with so many balls up in the air.
“It depends who’s available and who’s not,” Boone said.

item.content:encoded:
Cody Bellinger is out of the New York Yankees lineup for Wednesday night's game against the Tampa Bay Rays, but no injury has been reported.
With the top American League wild-card spot secured and Aaron Judge sidelined, the open question is how many at-bats Bellinger takes into a best-of-three series that starts in six days, most likely against the Boston Red Sox.
José Caballero moves into left field against Rays right-hander Mason Englert, according to CBS Sports. The site found nothing pointing to a physical problem and characterized the absence as a pre-playoff day off.
The timing follows a cold stretch. Bellinger opened September by hitting .373 through his first 14 games of the month, then managed just three hits in his next 20 at-bats.
He managed to come through on Tuesday. His fourth-inning, two-run homer off Nick Martinez, his 17th of the season, was the only scoring in a 2-0 Game 1 win before Tampa Bay took the nightcap of a doubleheader 6-1 and clinched the American League East.

| SP: Gerrit Cole (RHP #45) • 9-9, 3.63 ERA, 123 K | | | | |
| September 23, 2026 • Yankee Stadium, Bronx, NY • 7:05 PM EDT • Rays at Yankees | | | | |
| # | Player | Pos | AVG | OPS |

| 2 | George Lombard Jr. | SS | .237 | .670 |
| 3 | Luis García Jr. | 1B | .277 | .832 |
| 4 | Heliot Ramos | RF | .239 | .707 |
| 5 | Spencer Jones | CF | .246 | .751 |
| 6 | Jazz Chisholm Jr. | 2B | .233 | .716 |
| 7 | José Caballero | LF | .236 | .666 |
| 8 | Ryan McMahon | 3B | .206 | .615 |
| 9 | Ali Sánchez | C | .241 | .569 |
| Season stats shown (AVG / OPS). Rays lineup not yet available. Lineups subject to change. | | | | |
Yankees Rest Plan Includes Cody Bellinger
After the doubleheader, manager Aaron Boone singled out Bellinger, catcher Austin Wells and outfielder Spencer Jones as regulars due for rest over the final week, according to Yankees beat writer Gary Phillips.
"As best we can, we'll get ourselves sharp. They're real games, so we're playing, but I definitely will pick some spots to get some guys down. Some of our leverage guys in the 'pen, we want them pitching, but we'll be very selective in how we do it," Boone said as quoted by MLB.com's Bryan Hoch.
Gerrit Cole starts Wednesday, and Cam Schlittler follows Thursday before a three-game series against the Baltimore Orioles closes the schedule, according to Hoch.
At 90-67, New York holds the No. 4 seed and will host the No. 5 seed in the Wild Card Series opening Sept. 29, according to MLB.com. The Boston Red Sox, at 84-73, are the likeliest opponent.
Judge will not be part of it. Boone said the captain has a "moderate" right calf strain and is not expected back for that round, according to Hoch.
"Missing Judge, it hurts. We all know he's the best hitter in the game. For us in here, our mindset is, we're going to have to find a way," Bellinger said, as quoted by Hoch.
Bellinger Career Resume
Bellinger's September line sits at .338/.351/.581 with five homers and 14 RBI, according to Yardbarker. He has appeared in 76 playoff games, hitting 10 homers and driving in 37 runs.
Bellinger was born July 13, 1995, in Scottsdale, Arizona. The Los Angeles Dodgers drafted him in the fourth round in 2013, straight out of Chandler's Hamilton High School. He won National League Rookie of the Year in 2017 and NL MVP in 2019, when he hit .305 with 47 homers.
His path also runs through a 2020 World Series title with the Dodgers and two seasons with the Chicago Cubs. New York acquired him in a December 2024 trade and, after a 2025 season of 29 homers and 98 RBI, re-signed him in January to a five-year, $162.5 million contract that gives him two opt-out chances and full no-trade protection, according to Bronx Pinstripes.
Limited to 130 games by a 25-game injured-list stint for a left hamstring strain, Bellinger is hitting .268 this season with 17 homers, 73 RBI and 12 stolen bases. His career totals stand at 242 home runs and 768 RBI.

They split the two games on Tuesday.
Most recently, the Yankees lost 6-1.
George Lombard Jr. (who batted 7th) finished with one hit, one RBI and one strikeout.
Yankees Announce George Lombard Jr. Change
For Wednesday’s game, the Yankees have announced their starting lineup.
FantasyPros wrote: “NYY Yankees Lineup 09/23 1. Ben Rice DH 2. George Lombard SS 3. Luis Garcia 1B 4. Heliot Ramos RF 5. Spencer Jones CF 6. Jazz Chisholm Jr. 2B 7. Jose Caballero LF 8. Ryan McMahon 3B 9. Ali Sanchez C”
Lombard Jr. has been moved up to the 2nd spot in the order on Wednesday.
The 21-year-old rookie made his MLB debut last month.
He comes into the night batting .237 with 33 hits, five home runs, 18 RBIs, 20 runs and two stolen bases in 39 games.

item.content:encoded:
Updated Yankees projected Wild Card Series roster without Aaron Judge
NEW YORK - Here was the scenario these Yankees hoped to avoid, but couldn't - a triumphant Tampa Bay Rays team, celebrating their AL East title on Bronx turf.
"They've put together a fantastic regular season to earn that,'' said manager Aaron Boone, after the Rays' 6-1 victory in Tuesday's nightcap of a split doubleheader at Yankee Stadium.
"Hopefully, we get another crack at them.''
That would be in a best-of-five AL Division Series, but only if the Yankees advance from a best-of-three Wild Card series, which they'll host - likely against the rival Red Sox.
With that Wild Card opponent in mind, here is our updated version of a Yankees 26-man playoff roster (12 pitchers, 14 position players), for a series that would begin on Tuesday, Sept. 29.
Rosters can be altered before each postseason round. Injured players can be replaced in-series (pitcher for pitcher, position player for position player) but the injured player is ineligible for the next playoff series.
Projected Yankees pitchers (12)
Starters (3): RHPs Cam Schlittler, Gerrit Cole; LHP Max Fried.
Relievers (9): RHPs David Bednar, Paul Blackburn, Will Warren, Michael Fulmer, John Schreiber; LHPs Ryan Weathers, Tim Hill, Brent Headrick, Carlos Rodon.
On the bubble: RHPs Clarke Schmidt.
Also available: RHPs Luis Gil, Elmer Rodriguez, Yerry de los Santos, Bradley Hanner, Carlos Lagrange; LHP Ryan Yarbrough.
Currently injured: RHPs Fernando Cruz, Angel Chivilli, Kervin Castro.
Analysis: Would the Yanks start anyone but Schlittler in Game 1?
Well, nothing's been firmly stated about the first round rotation, though Schlittler - the odds-on choice for the AL Cy Young Award - would be on normal rest for the opener.
Cole (Wednesday) and Schlittler (Thursday) will make their final regular season starts during this Rays series, though Boone mentioned limiting both starters in these tune-ups for postseason.
In the bullpen, Schmidt's recent bout of biceps cramping wasn't fully resolved as of Tuesday; he was due to be re-examined after a throwing session.
It's possible that even a slight setback takes Schmidt out of consideration for an important playoff spot, moving Michael Fulmer off the bubble and on the roster.
Rodon's eight shutout innings in Tuesday's doubleheader opener was his best effort, during an impressive stretch drive.
He'd be certain to start Game 1 or 2 of a Division Series vs. the Rays, but the Yanks might need his services - in some capacity - to advance vs. Boston, so he's now included here.
Projected Yankees infielders, utility/DH (9)
Infielders (7): Luis Garcia Jr., 1B; Paul Goldschmidt, 1B; Ben Rice, 1B-DH; Jazz Chisholm Jr., 2B; George Lombard Jr., SS; Anthony Volpe, 2B-SS; Ryan McMahon, 3B.
Utility players: (2): Jose Caballero, IF-OF; Amed Rosario, 3B-2B.
On the bubble: None.
Also available: Max Schuemann.
Analysis: Garcia and McMahon are slumping at the wrong time, while Chisholm - who just returned off the IL (right thumb sprain) on Tuesday - has this week to find his rhythm again at the plate.
But that trio of lefty hitters might all be starting on the bench against Boston, which could employ three lefty starters against the Yanks.
That puts Caballero in play as a third base option, with the veteran Goldschmidt (.997 OPS vs. lefties) at first base, the rookie Lombard at short, and Volpe recast as a second baseman.
Projected Yankees outfielders (3)
Cody Bellinger, Spencer Jones, Heliot Ramos.
On the bubble: None.
Also available: Jasson Dominguez.
Currently injured: Aaron Judge, Trent Grisham.
Analysis: That's a thin outfield without Judge, whom the Yanks are not planning to have for at least the Wild Card series - per Boone - due to the captain's "moderate'' right calf strain.
It's increasingly unlikely that Grisham (strained hamstring) is available, too, by next week, and that presents a danger considering Ramos' defensive deficiencies.
For that same reason, Dominguez is on the outside. Mostly, the Yanks need the potent right-handed bats of Ramos (who has found his hitting groove) and Rosario to combat Boston's lefty pitching.
Caballero could find himself pressed into outfield duty, too.
Without Judge, "it's going to be super tough on us,'' said Ramos. "But we're going to go forward, for sure.''
Yankees' projected catchers (2)
Austin Wells, Ali Sanchez.
On the bubble: None.
Also available: J.C. Escarra.
Analysis: Wells has been a better offensive presence after a brutal first half, and Sanchez has learned the staff and he earned much praise from Rodon for his contribution to Tuesday's game one win.
Boone has kept the Cole-Wells pairing together, and you'd still anticipate Wells getting starts vs. Boston's lefty starters throughout this opening series.

item.content:encoded:
NUEVA YORK – La noticia sobre el regreso de Aaron Judge a la lista de lesionados aún estaba fresca, habiendo sido anunciada menos de una hora antes, y ya Cody Bellinger estaba imaginando cómo los Yankees podían tener éxito en la postemporada sin su capitán.
Desafortunadamente para Judge y su club, han tenido mucha práctica haciendo exactamente eso esta temporada. No han tenido otra opción.
"Falta Judge y duele", dijo Bellinger. "Todos sabemos que él es el mejor bateador del juego. Para nosotros aquí, nuestra mentalidad es que vamos a tener que encontrar la manera. Creo que el talento en este clubhouse habla por sí mismo. Estoy completamente seguro de que tenemos suficiente talento aquí para salir, ganar y vencer a cualquiera.
Ahora tendrán su oportunidad para demostrarlo.
El manager de los Yankees, Aaron Boone, confirmó el martes que Judge está lidiando con un esguince "moderado" de la pantorrilla derecha y no se espera que esté listo para una posible Serie del Comodín de la Liga Americana contra los Medias Rojas, que comenzaría el 29 de septiembre.
La disponibilidad de Judge para las rondas posteriores, especialmente la Serie Divisional de la Liga Americana, también está en duda. Pero los Yankees necesitan llegar allí primero. Aquí hay cinco motivos por los que los Yankees, elogiados como favoritos para ganar el banderín, aún pueden llegar a la Serie Mundial incluso si Judge no regresa:
Lanzadores abridores dominantes
**
Cuando Carlos Rodón lanzó ocho entradas sin permitir carreras en la **victoria por 2-0 del martes sobre los Rays, no sólo mantuvo el champán en el clubhouse de Tampa Bay (por el momento), sino que también sirvió como un recordatorio de la mayor fortaleza de los Yankees.
Rodón podría ni siquiera abrir un partido en una posible Serie de Comodines, quedando detrás de los favoritos al premio Cy Young de la Liga Americana, Cam Schlittler, Gerrit Cole y Max Fried. En pocas palabras, la rotación los ha mantenido a flote.
Los abridores de los Yankees han permitido dos carreras limpias o menos en 40 de 51 aperturas desde el 28 de julio, incluyendo una carrera limpia o menos en 33 de esas aperturas, acumulando efectividad de 2.50 en ese período. En general, han permitido una carrera o menos en 65 encuentros, un récord de franquicia en una sola campaña.
"Venimos a ganar cada partido, sin importar quién esté en el terreno", dijo Rodón. "Obviamente, es difícil cuando no tienes al mejor jugador del mundo en el terreno contigo. Tengo la esperanza de que vuelva. Pero... se trata simplemente de ganar juegos para nosotros.
Hay otro trueno
Esto no es el 2022, cuando los 62 jonrones de Judge establecieron un récord de la Liga Americana para una sola temporada y sirvieron como el motor indiscutible de la ofensiva. Principalmente debido a la lesión en la costilla, Judge se limitó a un promedio de .241, 18 vuelacercas y 41 impulsadas en 66 encuentros. Ben Rice asumió gran parte de la carga este año, cumpliendo con la predicción de la primavera de Boone de 39 cuadrangulares.
Bellinger sigue siendo una fuerza impactante, mientras que el aumento de la velocidad del bate del dominicano Luis García Jr. sugiere que su producción es sostenible, a pesar de una reciente caída. Mientras tanto, el puertorriqueño Heliot Ramos ha mostrado poder después de un comienzo lento y se confiará en él en los playoffs contra lanzadores zurdos.
"Sabemos que somos capaces de ganar partidos", dijo Boone, quien señaló el récord de 36-24 del club desde el descanso del Juego de las Estrellas, la mayor parte del cual ocurrió sin Judge. "Nos hemos tenido que enfrentar a jugar sin muchas piezas clave en diferentes momentos y durante grandes tramos de esta campaña”.
**Los jóvenes pueden dar la cara
**
El cubano-estadounidense George Lombard Jr. y Spencer Jones llamaron la atención durante la reciente serie del club contra los Diamondbacks, cuando dieron jonrones con un total combinado de 872 pies calculados por Statcast contra Corbin Burnes – potentes batazos de 424 y 448 pies, respectivamente, que sugieren que se están sintiendo más cómodos en Grandes Ligas.
Ha habido algunos obstáculos durante sus primeros meses de actividad en las Mayores, con Lombard cometiendo errores en seis compromisos consecutivos en un período y Jones mostrando los swings en blanco que probablemente siempre sean parte de su juego. Pero el talento es real y nadie debería sorprenderse si alguno de los novatos brilla en un gran momento de octubre.
"Realmente sólo tenemos que jugar uno para el otro; apoyarnos mutuamente, pasar la batuta", dijo Bellinger. "Haces tu trabajo y controlas lo que puedes”.
Mejorando la salud
Mientras la situación de Judge no está clara, los Yankees están volviendo lentamente a estar completos.
Jazz Chisholm Jr. fue activado de la lista de lesionados entre los juego de la doble-jornada del martes, restaurando una presencia dinámica. Ha sido un año decepcionante en general, pero Chisholm estaba en racha en el momento de su lesión (de 46-18, .391). Los Yankees esperarán que retome eso.
Mientras tanto, Anthony Volpe aprovechó al máximo una oportunidad ante la ausencia de Chisholm, lo que podría haberle valido un lugar en el roster de playoffs, especialmente si los Yankees optan por contar con 11 lanzadores y 15 jugadores de posición en la primera ronda. Se cree que Trent Grisham está en la contienda para el roster.
"Con suerte, más personas podrán unirse y hacernos más formidables en el camino", dijo Boone.
Un bullpen reforzado
Los relevistas de los Yankees han estado entre los mejores de Grandes Ligas todo el año, pero ha habido señales preocupantes últimamente. Brent Headrick ocupa el segundo lugar en las Grandes Ligas con 79 presentaciones y ha mostrado una velocidad inconsistente. Mientras tanto, David Bednar y Paul Blackburn siguen en buena forma.
Debido a que los Yankees no tendrían por qué para a tener cinco abridores en octubre, la ayuda está en camino. Will Warren tiene programada una última apertura y luego pasará a un rol de relevista, dando al bullpen una opción intrigante de múltiples entradas. Clarke Schmidt y Ryan Weathers también están en consideración.
"Eso es lo bueno de la postemporada; los muchachos caen en diferentes roles y muchas veces pueden ser heroicos en papeles que no necesariamente imaginabas al inicio de la temporada", expresó Boone.

item.title: [Yahoo Sports] Yankees’ Aaron Boone Delivers Clear Max Fried Verdict Before Playoffs
item.dc:creator: Keith Watkins
item.description: The New York Yankees saw the Tampa Bay Rays claim the AL East crown at Yankee Stadium on Tuesday night. A 6-1 loss in the nightcap of a doubleheader split ended whatever remained of the division chase and confirmed what had felt inevitable for weeks. The Yankees are headed to the Wild Card Series. item.content:encoded:
The New York Yankees saw the Tampa Bay Rays claim the AL East crown at Yankee Stadium on Tuesday night. A 6-1 loss in the nightcap of a doubleheader split ended whatever remained of the division chase and confirmed what had felt inevitable for weeks. The Yankees are headed to the Wild Card Series.
The sting of the celebration was real. So was the pragmatism that followed it. With five regular season games remaining and the postseason less than a week away, manager Aaron Boone's focus has already shifted to October.
His assessment of one pitcher in particular made that clear.
Boone's Comments on Fried
Max Fried will not pitch again in the regular season. Tuesday's start against the Rays was his final tuneup before the playoffs.
"I think he looks great," Boone said. "I thought he was really good tonight. He threw the ball well. His curveball was really, really good tonight. Cutter was there. For the most part, was filling up the strike zone really well."
Fried's night unraveled in the seventh when a bunt play went sideways and three runs came in. Before that, he had been efficient and sharp. Boone saw a pitcher who is ready for October, not one who got tagged for four runs.
"He managed contact really well. I thought he was efficient," Boone said. "He's in a good place ready to go. Looking forward to seeing him out there in the postseason now."
Managing the Final Five Games
With the standings locked in, Boone outlined how the Yankees will approach the rest of the week. The priority is keeping players sharp without wearing anyone down.
"Getting guys ready, picking some days for some guys to get off," Boone said. "We're the real game. So we're playing. But I will pick some spots to get some guys down."
Cody Bellinger and Austin Wells are candidates for rest days. Spencer Jones may get a day to manage. Boone also mentioned experimenting with defensive positions and being selective about when leverage relievers pitch.
The balance is delicate. The games do not matter in the standings. The rhythm and preparation matter for everything that comes after.
Final Word for the Yankees
The division belongs to Tampa Bay. The Yankees know it. They watched the celebration and walked off their own field.
What happens next is the only thing that counts. Fried is ready. Cole and Schlittler are lined up. The rotation has three arms capable of winning a postseason start.
The Wild Card Series begins next week, with a Red Sox series in the Bronx the most likely outcome. Boone's message on Tuesday was simple. His team is not done. The pitching is in place. Now it is time to prove it matters.
This article was originally published on HEAVY
The post Yankees' Aaron Boone Delivers Clear Max Fried Verdict Before Playoffs appeared first on HEAVY.

item.title: [El Imparcial] ¿Qué le pasó a Aaron Judge? La lesión por la que recibió una inyección y pone en riesgo su participación en los Playoffs de MLB 2026
item.dc:creator: Patrizio Caro
item.description: ¿Qué le pasó a Aaron Judge? La lesión por la que recibió una inyección y pone en riesgo su participación en los Playoffs de MLB 2026 El capitán de los Yankees recibió una inyección para tratar su nueva lesión. Te explicamos qué le pasó, cuándo podría regresar y cómo llegan los Yankees a los Playoffs de MLB 2026. Los New York Yankees podrían comenzar los Playoffs de MLB 2026 sin Aaron Judge. El capitán del equipo sufrió una nueva lesión en la pantorrilla derecha y recibió una inyección de plasma
item.content:encoded:
¿Qué le pasó a Aaron Judge? La lesión por la que recibió una inyección y pone en riesgo su participación en los Playoffs de MLB 2026
El capitán de los Yankees recibió una inyección para tratar su nueva lesión. Te explicamos qué le pasó, cuándo podría regresar y cómo llegan los Yankees a los Playoffs de MLB 2026.
Los New York Yankees podrían comenzar los Playoffs de MLB 2026 sin Aaron Judge. El capitán del equipo sufrió una nueva lesión en la pantorrilla derecha y recibió una inyección de plasma el lunes 21 de septiembre, en un intento por favorecer su recuperación antes del inicio de la postemporada.
El mánager Aaron Boone confirmó este martes que el jardinero presenta una distensión muscular moderada y que la organización está preparando la Serie de Comodines, programada para comenzar el 29 de septiembre, sin contar con él. No obstante, todavía no está descartado oficialmente.
La situación llega en un momento complicado para Judge, quien apenas había regresado de una fractura en una costilla que lo mantuvo fuera de actividad durante más de tres meses. Mientras tanto, los Yankees ya aseguraron su clasificación a los Playoffs, aunque terminaron perdiendo la División Este de la Liga Americana ante los Tampa Bay Rays.
¿Qué le pasó a Aaron Judge y cuál es su nueva lesión?
Aaron Judge sufrió una distensión moderada del músculo sóleo de la pantorrilla derecha el miércoles 16 de septiembre, durante el encuentro de los Yankees contra los Minnesota Twins.
El bateador de 34 años comenzó a sentir molestias desde la primera entrada, pero decidió mantenerse en el partido. Finalmente, tuvo que abandonar el encuentro en el sexto episodio y fue reemplazado por Heliot Ramos.
Al día siguiente, una resonancia magnética confirmó la lesión muscular. El sábado 19 de septiembre, los Yankees colocaron a Judge en la lista de lesionados de 10 días, con efecto retroactivo al jueves 17.
El sóleo es un músculo que se encuentra en la parte posterior de la pierna, debajo de los gemelos. Participa en movimientos fundamentales para un beisbolista, como correr, impulsarse y mantener la estabilidad.
¿Por qué le inyectaron plasma a Aaron Judge y en qué consiste el tratamiento?
La novedad de su recuperación
El lunes 21 de septiembre, durante el día de descanso de los Yankees, Aaron Judge recibió una inyección de plasma pobre en plaquetas (PPP) en la pantorrilla derecha.
La inyección forma parte del tratamiento médico que está recibiendo Judge para intentar favorecer la recuperación de su lesión muscular. Sin embargo, el procedimiento no garantiza una recuperación acelerada ni determina cuándo podrá regresar a los diamantes.
Tras la aplicación, Judge permanece con actividad física limitada mientras los servicios médicos del equipo evalúan su evolución.
¿Qué otras lesiones ha sufrido Aaron Judge durante la temporada 2026?
La lesión de pantorrilla representa otro episodio en una temporada marcada por los problemas físicos del capitán de los Yankees.
A finales de abril, Judge sufrió una fractura por estrés en la primera costilla del lado derecho, aparentemente durante una jugada defensiva contra los Houston Astros. Aunque continuó jugando varias semanas, las molestias aumentaron y finalmente tuvo que detener su actividad.
El 5 de junio, los Yankees anunciaron el diagnóstico. Judge permaneció fuera de los diamantes durante todo el verano y no regresó hasta el 8 de septiembre, cuando enfrentó a los Colorado Rockies.
Su retorno duró apenas siete encuentros antes de que apareciera la nueva lesión.
Cronología de las lesiones de Aaron Judge en 2026
| Fecha | ¿Qué sucedió? |
|---|---|
| 26 de abril | Sufrió la lesión que habría originado la fractura en una costilla. |
| 31 de mayo | Disputó su último partido antes de una ausencia de más de tres meses. |
| 5 de junio | Los Yankees confirmaron la fractura por estrés. |
| 8 de septiembre | Regresó a la alineación contra Colorado. |
| 16 de septiembre | Sufrió una distensión en la pantorrilla contra Minnesota. |
| 19 de septiembre | Ingresó a la lista de lesionados de 10 días. |
| 21 de septiembre | Recibió la inyección de plasma pobre en plaquetas. |
| 22 de septiembre | Boone confirmó la gravedad moderada de la distensión y expresó sus dudas sobre su disponibilidad para los Playoffs. |
¿Qué dijo Aaron Boone sobre la lesión de Aaron Judge?
El mánager de los Yankees actualizó el estado de su capitán este martes 22 de septiembre y reconoció que no espera tenerlo disponible para el comienzo de la postemporada.
Estamos planificando que no forme parte de ella".
Así explicó Boone la postura del equipo ante la próxima Serie de Comodines. Aunque no descartó definitivamente al bateador, los Yankees se preparan para afrontar los primeros encuentros de eliminación directa sin él.
El propio Judge había manifestado el sábado 19 de septiembre su deseo de estar recuperado para los Playoffs, pero reconoció que todavía no tenía respuestas sobre los plazos de su rehabilitación.
¿Cuándo volverá a jugar Aaron Judge con los Yankees?
La primera fecha en la que Judge podría ser activado es el domingo 27 de septiembre, cuando los Yankees disputarán su último encuentro de la temporada regular contra los Baltimore Orioles.
Sin embargo, esa fecha corresponde únicamente al cumplimiento del periodo mínimo de su estancia en la lista de lesionados. No significa que el jugador vaya a estar físicamente preparado para reaparecer.
La organización no ha anunciado una fecha definitiva para su regreso. Su disponibilidad dependerá de la recuperación muscular y de las evaluaciones médicas que se realicen durante los próximos días.
¿Aaron Judge jugará los Playoffs de MLB 2026?
Su participación en la primera ronda se encuentra seriamente comprometida.
La Serie de Comodines comienza el martes 29 de septiembre, solamente ocho días después de que Judge recibiera la inyección de plasma. La cercanía de ambas fechas y la gravedad moderada de la distensión explican por qué los Yankees están preparando su alineación sin el capitán.
Si Nueva York avanza a la Serie Divisional, programada para comenzar el 3 de octubre, Judge dispondría de algunos días adicionales de recuperación. Sin embargo, tampoco está garantizada su participación en esa instancia.
Por ahora, los Yankees mantienen abierta la posibilidad de su regreso durante la postemporada, pero no existe un calendario médico confirmado.
¿Cómo están los Yankees en la temporada 2026 y cuál es su situación rumbo a los Playoffs?
Clasificados a la postemporada
Los Yankees aseguraron su boleto a los Playoffs de MLB 2026 el 14 de septiembre, pero no consiguieron conquistar la División Este de la Liga Americana.
Este martes 22 de septiembre disputaron una doble cartelera contra los Tampa Bay Rays. Primero ganaron 2-0, resultado que les permitió asegurar la ventaja de local para la Serie de Comodines. Sin embargo, en el segundo encuentro cayeron 6-1 y Tampa Bay se proclamó campeón divisional.
Así quedó la División Este de la Liga Americana
Al cierre del martes 22 de septiembre
| Equipo | G | P |
|---|---|---|
| Rays (Campeón) | 96 | 61 |
| Yankees | 90 | 67 |
Los Rays aseguraron el primer sembrado de la Liga Americana, mientras que los Yankees disputarán la Serie de Comodines.
La derrota ante Tampa Bay dejó a los Yankees con cinco partidos pendientes de temporada regular. Ahora deberán concentrarse en llegar a la postemporada con su plantel recuperado y definir cómo cubrirán la ausencia de Judge.
¿Contra quién jugarían los Yankees en la Serie de Comodines de MLB 2026?
Los Boston Red Sox son el rival que actualmente aparece en el posible cruce de primera ronda contra los Yankees.
Boston también aseguró su clasificación a los Playoffs, por lo que ambos equipos podrían protagonizar otra serie de postemporada entre históricos rivales de la División Este.
La Serie de Comodines se disputa al mejor de tres partidos. El ganador avanzará a la Serie Divisional.
Nueva York ya aseguró que será local durante esta ronda, por lo que disputará en el Yankee Stadium todos los partidos que sean necesarios. El enfrentamiento definitivo dependerá de las posiciones al cierre de la temporada regular.
¿Quién reemplazará a Aaron Judge en la alineación de los Yankees?
Heliot Ramos es una de las alternativas que Boone ha utilizado en el jardín derecho. De hecho, fue el encargado de sustituir a Judge cuando abandonó el encuentro del 16 de septiembre contra Minnesota.
El equipo también cuenta con Cody Bellinger y Spencer Jones entre sus opciones para los jardines, mientras continúa evaluando la recuperación de Trent Grisham.
En la ofensiva, los Yankees también disponen de Ben Rice y recuperaron este martes a Jazz Chisholm Jr., quien había permanecido fuera por un esguince en el pulgar derecho.
La conformación definitiva del orden al bate y del roster para la Serie de Comodines dependerá de las decisiones de Boone y de la evolución de los peloteros lesionados.
¿Cuáles son los números de Aaron Judge en la temporada 2026 de MLB?
La prolongada ausencia de Judge ha reducido considerablemente sus estadísticas con respecto a sus temporadas anteriores.
En su regreso del 8 al 16 de septiembre, el capitán de los Yankees conectó cuatro imparables en 23 turnos, incluido un cuadrangular, y produjo tres carreras. También acumuló 13 ponches durante ese periodo.
Estadísticas de Aaron Judge en 2026
| Estadística | Total |
|---|---|
| Juegos | 66 |
| Promedio de bateo | .241 |
| Porcentaje de embasado | .360 |
| Slugging | .511 |
| Jonrones | 18 |
| Carreras impulsadas | 41 |
Estadísticas hasta su última participación, el 16 de septiembre.
¿Qué sigue para los Yankees antes del inicio de los Playoffs?
Con la División Este ya definida, los Yankees deberán aprovechar los últimos cinco encuentros de la temporada regular para preparar su participación en la Serie de Comodines.
Nueva York terminará su serie contra Tampa Bay y posteriormente recibirá a Baltimore del 25 al 27 de septiembre.
Mientras tanto, Boone deberá definir su rotación abridora, evaluar el regreso de otros jugadores lesionados y decidir qué peloteros integrarán el roster de postemporada.
La primera ronda comenzará el 29 de septiembre, mientras que las Series Divisionales están programadas para iniciar el 3 de octubre.

item.title: [mlb.com] 5 reasons the Yankees can win without Judge
item.dc:creator: Bryan Hoch

Unfortunately for Judge and his club, they’ve had plenty of practice doing exactly that this season. They’ve had no choice. “Missing Judge, it hurts,” Bellinger said. “We all know he’s the best hitter in the game. For us in here, our mindset is, we’re g
item.content:encoded:
NEW YORK – The news about Aaron Judge’s return to the injured list was still fresh, having been announced less than an hour earlier, and already Cody Bellinger was envisioning how the Yankees could succeed in the postseason without their captain.
Unfortunately for Judge and his club, they’ve had plenty of practice doing exactly that this season. They’ve had no choice.
“Missing Judge, it hurts,” Bellinger said. “We all know he’s the best hitter in the game. For us in here, our mindset is, we’re going to have to find a way. I think the talent in this locker room speaks for itself. I’m fully confident that we have enough talent in here to go out, win and beat anybody.”
Now they’ll have their chance to prove it.
Yankees manager Aaron Boone said Tuesday that Judge is dealing with a “moderate” strain of his right calf and is not expected to be ready for a potential American League Wild Card Series against the Red Sox, which would begin on Sept. 29.
Judge’s availability for subsequent rounds, especially the AL Division Series, is also in doubt. But the Yankees need to get there first. Here are five reasons why the Yankees, lauded as pennant favorites, still can reach the Fall Classic even if Judge doesn’t return:
Dominant starting pitching
Rodón might not even draw a start in a potential Wild Card Series, standing in line behind AL Cy Young Award frontrunner Cam Schlittler, Gerrit Cole and Max Fried. Simply put, the rotation has kept them afloat.
Yankees starters have permitted two earned runs or fewer in 40 of 51 starts since July 28, including one earned run or fewer in 33 of those starts, compiling a 2.50 ERA over that span. Overall, they’ve allowed one run or fewer in 65 games, a single-season franchise record.
“We come to win every game, regardless of who is on the field,” Rodón said. “Obviously it’s tough when you don’t have the best player in the world on the field with you. I’m hopeful that he’ll be back. But … it’s just about winning games for us.”
There’s other thump
This isn’t 2022, when Judge’s 62 home runs set a single-season AL record and served as the unquestioned engine of the offense. Mostly because of the rib injury, Judge was limited to a .241 average, 18 homers and 41 RBIs across 66 games. Ben Rice shouldered much of the load, fulfilling Boone’s spring prediction of 39 homers.
Bellinger remains an impactful force, while Luis García Jr.’s increased bat speed suggests his production is sustainable despite a recent slump. Meanwhile, Heliot Ramos has shown power after a sluggish start and will be leaned upon in the playoffs against left-handed pitching.
“We know we’re capable of winning games,” said Boone, who noted the club’s 36-24 record since the All-Star break, most of which occurred without Judge. “We’ve had to play without a lot of key pieces at different points and for large chunks of this season.”
The kids are all right
George Lombard Jr. and Spencer Jones opened eyes during the club’s recent series against the Diamondbacks, when they crushed a Statcast-calculated combined 872 feet of home runs against Corbin Burnes – big-boy blasts of 424 and 448 feet, respectively, that suggested they’re growing more comfortable in The Show.
There have been growing pains across their first months of big league activity, with Lombard committing errors in six consecutive games over one span and Jones showing the swing-and-miss that will probably always be part of his game. But the talent is real, and no one should be surprised if either rookie delivers in a big October moment.
“We really just have to play for each other; lean on each other, pass the baton,” Bellinger said. “You do your job and control what you can.”
Improving health
While Judge’s outlook is cloudy, the Yankees are slowly becoming more whole.
Jazz Chisholm Jr. was activated from the injured list between games of Tuesday’s doubleheader, restoring a dynamic presence. It has been a disappointing year overall, but Chisholm was hot at the time of his injury (18-for-46, .391). The Yanks will look for him to pick up where he left off.
Meanwhile, Anthony Volpe made the most of an opportunity in Chisholm’s absence, which could have earned him a spot on a playoff roster – especially if they go with 11 pitchers and 15 position players in the first round. Trent Grisham is thought to be in play for the playoff roster.
“Hopefully more people are able to join and make us more formidable along the way,” Boone said.
A bolstered bullpen
The Yankees’ relievers have been among the league’s best all year, but there have been concerning signs of late. Brent Headrick ranks second in the Majors with 79 appearances and has seen inconsistent velocity, for example, suggesting he could benefit from a breather once the AL East is decided. David Bednar and Paul Blackburn, meanwhile, remain sharp.
Because the Yankees would have no reason to roster five starting pitchers in October, help is on the way. Will Warren is scheduled to make one more start and then transition to a relief role, giving the ’pen an intriguing multi-inning option. Clarke Schmidt and Ryan Weathers are also in the mix.
“That’s the beauty of the postseason; guys fall into different roles and a lot of times can become heroic in roles you didn’t necessarily count on at the start of the season,” Boone said.

item.content:encoded:
Field Level Media

23 Sep 2026, 08:10 GMT+10

(Photo credit: Brad Penner)
Drew Rasmussen allowed one hit in 6 2/3 outstanding innings and the visiting Tampa Bay Rays clinched the AL East with a 6-1 victory over the New York Yankees on Tuesday night in the nightcap of a day-night doubleheader.
The Rays (96-61) won for the 20th time in 28 games and clinched their fifth division title. Tampa Bay last won the AL East in 2021 when it won a team-record 100 games.
Tampa Bay also claimed division titles in the pandemic shortened 2020 season, 2010 and 2008 and will head to the postseason as the top seed in the AL.
Rasmussen (16-5) took a no-hitter into the seventh until Heliot Ramos opened the inning with a double to left. Ramos eventually scored on an RBI single by rookie George Lombard Jr. off Kevin Kelly.
Rasmussen finished with 11 strikeouts for his fourth career double-digit strikeout performance. He finished two shy of his career-high set June 10 against the Boston Red Sox and the Rays won his 12th consecutive start.
Rasmussen threw a career-high 114 pitches and struck out New York leadoff hitter Ben Rice twice. He also struck out rookie Spencer Jones to end the fourth after allowing a walk to Cody Bellinger, who he fanned in the first inning.
The right-hander exited after walking Jazz Chisholm Jr. and Kelly retired Austin Wells following Lombard's hit.
Yandy Diaz drove in two runs with a single in the seventh off reliever John Schreiber. Diaz added another two-run single in the ninth. The Rays scored their first run in the third when Ryan Vilade grounded out against New York's Max Fried (5-5), scoring Taylor Walls.
Cam Booser pitched a 1-2-3 eighth and Bryan Baker put two on in the ninth before retiring Lombard to secure the division crown.
Fried allowed four runs on six hits in 6 2/3 innings. The left-hander struck out four, walked two and notched 10 ground ball outs.
--Field Level Media

item.content:encoded:
Rays' Drew Rasmussen loses no-hit bid in 7th inning on leadoff double by Heliot Ramos
NEW YORK (AP) — Tampa Bay right-hander Drew Rasmussen lost a no-hit bid against the New York Yankees on Tuesday night when Heliot Ramos led off the seventh inning with a double.
The Rays, attempting to clinch the AL East title, had a 4-0 lead when Ramos lined a 1-2 sinker to left field, two pitches after hitting a foul ball down the right field line.
Before losing his no-hit bid, Rasmussen had 10 strikeouts and has thrown 93 pitches, 59 for strikes through six innings.
Matt Garza is the only Tampa Bay pitcher to throw a no-hitter. Garza no-hit Detroit on July 26, 2010, at Tropicana Field.
Rasmussen ended the sixth inning by getting New York's Cody Bellinger on a flyball to right field.
Rasmussen walked Austin Wells with one out in the third and ended the inning by striking out Ben Rice on a high fastball. The 31-year-old issued a leadoff walk to Cody Bellinger and ended the fourth by striking out rookie Spencer Jones with a fastball.
Rasmussen got consecutive strikeouts on rookie George Lombard Jr. and Austin Wells to finish the fifth at 78 pitches.
The Rays can claim their fifth AL East title with a victory and took a 1-0 lead on Ryan Vilade’s groundout in the third against Max Fried. They added three in the seventh on a bunt single by Taylor Walls and a two-run base hit by Yandy Diaz.
The Yankees have been no-hit eight times. The last was a combined no-hitter by Houston’s Cristian Javier, Hector Neris and Ryan Pressly on June 25, 2022, at Yankee Stadium.

item.content:encoded:
When Aaron Judge is healthy, he’s the most dangerous hitter in baseball. Sometimes I get alarmed at how uncontroversial a statement that is; ours is a sport that so frequently humiliates those who make such sweeping, unequivocal judgments as those.
But the empirical evidence is what it is. Judge has played 150 or more games in a season four times in his career. In those four seasons, he’s led all position players in WAR four times and led the league in wRC+ three times. He’s been named AL MVP three times and finished second once, ahead of some real doozies: Cal Raleigh’s 60-homer year, Bobby Witt Jr.’s 10.5-WAR campaign in 2024, Shohei Ohtani’s best pitching season — in fact, a healthy Judge is the only thing that’s ever trumped a healthy Ohtani in an MVP race.
So again, it’s not uncontroversial to say that when Judge is healthy he’s the best hitter in the world. He has not, however, always been healthy. Least of all this season, when he missed three months with a broken rib. And now, the single-season AL home run king is back on the IL with a calf strain. The timing could not be worse.
Judge last played on Wednesday, leaving open the option to activate him on Sunday for the final game of the regular season. That seems like a theoretical concern at the moment rather than a practical one. Our Matt Martell was at Yankee manager Aaron Boone’s pregame media availability on Tuesday morning, where Boone illustrated the inadequacy of a return-to-play timeline at this point in the season.
“We’re planning on [Judge] not being a part of [the Wild Card Series],” Boone said. “You hear all the time with injuries, we give ranges: two to four weeks, four to six. They’re ranges for a reason. We’re at a point in the year where, obviously, we’d push it a little bit if that was in play, but that’s a week away. I’m not expecting it, but I’m not ruling it out either.”
That’s the problem. A range of two weeks in recovery time isn’t a big deal in a six-month season, but even one week is twice as long as the Yankees’ entire first playoff round. And muscle injuries can be finicky to begin with — you go to bed one night feeling fine and wake up the next morning with weakness or stiffness.
For what it’s worth, the Yankees are technically still alive in the AL East race as of this writing, but you can forgive Boone for speaking as if the division is already lost.
Either way, in order to speed things along, Judge received a platelet-poor plasma (PPP) injection on Monday, not to be confused with a platelet-rich plasma (PRP) injection.
Now, apparently having read The Magic School Bus Inside the Human Body as a child is not a sufficient qualification to perform surgery on live patients. At least, that’s what the police told me. But anyone who’s read that book can tell you the makeup of human blood: Red blood cells, which carry oxygen; white blood cells, which fight infection; platelets, which stop bleeding and heal wounds; and plasma, which is the broth all the other stuff floats around in.
PRP injections are a pretty common treatment for sports injuries, but taking the healing bits out of plasma seems kind of counterintuitive. Sort of like a vodka-poor screwdriver. But evidently PPP contains high levels of fibrinogen, which is itself a healing agent. Ms. Frizzle didn’t cover fibrinogen, but sure, I’ll buy it.
Unless the PPP works an actual miracle, though, it looks like the Yankees are going to have to navigate at least the first round of the playoffs without their best player.
And even if Judge does return — either in the Wild Card round or later, if the Yankees advance — I’d caution against assuming that we’d be seeing the best of him right off the proverbial bat. For starters, 99% of star athletes in history are going to try to force their way into the lineup for the playoffs regardless of whether they’re actually healthy.
To say nothing of the fact that Judge can be streaky. This is the nature of Judge’s unusual skill set; there are 1,073 hitters in major league history with at least 5,000 career plate appearances. Judge is the only one of those who’s produced one of the three true outcomes (home run, strikeout, walk) in more than half of his career plate appearances. (I’d like to express my immense gratitude to Adam Dunn, who has a career TTO% of 49.9, for making this fun fact possible.)
Living on the extremes, as he does, Judge will have weeks where he homers every night, and others where he goes 1-for-20 with 12 strikeouts. But you live with it because, over a long enough timeline, it works out heavily in his favor. Among hitters with at least 5,000 career plate appearances, Judge has the third-highest career wRC+, trailing only Babe Ruth and Ted Williams. If you wanted to go further than “best hitter now” and anoint Judge the best hitter ever, leaning heavily on the argument that quality of competition increases over time, you’d have a credible case.
But that’s not what the Yankees got out of Judge this year. In 66 regular-season games, he’s hit .241/.360/.511, with his highest strikeout rate (29.8%) since 2019 and lowest wRC+ (141) since 2020. In seven games since he returned from his rib injury, Judge was just 4-for-23 with one home run, one walk, and 13 strikeouts.
I’ve done enough of these injury reaction posts to figure out that they’re not really about the guy who got hurt, but about the teammates he’s leaving behind.
And I don’t want to underrate the value of Judge — even the version of Judge that has a 141 wRC+, rather than a 200 wRC+ — but the Yankees have done OK without him.
In the weakest American League field in decades, the Yankees are one of only two teams with a winning percentage of .550 or better. Entering their doubleheader with the Rays on Tuesday, the Yankees are still first in the AL in home runs (216) and second in runs scored per game (4.60). Even without Judge (or Giancarlo Stanton, for that matter), their lineup has plenty of beef.

Ben Rice in particular has been absolutely terrific this season. He’s fourth among qualified AL hitters in wRC+ and third in both home runs and runs scored. The Astros have AL MVP frontrunner Yordan Alvarez in their lineup; apart from him, is there any hitter in the AL bracket who’s been Rice’s equal this year? Maybe Junior Caminero? Willson Contreras, if you value OBP over raw power? Even if you’re being charitable, it’s a short list.
Now, past Rice, things get interesting, because if you want to talk about the Yankees’ offensive depth, you have to be able to hold multiple ideas in your head at once.
As of Tuesday morning, the Yankees have 11 hitters with double-digit home runs this season, which is tied for the most in the league. That’s just counting players who have hit 10 or more home runs in pinstripes, and the Yankees brought in substantial reinforcements midseason. Luis García Jr. has just seven homers for the Yankees but 30 overall. Heliot Ramos has four home runs in 32 games and 13 overall, with 20-plus in each of his previous two seasons. George Lombard Jr. has just five home runs in 37 major league games, but he hit 12 dingers in 78 minor league games before he got called up.
Count all this up and the Yankees have more hitters with at least decent pop than they can fit on the roster at once.
At the same time, Rice is the only Yankee with 20 home runs in pinstripes this year. So while this lineup is short on automatic outs, if Judge is out, there’s a massive drop-off after Rice.
If you take Judge out of the picture, Cody Bellinger is second on the Yankees in wRC+, at 119. The Rays don’t have anyone with 100 or more plate appearances and a better wRC+ than Rice this season, but they have four hitters (Caminero, Yandy Díaz, Jonathan Aranda, and Victor Mesa Jr.) with 100 or more plate appearances and a better wRC+ than Bellinger. So do the Rangers (Justin Foscue, Josh Jung, Joc Pederson, Wyatt Langford). The Astros have Alvarez, plus Isaac Paredes and Jeremy Peña. The White Sox have Miguel Vargas, Munetaka Murakami, and Tristan Peters.
As good as Rice has been, the Yankees’ lineup looks concerningly pedestrian without Judge. If you aren’t already a FanGraphs Member, please consider becoming one; it’s the only way to get trenchant original analysis like this.
The good news is that Judge’s calf injury runs counter to the rest of the team’s injury luck. Carlos Rodón, who missed almost three months with an elbow injury earlier this year, dominated the Rays in eight scoreless innings in Game 1 of a doubleheader on Tuesday. The same day, the Yankees activated Chisholm, who’d spent two weeks on the IL with a sprained thumb. Clarke Schmidt just returned from Tommy John surgery last week, and while he suffered biceps cramping in the bullpen on Sunday, it appears to be a minor setback. Trent Grisham remains a question mark for the start of the playoffs as he recovers from a hamstring injury, but his prognosis also looks good.
Judge is as important to the Yankees as any two or three other players put together, but with a healthy and deep rotation and Rice leading the way offensively, they’re not in bad shape. The remainder of this roster could easily survive and advance through a weaker AL bracket, setting the stage for a dramatically timed Judge return in mid-October. Like Kirk Gibson, only bigger.
Michael is a writer at FanGraphs. Previously, he was a staff writer at The Ringer and D1Baseball, and his work has appeared at Grantland, Baseball Prospectus, The Atlantic, ESPN.com, and various ill-remembered Phillies blogs. Follow him on Twitter, if you must, @MichaelBaumann.

item.title: [pinstripealley.com] Yankees win first game of doubleheader behind Carlos Rodón’s milestone performance
item.dc:creator: Peter Brody
item.description: The chances are now paper thin after a series loss in Arizona, but if the Yankees are to have any shot of chasing down the Rays in the final week of the season, they absolutely must sweep this four-game series. That required a dominant performance from Carlos Rodón facing one of the AL’s best starters in Nick Martinez. They certainly got that, Rodón running rampant for eight scoreless innings, achieving both the 1,500th strikeout and 100th win of his career as the Yankees took the first game of
item.content:encoded:
The chances are now paper thin after a series loss in Arizona, but if the Yankees are to have any shot of chasing down the Rays in the final week of the season, they absolutely must sweep this four-game series. That required a dominant performance from Carlos Rodón facing one of the AL’s best starters in Nick Martinez. They certainly got that, Rodón running rampant for eight scoreless innings, achieving both the 1,500th strikeout and 100th win of his career as the Yankees took the first game of the day’s doubleheader, 2-0.
Rodón burst out of the gate like he had a point to prove, whiffing the first two batters of the game Yandy Díaz and Jonathan Aranda on a pair of filthy sliders. Cam Schlittler and Max Fried are likely locks for the postseason rotation, meaning if the Yankees elect to stick with a three-man unit, that final spot comes down to Rodón and Gerrit Cole. Aaron Boone has affirmed his commitment to Cole as the Game One starter in a prospective Wild Card Series. This seemingly leaves Rodón on the bubble, which might explain the extra edge he was pitching with this afternoon.
His teammates didn’t do themselves any favors early, burning both ABS challenges in the first inning. I expect the Yankees to tighten the strings on who gets to challenge and in what situation come the playoffs as you cannot deprive yourself of such a vital tool with eight innings still to play.
Martinez entered this game with the lowest walk rate of any qualified starter and among the league’s best at limiting hard contact. He was true to form going the first turn through the order without allowing a base runner. He was helped by the collectively poor approach from the lineup, with four out of the nine batters including the side in the third striking out against a pitcher with the lowest strikeout rate among qualified starters.
That started to change the second turn through the order, the Yankees finally starting to do some damage against the high volume of pitches Martinez was throwing over the heart of the plate, starting with a Ben Rice double into the corner in right to lead off the fourth. The very next pitch Martinez threw rocketed out of the yard, Cody Bellinger blasting a first pitch sinker into the seats in right for a two-run homer — his fifth homer in the last 12 games.
George Lombard Jr. and Spencer Jones singled with two outs to put runners on the corners. Jones then stole second unopposed, but Anthony Volpe struck out swinging to strand the pair in scoring position. They kept up the pressure in the fifth, José Caballero reaching on a bunt single against his former team and then stealing second and third followed by a Rice walk to put runners on the corners with one out. However, Bellinger popped out and Heliot Ramos flew out as they stranded a pair in consecutive frames.
Rodón settled into an impressive groove after a Chandler Simpson single in the second, retiring the next ten batters in order until Victor Mesa Jr. led off the sixth with a single. After Rodón whiffed Jorge Mateo on a slider for his sixth strikeout, he got Richie Palacios to line out to left. Mesa was running on the play and momentarily forget he had to sprint back to first, allowing Bellinger to throw an absolute seed to Luis García Jr., who applid the tag for the inning-ending double play.
With Rodón’s pitch count standing at just 89 after seven, Boone decided to go batter-to-batter in the eighth. However, Rodón ensured his manager had no choice to make, completing the eighth inning on just seven pitches, including the 1,500th strikeout of his career. It’s tied for his longest start as a Yankee, matching the eight innings he pitched against the Cubs on July 11, 2025.
Rodón entered this start as perhaps the Yankees’ most in-form pitcher behind Schlittler. Including today, in his last eight starts, Rodón has a 1.67 ERA while holding batters to a measly .134 batting average against. He had all his pitches working today, but this really felt like a throwback to his peak years with Chicago and San Francisco. He got whiffs in bunches on the four-seamer above the zone and slider below it. In likely his penultimate start of the regular season, Rodón dominated for eight scoreless innings, allowing three hits and no walks while striking out eight to lower his ERA to 2.67 on the year.
The Yankees didn’t manage another base runner in the final three innings, but Rodón made sure that it wouldn’t come back to haunt them. David Bednar pitched a one-two-three ninth to secure his 35th save of the season. The gap to the Rays now stands at five games as the Yankees become the second team in the AL to 90 wins. At worst, they have clinched the four seed in the AL, guaranteeing home field advantage in a prospective AL Wild Card Series.
The Yankees have a few hours’ rest before taking the field again tonight. Max Fried starts the night game of the doubleheader against Drew Rasmussen. First pitch is scheduled for 7:05 pm ET with the broadcast remaining on YES, so stick around!

item.description: Carlos Rodón delivered his best starts of the season Tuesday afternoon, leading the New York Yankees to a 2-0 victory over the Tampa Bay Rays in the first game of a doubleheader at Yankee Stadium. Rodón allowed only three hits, all singles, while striking out eight over eight scoreless innings. It was his first eight-inning performance since July 11, 2025. The left-hander retired 19 straight batters at one point, with two double plays helping preserve the perfect stretch. Jose Caballero started
item.content:encoded:
Carlos Rodón delivered his best starts of the season Tuesday afternoon, leading the New York Yankees to a 2-0 victory over the Tampa Bay Rays in the first game of a doubleheader at Yankee Stadium.
Rodón allowed only three hits, all singles, while striking out eight over eight scoreless innings. It was his first eight-inning performance since July 11, 2025.
The left-hander retired 19 straight batters at one point, with two double plays helping preserve the perfect stretch. Jose Caballero started a 5-4-3 double play in the second inning, while Cody Bellinger caught a line drive in the third before throwing to first base, where Luis García Jr. tagged Victor Mesa Jr. trying to return to the bag.
Rodón also reached a career milestone in the eighth inning when he recorded his 1,500th strikeout. His season earned-run average dropped to 2.67, while he has posted a 1.42 earned-run average in four September starts.
New York’s offense struggled to generate much against Tampa Bay starter Nick Martinez, who retired the Yankees in order the first time through the lineup.
That changed in the fourth inning. Ben Rice opened the frame with a double before Bellinger followed with a two-run home run to right field, giving New York its only runs of the game.
George Lombard Jr. and Spencer Jones followed with consecutive two-out singles, but Anthony Volpe struck out to end the inning.
David Bednar closed the game with a scoreless ninth for his 35th save.
The victory moved New York to within five games of Tampa Bay in the American League East.
The teams meet again Tuesday at 7:05 p.m. Max Fried starts for New York against Drew Rasmussen.

item.title: [fansided.com] Projecting the Yankees Wild Card series lineup after brutal Aaron Judge's injury update
item.dc:creator: Zachary Rotman
item.description: It felt like Aaron Judge was returning at the perfect time. A September return following a three-month stint on the IL gave Judge enough time to find his timing before the postseason. Unfortunately, Judge suffered another injury before the playoffs even began, hurting his calf in a game against the Minnesota Twins. The New York Yankees hoped it'd be minor, but it was serious enough for the team to place its captain on the Injured List. Now, it sounds as if a return for the Yankees' first postsea
item.content:encoded:
It felt like Aaron Judge was returning at the perfect time. A September return following a three-month stint on the IL gave Judge enough time to find his timing before the postseason. Unfortunately, Judge suffered another injury before the playoffs even began, hurting his calf in a game against the Minnesota Twins. The New York Yankees hoped it'd be minor, but it was serious enough for the team to place its captain on the Injured List. Now, it sounds as if a return for the Yankees' first postseason series is a long shot at best.
A "moderate grade" calf strain is serious enough for Yankees manager Aaron Boone to proceed as if his best player won't be active at all for the Wild Card series. That is an insanely difficult blow for a Yankees team that, with Judge, is as good as any in a weak American League. For the Yankees to advance to the ALDS and potentially get their captain back, they'll need to rely on this projected lineup below.
What the Yankees lineup could look like without Aaron Judge
Judge is an instrumental piece in the Yankees' lineup for a couple of reasons. First, he's the best hitter in the sport when healthy. That obviously matters. Second, Judge is one of the few right-handed bats on this roster. He provides much-needed balance that, without Judge, the Yankees lack.
| Position | Player |
|---|---|
| Ben Rice | DH |
| Cody Bellinger | LF |
| Heliot Ramos | RF |
| Luis Garcia Jr. | 1B |
| Spencer Jones | CF |
| George Lombard Jr. | SS |
| Jazz Chisholm Jr. | 2B |
| Austin Wells | C |
| Jose Caballero | 3B |
This lineup still has some good pieces in it. Ben Rice has had a breakout year, Cody Bellinger is a well-rounded star, and trails only Yordan Alvarez and Pete Crow-Armstrong, the AL and NL MVP favorites, with a .532 slugging percentage. If Jazz Chisholm Jr. can return from the IL looking like the player he's capable of being, the Yankees can score runs.
The problem, though, is that six of the nine hitters in this lineup are left-handed, and most of them are much better against righties than lefties. The Yankees will use guys like Paul Goldschmidt and Amed Rosario against left-handed pitching, but having Heliot Ramos, who has a .672 OPS since being acquired by the Yankees at the deadline, in the No. 3 hole against righties isn't ideal. The Yankees don't have much of a choice with Judge out, though.
Ultimately, with Judge out, this is a team heavily reliant on lineup platoons. It'll be on Aaron Boone to try to push the right buttons in order to get this offense, which has been remarkably inconsistent without Judge, to score runs against (likely) a potent Boston Red Sox pitching staff.
Aaron Judge injury update: Can the Yankees expect their star to return?
What's most frustrating about the Judge injury update is that we have no idea what the injury is. The Yankees, for whatever reason, keep information regarding injuries, particularly to Judge, extremely close to the vest, making it difficult to know when or even if Judge will be back. All we know is that Judge is dealing with what Aaron Boone deems a "moderate" strain.
That doesn't sound good, especially for a player who has had trouble with the same right calf in the past. In the shortened 2020 season, Judge attempted to return from a calf strain in a couple of weeks, but wound up re-aggravating the injury, pushing his return back several weeks. Calf injuries and other soft-tissue ailments are not to be messed with, and can lead to a major setback if rushed through.
Plus, if the injury was minor, wouldn't the Yankees be quick to tell the world that? I'd love to say Judge is a lock to return at some point, but even if the Yankees were to advance to the ALDS, given how little we know and how tricky returns can be from calf injuries, it's probably wishful thinking to assume he'd be back right at the start of a potential ALDS, which is the last thign any New York fan wants to hear.

With a magic number of two over the Yankees, the Rays can seal their fate in the afternoon opener. item.content:encoded:
The Tampa Bay Rays will get two chances to clinch their first American League East title since 2021 when they visit the New York Yankees for a day/night doubleheader on Tuesday.
With a magic number of two over the Yankees, the Rays can seal their fate in the afternoon opener.
Tampa Bay (95-60) has won six of the nine games against New York and owns a six-game lead on the Yankees. New York (89-66) has a magic number of two for clinching the AL's top wild-card spot over the Boston Red Sox.
The Rays, who are seeking their fifth division title, have led the AL East every day since June 27.
Following a 2-7 run last month, Tampa Bay is 19-7 since Aug. 23 and just went 8-1 on a homestand against the Houston Astros, Athletics and Red Sox. It featured three walk-off wins and ended with Sunday's 5-1 win over Boston which saw Chandler Simpson and Jonny DeLuca drive in two runs apiece.
"We knew what we had to do," Tampa Bay pitcher Griffin Jax said. "We wanted to put ourselves in a good place going into New York, make it a little bit easier."
The Yankees play host to the Rays for the first time since Aaron Judge's game-ending two-run homer for a 2-0 victory May 24. Judge returned Sept. 8 after missing 84 games with a fractured rib, played seven games and returned to the injured list with a strained calf.
The Yankees are 48-41 in games Judge has not played and enter the upcoming series after losing two of three at Arizona, including an 8-4 loss Sunday. Rookies George Lombard Jr. and Spencer Jones hit two of New York's three home runs in the third inning, but Brent Headrick gave up a grand slam to Arizona's Nolan Arenado in the fifth.
"We're going to show up and try to win the games on Tuesday, and then we'll keep going from there," Yankees manager Aaron Boone said. "We've been through a lot as a team this year already, and we've answered the bell at the turns. We're looking forward to hopefully playing a good week of baseball and building some momentum going into the postseason."
Nick Martinez (15-4, 2.94 ERA) will start the opener for Tampa Bay followed by Drew Rasmussen (15-5, 2.72) in the second game. Martinez is 3-0 with a 2.43 ERA in his past five starts and 2-2 with a 4.30 ERA in 12 career appearances against the Yankees.
Since allowing six runs in 2 1/3 innings at home against the Yankees on July 9, Rasmussen is 8-0 with a 1.91 ERA in his past 11 starts. He is 4-2 with a 1.87 ERA in 10 career outings against the Yankees.
New York will start Carlos Rodon (6-3, 2.95) in the opener followed by Max Fried (5-4, 2.63).
Rodon is 2-1 with a 2.40 ERA in six starts since returning from the injured list Aug. 18 and is 3-3 with a 3.88 ERA in 10 career starts against the Rays
Fried is 1-0 with a 1.83 ERA in four starts since returning from the injured list Aug. 29 and allowed one run in seven innings last Tuesday at Minnesota. He is 5-0 with a 1.26 ERA in six career starts against Tampa Bay.

item.title: [Yahoo Sports] Yankees Announce Paul Goldschmidt Decision Before Rays Doubleheader

item.content:encoded:
The New York Yankees are coming off two straight losses in Arizona to the Diamondbacks, a setback that left them a full six games behind the Tampa Bay Rays in the American League East pennant race.
But the Yankees still have a chance to win the division and with it, the top seed in the AL and a bye out of the Wild card playoff round.
The Yankees and Rays open a four-game, head-to-head series with the first game of a doubleheader Tuesday at Yankee Stadium. With a four-game sweep, the Yankees would take the season tiebreaker and need to win at least two of three against the Baltimore Orioles, while the Rays lose two of three to the Philadelphia Phillies to close out the regular season.
Before Game One of the twin bill, the Yankees announced a decision on how they will utilize veteran first basinal Paul Goldschmidt.
Goldschmidt is out of the New York Yankees lineup for a third straight game, sidelined again by a stark platoon split against right-handed pitching.
The pattern has held all September, and it likely has fans wondering about how much longer the 39-year-old holds even a part-time role with October two weeks away.
| NEW YORK YANKEES STARTING LINEUP (GAME 1) | | | | |
| SP: Carlos Rodón (LHP) • 6-3, 2.95 ERA | | | | |
| September 22, 2026 • Yankee Stadium, Bronx, NY • 1:05 PM ET • Rays at Yankees | | | | |
| # | Player | Pos | AVG | SLG |
| 1 | Ben Rice | DH | .261 | .528 |
| 2 | Cody Bellinger | LF | .270 | .435 |
| 3 | Heliot Ramos | RF | .241 | .409 |
| 4 | Luis García Jr. | 1B | .281 | .532 |
| 5 | George Lombard Jr. | SS | .235 | .386 |
| 6 | Spencer Jones | CF | .248 | .442 |
| 7 | Anthony Volpe | 2B | .248 | .340 |
| 8 | Alí Sánchez | C | .250 | .316 |
| 9 | José Caballero | 3B | .236 | .373 |
| Lineups confirmed. Season stats shown (AVG / SLG). Umpire: Sean Barber • Weather: 63°, Wind 13 mph • O/U: 7 Runs • Line: TB +112 / NYY -135. | | | | |
Boone's Platoon Explains Goldschmidt Sit
Aaron Boone's lineup card for Tuesday's series opener against Tampa Bay leaves Goldschmidt out again, extending a run that traces back to Saturday. He started Friday against left-hander Eduardo Rodriguez in Arizona and went 1-for-4 with a walk and two runs, then sat both weekend games against right-handers Brandon Pfaadt and Corbin Burnes. That's three benchings in the last three games against right-handed starters.
Why? Goldschmidt has produced an elite 1.006 OPS against lefties this season but an anemic a .572 mark versus right-handers, a gap wide enough that Boone starts Ben Rice at DH and Luis García Jr. at first whenever a right-hander pitches. An Athletic report on the lineup moves after Aaron Judge's calf strain named Goldschmidt and Heliot Ramos as the bats Boone leans on against lefties, with García handling the right-handed side.
Nick Martinez, Tuesday's Tampa Bay starter, has largely dominated Goldschmidt in his career. The former National League MVP is 2-for-10 with four walks and two strikeouts against Martinez, and he is 0-for-13 with four strikeouts in his last three meetings with the right-hander since 2024. Martinez enters at 15-4 with a 2.94 ERA this year, and beat the Yankees in the Bronx in May, giving Boone both the season splits and the head-to-head history pointing toward a Goldschmidt benching.
Tuesday's day-night doubleheader against two more right-handed Rays starters gives Boone an easy excuse to sit the 39-year-old.

Goldschmidt's Future in New York
Goldschmidt turns free agent again this winter, and the Yankees have made no public commitment either way. A cheap return as a lefty-masher and clubhouse mentor remains plausible given Rice's grip on first base, and his credentials, a 2022 NL MVP award, seven All-Star selections, four Gold Gloves and five Silver Sluggers still makes him a name teams will inquire about this winter.
First base belongs to Rice, who has grown into an everyday role with 39 home runs and 95 RBI this season, pushing Goldschmidt into a complementary, short-side platoon job. That role fits the final stretch of a one-year, $4 million contract that can grow by $500,000 at each of four plate-appearance thresholds, according to Spotrac, a modest deal compared with the $12.5 million he earned in his first Yankees season a year earlier.
This article was originally published on HEAVY
