item.title: [Pinstripe Alley] New York Yankees vs. Tampa Bay Rays: Carlos Rodón vs. Nick Martinez
item.dc:creator: Peter Brody
item.description: This four-game tilt against the Rays in the penultimate series of the season had the chance to be a blockbuster showdown to decide the division. However, the Yankees losing two out of three to the Diamondbacks removed a lot of the jeopardy from this series, New York now needing to sweep just to avoid being eliminated from the AL East title race and depending on a very unlikely collapse from Tampa in their final series of the season to keep the divisional door the slightest bit ajar. All the same
item.content:encoded:
This four-game tilt against the Rays in the penultimate series of the season had the chance to be a blockbuster showdown to decide the division. However, the Yankees losing two out of three to the Diamondbacks removed a lot of the jeopardy from this series, New York now needing to sweep just to avoid being eliminated from the AL East title race and depending on a very unlikely collapse from Tampa in their final series of the season to keep the divisional door the slightest bit ajar. All the same, this could be a preview of a prospective ALCS showdown, so I expect both teams to come out firing. The first game of today’s doubleheader is a makeup of the rainout from May 23rd.
Carlos Rodón finds himself in the unexpected position of being on the postseason rotation bubble. Cam Schlittler and Max Fried are seemingly locks which would pit Rodón against Gerrit Cole for that final spot if they roll out a three-man rotation. It almost comes down to a style choice at that point — Rodón walks almost three times as many batters as Cole, but surrenders about half as many home runs per nine. He’s a good choice to start a game against the Rays — in six starts against Tampa with the Yankees, Rodón has a 3.69 ERA and 31.3-percent strikeout rate in 31.2 innings. In 15 starts this season, Rodón is 6-3 with a 2.95 ERA (142 ERA+), 3.69 FIP, and 83 strikeouts in 76.1 innings.
The Rays have a maddening habit of transforming other teams’ castoffs into rotation stars. This season’s example is longtime journeyman Nick Martinez, who had pitched as a swingman the previous four years in San Diego and Cincinnati. Martinez owns the lowest walk rate (3.5-percent) of any qualified starter, using deception and precise command to induce soft contact. He’s technically got a six-pitch mix but usually sticks with sinker, changeup, cutter, and four-seamer. In 29 starts, Martinez is 15-4 with a 2.94 ERA (142 ERA+), 3.98 FIP, and 101 strikeouts in 171.1 innings.
This is more or less the Yankees’ go-to lineup for the rest of the regular season with Aaron Judge on the IL. Heliot Ramos and Spencer Jones are both going to get a lot of run out in the outfield, so it was encouraging to see them both hit home runs against the former Cy Young winner Corbin Burnes in their last game. José Caballero gets the start over Ryan McMahon at third and sounded eager to make an impact against the team that traded him to the Yankees at last year’s deadline.
The Rays have their three-headed slugging monster atop lineup and then stack the bottom two-thirds with speed. Junior Caminero is third in MLB with 41 home runs giving him back-to-back 40-HR seasons. Chandler Simpson is MLB’s stolen base leader with 46 and third in batting average at .309, but is the only qualified hitter in baseball without a home run this season.
How to watch
Location: Yankee Stadium - Bronx, NY
First pitch: 1:05 pm ET
TV broadcast: YES, Rays.TV
Radio broadcast: WFAN 660/101.9 FM, WADO 1280 (NYY) | WDAE 95.7 FM, WQBN/1300AM (TB)
Streaming: Gotham Sports App, MLB.tv (out-of-market only)

item.title: [Pinstripe Alley] Yankees At-Bat of the Week: George Lombard Jr. (9/20)
item.dc:creator: Peter Brody
item.description: Unfortunately, the Yankees effectively pissed away whatever slim chance they had to catch the Rays in the division by losing two out of three to the Diamondbacks, the pitching staff wobbling uncharacteristically in the desert. It was at least encouraging to see the offense mostly carry their weight in the wake of Aaron Judge’s placement on the IL with a right calf strain. The biggest fireworks of the series came in the rubber game loss, three home runs in the third off former NL Cy Young winner
item.content:encoded:
Unfortunately, the Yankees effectively pissed away whatever slim chance they had to catch the Rays in the division by losing two out of three to the Diamondbacks, the pitching staff wobbling uncharacteristically in the desert. It was at least encouraging to see the offense mostly carry their weight in the wake of Aaron Judge’s placement on the IL with a right calf strain. The biggest fireworks of the series came in the rubber game loss, three home runs in the third off former NL Cy Young winner Corbin Burnes momentarily giving them the lead. We’ll look at the middle of those home runs, a two-run blast from George Lombard Jr., on At-Bat of the Week.
We join Lombard with two outs in the top of the third in the rubber game in Arizona on Sunday. Heliot Ramos tied the game with a two-out solo shot two batters earlier and Luis García Jr. kept the inning alive with a single. Wavering with his command from the first batter but particularly this inning, the Yankees need to keep up the pressure and bury Burnes.
Burnes starts this AB like he does many others, with his bread and butter cutter.
Lombard’s swing is pretty much on time to this 92 mph cutter. However, he’s a tick underneath it and fouls it back to the screen.
Burnes apparently likes the way that pitch comes out because he tries to nail the exact same spot with another cutter.
This is no longer the dominant version of Burnes that won the 2021 NL Cy Young award with Milwaukee by painting the corners with upper-90s cutters. Multiple serious arm injuries have limited him to just over 75 innings since signing a six-year, $210 million free agent contract with the Diamondbacks following the 2024 season and robbed him of his top end velocity. This is apparent in just his third start of the year, his cutter averaging just 91 mph and with none of the sharp command of his peak years. Nonetheless, he’s still able to beat Lombard up in the zone with the last two cutters. Both swings have been underneath, telling me that Lombard hasn’t quite figured out the movement profile of the pitch and how it doesn’t drop as much as you might expect.
After hitting the same spot with two straight cutters to jump quickly ahead, 0-2, it’s a perfect time to tunnel a curveball down the same aiming point as the first two pitches of the AB, which should be almost impossible for Lombard not to chase.
The logic is sound but the execution not so much. This pitch exits Burnes’ hand way lower than the first two cutters. Lombard is surely cognizant of a possible breaking ball below the zone for the strikeout here and therefore is able to take this ball in the dirt without much of a flinch.
Burnes must not love the way that curveball came out because he immediately switches back to the cutter. It’s a pitch he’s been able to command in this AB and one that Lombard has not shown he can hit yet.
Burnes yanks this cutter low and away for another straightforward take from Lombard.
After a poorly executed curveball immediately followed by a cutter in a strikeout count, Burnes might have Lombard thinking that another cutter is coming, so he has a second attempt at a curveball below the zone.
Once again, Burnes mis-executes the curveball badly, looping this one high and inside for ball three and another automatic take from Lombard.
Lombard has done well to fight back from 0-2 down to a full count, though he wasn’t put under too much stress by any of Burnes’ attempted strikeout pitches. He likely knows he can hunt a cutter in the zone as Burnes won’t want to put another runner on with two outs and Spencer Jones due up.
As Joe Girardi has said multiple times on the broadcast, a hanging cutter is the best pitch to hit because it runs right into the barrel of your bat. Lombard got a hanger and he did not miss it, demolishing this middle-middle cookie to left for a no-doubter two-run blast. I’ll be honest, I did not know Lombard had this kind of pop. This is 109 mph, 424 feet — the second-hardest-hit ball and by far the longest home run of his young career.
Here’s the full AB:
It’s been really cool to watch Lombard adjust to the Major League level in real time. In this AB specifically, Lombard adjusted his swing path mid-AB to make sure that he stayed on top of an in-zone cutter after swinging underneath a pair. After bursting onto the scene his first two or so weeks post-debut, Lombard like every other big leaguer experienced the growing pains of the league making adjustments. He endured a rocky error streak with the glove and saw the hits dry up, leading to a much needed rotation out of the starting lineup for a day here and there. This apparently allowed him to reset, because he has looked way more sound with the glove and isn’t chasing nearly as much over the last ten days. He’ll need to keep making these adjustments throughout his career, and the ability to do so early in one’s rookie season is a good omen for the future.

item.title: [blogs.fangraphs.com] Ben Clemens FanGraphs Chat - 9/21/26
item.dc:creator: Ben Clemens
item.description: Ben Clemens Hey everybody, welcome to the chat. We're testing out a new chat interface today, one that we'll hopefully roll out more broadly in the weeks to come. So come on, let's run it through its paces. Kevin In a weekly transactions H2H league, would you risk rolling with Aroldis this week? I don't see why the Bosox would rush him back into action. Ben Clemens Yeah, I would not. For exactly the reason you said. It just feels like you're opening yourself up to some risk without enough upside
item.content:encoded:
Ben Clemens
Hey everybody, welcome to the chat. We're testing out a new chat interface today, one that we'll hopefully roll out more broadly in the weeks to come. So come on, let's run it through its paces.
Kevin
In a weekly transactions H2H league, would you risk rolling with Aroldis this week? I don't see why the Bosox would rush him back into action.
Ben Clemens
Yeah, I would not. For exactly the reason you said. It just feels like you're opening yourself up to some risk without enough upside back for it. You're going to feel REALLY bad if they ease him back in and you're playing him. And on the flip side, what if he's not right immediately? Can't have a 0% chance of that.
SPArn
Any favorite random MLBers as we wind down the stretch, or little hopeful glimpses? I still don't believe Scott Bandura is real, even though Mo'Ne Davis went to his debut, and I nearly shed a tear during Josiah Gray's return
Ben Clemens
I mean, this guy is definitely very real, but David Freese is my all-time favorite good but not great guy who stuck around long enough for me to have fond memories of them.
Ben Clemens
Many of mine are Cardinals themed because that's when I was most strongly a fan of a single team. Pete Kozma. Bo Hart.
Ben Clemens
If we're talking current guys, well, how about Trent Harris, who I've grown inordinately fond of very quickly this year
SPArn
Your piece(s) on Cade Cavalli are excellent, much more thorough and better reasoned than this. But, I think the extension boils down to: 4/47 is low risk enough it doesn't hurt if he regresses or breaks, and if it turns into 5/70, it must have worked out great for the Nats. All reporting seems like he's a truly excellent leader too. We came a long way from "sit down, boy" and we can all be grateful for that
Ben Clemens
Yeah, I think that's basically the risk management part of mine. It's a good bet even if you know he gets hurt some of the time, because on average you get a nice amount of value out of signing him. I leave the leadership stuff aside – I agree with you that it's widely reported that way, I just think that those types of things are extremely subjective and don't hold over long periods of time anyway.
aldrinbatistarocks
A while ago, I remember listening to a BP podcast in which they were talking about christopher morel, the gist of the discussion being "it's okay to acknowledge when a guy is probably having their career year." Are there any candidates in 2026 for guys you think hit their apex production this season?
Ben Clemens
Love this one. Some easy ones for me: Otto Lopez. PCA. Gabriel Moreno. Randy Arozarena. Jake Bauers.
Ben Clemens
I don't mean any of them ill by that. But I just think a ton of stuff broke well for those players in their years, and that it feels hard to have all of that plus more hit right in a future year for them to eclipse it. You can still be a very good player after hitting your apex production
smoothio
Does Tatis have an MVP season in him?
Ben Clemens
Whether he actually wins one? who can say. Whether he has the capability to? Clearly yes. He's played at an MVP level for half of this year, for example. The talent is definitely there. Winning an MVP is tough because you have to have it hit for a whole year when no one else hits their even better outcome.
oaktownblues
Think the A's can hold onto a winning record against every AL west team this season? Just need to not lose series vs Angels and Astros
Ben Clemens
I do. I think that'd be a pretty cool footnote on what was just a real bummer of a season. Kind of a hilarious one, too. The AL is a mess this year.
bosoxforlife
The Red Sox should start Tolle in game 1 in The Bronx. The reality is that the Red Sox look outmatched and his personality fits the occasion perfectly and a few quick K's could change the mood.
Ben Clemens
I like the idea of starting Tolle game one. I feel crazy saying this, but I kind of like the idea of just starting three lefties and daring the Yankees to play their righty platoon bats, kind of gambling on Judge being less than 100%
Anonymous Member #46
Holy crap, I dig the new chat interface so far. No login issues!
Ben Clemens
Great to hear. Sean and team are still working on adding functionality (polls, images, that kinda thing) but I have been liking the clean look and it gives us more flexibility on our end
Ben Clemens
a little more legible and the scroll bars are nicer. Setting up the chat has more options. Basically this just has more options across the board. Oh, and I love the little FanGraphs icon by my name, so fun
oaktownblues
How does the new chat interface differ on your end? Are questions organized differently than before?
Ben Clemens
so, there's something I'm still getting used to, published those two out of order
riceball
where does Yordan rank among unlikely batting title winners? (assuming he holds on)
Ben Clemens
Nowhere near the top. He has a career .300 batting average! Among big league regulars, only Luis Arraez, Chandler Simpson (small-ish sample), and Jose Altuve are better
bosoxforlife
I can't get over the fact that either the Guardians or the White Sox will, most likely, receive a bye in the first round while whoever wins the AL West plays the team that finishes second but gets the home field against a team with a better record. I don't want to pour cold water on the new interface but the submission box is too small to handle more than two lines of copy.
Ben Clemens
Great feedback on the submission box. That sounds like an easy fix to me, I'll let Sean know.
As to the playoff system, yeah, I agree that this is a problem. I really like the bye system we have at current. It gives a reward for teams that have great regular seasons. But I agree that the divisional system interacts awkwardly with it. What if they handed out playoff spots the way they do now but pre-reseeded, ordering teams by record? I'm totally with you that it's a good idea that feels obviuosly unfair in practice.
SPArn
Pitchers having their best year: Nick Martinez, Luzardo, Messick, Louis Varland, Martin Perez some candidates that leap to mind. (Don't say the Miz, don't say the Miz, don't say the Miz)
Ben Clemens
I don't think the Miz counts. Like, yes, he's having an extremely good year. But he could throw more innings. the strikeouts don't look crazy unsustainable. it COULD be a career year but it doesn't feel like a blow-off top (a finance term I love and have been trying to use more of late) in the way that, say, Otto Lopez does
didace
Submission box – The default seems small, but click/hold and drag the little thing in the bottom right corner and you can make it very large.
Sean Dolinar
We are going to fix that once this chat is over. Thanks everyone for the feedback! – Sean
Ben Clemens
Martinez doesn't count because this isn't even his best year! He had his career year in 2024 in Cincy. Luzardo, same kinda deal, he's basically repeating last season. probably not 'career year' territory. I definitely agree with you on Varland, don't think Messick is really fair since he's a rookie, and Martin Perez got a qualifying offer once!
Ben Clemens
My own list would have: Reid Detmers, who I think is good but not this good. Sean Burke, though without much conviction there. And Foster Griffin.
Michael De Vivo
will spencer jones be overmatched by playoff level pitching?
Ben Clemens
If by overwhelmed you mean he'll strike out a lot, absolutely yes. He's a high-strikeout guy and the octane of pitchers ramps up int he playoffs. But it's not like he hasn't faced hard pitches in the regular season or in the minors. His game is tons of strikeouts and sometimes the ball leaves the yard. One playoff homer or so and we'llb e like man, this guy has it. And since homers are pretty rare events, it feels like Jones could be basically the same hitter and based on whether he happens to run into one or not we'll say he just didn't have it or performed as expected.
ado64
Who do you think starts Brewers playoff game 3, and how many innings do they get? 3 innings of Gasser or Drohan, maybe? Does May ever start a game with his recent inconsistency?
Ben Clemens
I think that some kind of piggyback situation is reasonable here. Like, three of Drohan with May backing him up? Or some other lefty/righty switch of that style. I'm extremely curious to see how they deploy Harrison.
Ben Clemens
I really don't know what you do with Harrison. Like, he's been so bad recently! But he has such high highs. The test in relief hasn't gone all that well so far. It's not like they can afford to just not have him pithc, he was a big part of their run prevention this year.
Ben Clemens
Sorry, I missed an answer before messing around iwth the interface. I meant to say that Harrison is the highest-unceratinty question in the entire playoff picture for me. The Brewers were the best team in baseball this year and Kyle Harrison was a ton of that. What are they going to look like with less good pitching? Can they figure out what ails him in time? I have no clue but I'm very excited to find out.
Anon21
Maybe dumb question. When Team A is one game ahead of Team B in the standings and also holds the tiebreaker on Team B, it's often said that they effectively have a two-game lead. But is there a similar way of describing the situations of the Astros and White Sox, who are one game back in the standings but hold the tiebreaker over the team ahead? Like are they effectively 0.8 (or something) games back, rather than one? (I know this is accounted for by magic numbers, just wondering if there's a simple way to describe this situation.)
Ben Clemens
I'd say they're one back with the tiebreaker. Or alternately that they're 'effectively only a half game back' because of the breaker. I agree with you that the wording is kind of tricky, though. You can't say they're 'effectively tied', that's not true. If they hvae the same records they won't make the playoffs
Nomar6666666
No question really. Just a frustrated fan with few places to vent. If the owners lock out the players next season, and we miss one single game, I will not go to a single game next year, nor will I buy the MLB TV package. I Wii continue to support this site
Ben Clemens
Nomar, we appreciate your continued support, of course. That's very kind. And honestly, I feel pretty similar. I think the owners are more to blame than the players for the upcoming fight we're sure to have. I don't feel great about anyone's role in this though. There's so much freaking money in baseball. Work it out between yourselves like adults so that we the fans, who pay a ton of money to enjoy your product, can still get it. No one is on our side in this negotiation, and that makes it feel bad
Braydon Roberts
Thoughts on the NL RoY race? Seems like everyone gave it to Sal Stewart when JJ went on the IL, but Stewart has had a rough September. fWAR is 4.4 to 2.2 in JJ's favor.
Ben Clemens
So, I've had JJ all along. I just don't really buy the arguments that some counting numbers matter so much that they're more important than the overall picture. I'm not saying Stewart's homers don't matter or anything. Obviously they do. But eh, the RBI's, I'm not as convinced by, because a stat like RE24 (which cares about driving in runs, but also cares about how many opportunities you had to drive in runs) says Stewart was about 10 runs better with the bat than Wetherholt this year so far.
Ben Clemens
That's not a ton of runs better. And again, that accounts for the RBI and the homers and all. And if you care about win probability – as in how important those RBIs were – Wetherholt actually has a BETTER bat than Stewart
Ben Clemens
Also he's a plus defender at an important position instead of a first baseman who defensive metrics aren't fond of
Ben Clemens
Like, I get the sentiment. And I get wanting to push back against WAR and be like 'no the old stats we love still matter'
Ben Clemens
There are times where I think that's true! I'd vote for Yordan by a mile for AL MVP, and it's because I think that his offensive value is so high that WAR is overly penalizing him for his defense. no one cares when you hit that well. BUt that's not Sal Stewart's case.
war2d2
Don’t like the new interface, all my questions are still poorly thought out and badly edited. Thought it would have fixed that.
Ben Clemens
That's coming in FanGraphs 2.0 🙂
Greg Simons
Regarding last week's lack of any questions about lunch, I think we all figured someone else would ask. Of course, when that happens, you make a "fig" out of "u" and "re," or something like that. Whatever the case, I hope you have a good lunch planned today.
Ben Clemens
Why thank you. It's like House said once, I think: That's what happens when you make a presumption. You make a pres out of you and some guy named umption.
As for lunch, leftovers from a very nice salmon dish that a friend of ours cooked this weekend.
WonderWall
Piggybacking on Nomar's comments, why do you think that both the owners and the Union seem to pretty much refuse to let the situation continue. Why do both sides feel like something needs to change?
Ben Clemens
Many possible answers to this. I think the most important, for me, is that they'd act this way even if they thought that 'no change' was acceptable, because that's how bargaining well in advance of a deadline works. So I'm hopeful that when the rubber meets the road, both sides will cave simultaneously.
Barbaro Garbey
Thank you for the chat Ben. The Tigers have to feel good about former top prospects Kevin McGonigle and Max Clark thriving in their first big league action this year. Wondering though if you have any thoughts on any of the "other" Tigers rookies who have been getting run down the stretch? Personally, I have loved watching the energy guys like Hao-Yu Lee and Eduardo Valencia have brought; and Ben Malgeri and Brett Callahan have at least looked like quality defensive outfielders (at least compared to some of the butchers the Tigers have put out there). Do you think any of this group could succeed/thrive in closer to a full time role next year?
Ben Clemens
Truthfully I don't think I've seen enough of any of them to be all that sure, but I do think that they did enough that if I'm the Tigers, I'm interested in leaving some space for the minor leaguers to have bigger roles next year. Like, leave an outfield hole perhaps?
Phil
Are we sure the Sox' best option, with Rafaela back, isn't Anthony in right and Gasper/Jones at DH? I'm not really believing in Duran right now.
Ben Clemens
This seems like possibly the best option, but their behavior year to date basically tells me they won't be doing this. Or, well, assuming you mean Anthony in left, I like Abreu in right.
PC1970
Would you even put Harrison on the roster if you were Milwaukee? He looks unplayable at the moment. Maybe overreaction, but, you also can't just punt a playoff game like they can a regular season game.
Ben Clemens
I mean, I would. If I thought playing Harrison was punting a game, I wouldn't put him on there. But I kind of think that you need to give yourself chances to have your best possible team. And c'mon, if he's awful for two innings and you yank him, I think that's short of punting the game. I think that not rostering him would basically be playing too conservative. You should try to hit your high-upside outcomes to win in the playoffs, imo
Anon21
Following up more on the lockout question…I think implicitly I'm assigning the probability of missing any games to be low, definitely less than 10%. Commentators throwing around the possibility of losing the whole season seem nuts to me–isn't that obviously suicidal from a business perspective? Where do you stand on probabilities of losing any games/a significant number of games/the whole season?
Ben Clemens
I'm at least close to you on this one. I think I have the odds of missing games very low and the odds of missing a season at pretty close to zero. I just don't think the owners have the collective will. I don't think the players do either, when push comes to shove.
Robert Stewart
After the Bregman injury, should MLB enforce the rule that on deck hitters should be in the on deck circle? I remember a few years ago when they did that and the batter (I think it was Beltre) moved the actual circle to where he was standing. He may have been ejected.
Ben Clemens
No, because clearly this enforcement wouldn't stick and no one likes feeling either like a nanny or like they're being nanny stated by the umpires. The Beltre thing was a while ago at this point I think? But a specific umpire told him to get back in the circle so he moved it. It wasn't at the same time as an enforcement push or anything, if I'm remembering correctly.
wheelhouse
Boston’s about to sail to the WS, no? Easy opponent after easy opponent ahead of them
Ben Clemens
A jinx? A stealth insult? Who knows, let's hit publish.
Vee
i would be very happy if this is not Pete's peak. I dream of 12 war PCA.
Ben Clemens
Haha right? That one was kind of a gimme just because it's SO hard to imagine a better season.
HappyFunBall
Is Kyle Harrison at risk of not even making the playoff roster?
Ben Clemens
Didn't realize that this was less of a fringe opinion and more of a 'thing people are thinking'. I guess that I underestimated it. I don't really think that it's likely because he's good! Clearly capable of dominance. But the Brewers have a lot more granular data and maybe they really do think he's cooked for the moment. I just…. c'mon, the guy was so good earlier this year, and if you leave him off the playoff roster in the NLDS, you're never bringing him back on, you're accepting that you're just playing without this big important piece. I just hate settling like that.
Tim Tebow's Thunder Thighs
Dider Fuentes is rolling as a mid-reliever, but do you think the Braves should stretch him back out into a starting role next year a la Strider?
Ben Clemens
I think they'll try, realize that he's better in this current role, and move him back. They should try even if they don't think it'll work. The odds of it working are obviously not zero and he'd be more valuable by a lot if it stuck
appayipyip
If you had to sit down and name every baseball player you can think of how many names could you get to?
Ben Clemens
Oh man. Hundreds. Probably a thousand? I think I'd get tired before I ran out of names. Playing OOTP for many years, and Perfect Team in particular (Paul Sporer curates the sets over there and does an incredible job of finding fun old players) has given me a big memory bank of names
Tim Tebow's Thunder Thighs
Holy crap, am I able to submit a question as a logged in FG member? That's the first time in months.
What you do suspect the Braves will do with Profar's contract after two long term suspensions with one year remaining (which isn't far off from a qualifying offer)? I can't imagine AA getting much of anything for him
Ben Clemens
Oh yeah…. I think they'll either cut him or trade him eating all the money for a lottery ticket.
Ben Clemens
Tebow sighting yesterday btw! At the Broncos Jags game. Florida man with Denver connections, makes sense.
Phil
Yes, by right I meant left, sorry, and thanks. Also, Sean, can we bring back the thing where your own question is blue? That was both pleasurable and, particulalry when illicitly following the chat on a phone at work, useful.
Ben Clemens
putting this in the log so Sean can see it too. I didn't even know about that feature. See, this is why it's good to test things.
jonmberra
Do you think the Mariners can fix their defense this offseason? Seems like they hit a little worse than expected, and the team imploded because their defense is terrible.
Ben Clemens
I do think this is fixable. I think it might kind of fix itself, to be honest. Their worst defenders by FRV are Crawford and Arozarena, both FA's. Luke Raley was bad in right before he got hurt, but he was also just not great overall, they're surely looking for better options. TO me, it looks like they're set up to improve on defense without even focusing on it specifically, just from the change in team composition.
draftdingers
Do the Cardinals test the trade market for Herrera this offseason and could they even get a good return? Burleson seems to be the First Basemen for the next few years and I can't see Herrera staying behind the plate with his subpar defense and the glut at catcher coming through the system.
Ben Clemens
I think that they'll test the trade market, and I think they will definitely get a good return if they decide to trade him. I think that zero-ish other teams see him as a catcher, though. I see him as a 1B/DH who can maybe be an emergency catcher, I didn't like the way the Cards kept tring him at catcher even after the writing was on the wall, at least to me.
Ben Clemens
But when I was bouncing players off of my sources this summer and talking about Herrera as a fringy name, probably not top 50 trade value but surely top 100, people didn't have much to say about that eitehr way, which suggests to me that it's roughly right. Good plus bat, might benefit from not having to play catcher so often, cost controlled for a while. Teams would be interested in this for sure. He has a batting line 20% above average for his career and doesnt' cost much; the pitch sells itself.
kingkash7788
how much has nimmala rose post trade deadline
Ben Clemens
This is really more of a question for the prospect guys than for me but his stock is clearly up, impressive performance in Double-A at 20. I am not sure he's their starting shortstop on opening day next year because Neto is awesome and I'm not sold on a move to third base being inevitable. But I think that he's clearly arrow up from what we thought of him at the deadline. Good trade for the Angels. Might be a win-win, I think Soriano is gonna play well in Toronto next year, but the Angels have 100% done well there.
HappyFunBall
re: Dider Fuentes. The question to ask is not whether or not he'll be better as a reliever. MOST pitchers are. That's why they get put there in the first place. The question to ask is will Fuentes be able to thrive in a 5+ innings role or not.
Ben Clemens
Concur with this. And my thinking there is that if you're being honest with yourself, it's not certain whether he'll thrive in a 5+ inning role but he certainly hasn't ruled it out with his performance. Particularly if the Braves feel good about his feel for the splitter, which he's basically been able to mothball in relief but would surely need to add back in as a starter, I think it'd be crazy NOT to try. He's 21 and destroying major league hitting and came up as a starter.
sloejoe
Thanks for the chat! Is Robert Gasser a starter next year? According to Roster Resource he is their 5th starter. Has he shown to have the stuff to move up?
Ben Clemens
Yeah, the Brewers always use a bunch of starters interchangeably throughout the year but I have no reason to think he won't be one of them.
appayipyip
If you were the Jays would you try to extend Soriano?
Ben Clemens
I would. The weird part is the timing – like, if they haven't started on it now, I doubt they're getting it done before the lockout unless both sides really want it. So is it a next year post lockout kinda thing? Maybe. But I am generally a fan of trying to sign contract extensions when it makes even a little sense, and this one clearyl makes some sense.
fincampbell05
What are the Red Sox going to do? They're going to have some money to spend, but there really isn't a clear hole on the roster except for SS, where they surely would not sign someone that blocks Arias, if there were even any good free agent shortstops.
Ben Clemens
This isn't a great year to spend money, it's looking like. But that suits them just fine – like you said, there isn't a super clear hole on the roster aside from shortstop. And for me, backup at 3B because I dno't quite believe Durbin's torrid stretch. But I think I'd just be willing to keep some powder dry, basically. I think we've discussed their payroll situation some in recent weeks; it's really well set-up for next year, very few players leaving. Maybe they try to work out another year of Sonny Gray, maybe they just top up on pitching, but this is a great year to not need a bunch of players in FA, because the FA class is not good. I don't think they need to overcomplicate things too much – they went hard last winter, they can cool it this winter.
Rayball
Who do you have emerging in this final week between TEX and HOU?
Ben Clemens
Houston because they're like the bogeyman, they always seem to keep coming even when you think they're done. But no strong lean
drplantwrench
Also another note: it would be nice to make `Your questions awaiting the host` collapsible
Ben Clemens
Noted.
randomname1234
If you're the Red Sox, do you tank this week and hope to get WC#3 instead of WC#2? Almost certainly not catching NY for WC#1, and road games against AL West and AL Central winners sound much better than road games against Yankees and Tampa.
Ben Clemens
A few people asked versions of this earlier, I happened to like this phrasing most. But I'm answering all of your questions. No. I'd be happy if that happened, but I would not mess with wanting my good players to play well a week before the playoffs, for marginal gain. Matchups matter, but only so much, and there's no guarantee.
bosoxforlife
I do not understand why teams don't see players like Herrera as a potential career DH and as a very valuable third catcher. Mickey Gasper is presently showing just how valuable that type of player is even if doesn't keep hitting at this level. When a team has two catchers it really only has one but with three all can be used freely.
Ben Clemens
Oh I 100% agree. I think this is a leak among teams. And Herrera hits well enough, or at least projects to hit well enough, that you're not sacrificing offense anywhere, it's just free-ish value.
Phillip Denny
Do you think Luzardo's injury means he's just a glorified opener (or maybe gives you 2-3) in the WC/DS? If so, is there an argument for turning him into a late inning fireman instead?
Ben Clemens
I am unsure, but I am leaning towards him having very short starts, at which case yes, I'd prefer him as an impact reliever. I don't know if he is ready to warm up and play in that role, though, and given his at-times-injured past and his contract, if I'm the Phillies, I want him to give me a strong sign that he's interested in this role and thinks he'd do well at it
Ben Clemens
Okay everyone, this was a wonderful chat, but now I'm going to go have that aforementioned salmon and start working on an article for tomorrow.
Ben Clemens
Thanks for all the great questions, and for helping us test out the new chat interface. May the last week of the regular season be delightful for you, and let's get ready for the playoffs.
Ben is a writer at FanGraphs. He can be found on Bluesky @benclemens.

item.title: [Yahoo Sports] Spencer Jones is earning his spot on the postseason roster
item.dc:creator: Dani Mohr
item.description: Spencer Jones is finally gaining some momentum at the plate and earning his spot on the postseason roster after making some needed adjustments. Who does he have to thank, you might ask? Aaron Judge's hitting coach, perhaps. Jones, whose height and build are very similar to the Yankees captain, first met with Judge's hitting coach, Richard Schenk, during the offseason to make adjustments to his stance. item.content:encoded:
Spencer Jones is finally gaining some momentum at the plate and earning his spot on the postseason roster after making some needed adjustments. Who does he have to thank, you might ask?
Aaron Judge's hitting coach, perhaps.
Jones, whose height and build are very similar to the Yankees captain, first met with Judge's hitting coach, Richard Schenk, during the offseason to make adjustments to his stance. Although he may still struggle with frequent strikeouts, Jones is making a lot of positive progress that has helped him earn his place on this team.
The 25-year-old outfielder is hitting a .279 average with a .343 on-base percentage and .475 slugging percentage in September. Among Yankees, his .819 OPS and 130 wRC+ for the month are topped only by Ben Rice and Cody Bellinger, helping boost a Bombers lineup that sagged in August. After dealing with a sore left foot that kept him sidelined on Saturday, Jones returned to the lineup prepared to make some noise and launched a 448-foot homer off Corbin Burnes during the series finale against the Diamondbacks.
With Grisham still recovering from a right hamstring strain, Jones will be a valuable asset in the outfield—be it in center or right—who adds some depth to the lineup as well. It's also worth noting that Aaron Judge, who joined the IL on Friday with a right calf strain, will likely be sidelined for the beginning of the playoff run. As long as Jones can focus on developing his swing through these critical postseason at-bats, he has the potential to help the Yankees go far.
Beginning tomorrow afternoon, the Yankees will face the Rays in a critical four-game series that will ultimately determine the division and could even serve as a playoff preview. If he can stay consistent with his offensive production, Jones might just be the secret the Pinstripes need to seize the American League.

item.content:encoded:
PHOENIX -- Varias latas de cerveza fueron vaciadas sobre la cabeza de Aaron Judge mientras el capitán de los Yankees permanecía en el centro del clubhouse de visitantes en el Target Field la semana pasada, rodeado de compañeros eufóricos que celebraban la clasificación del club a la postemporada.
Judge entrecerró los ojos por el ardor y les advirtió a sus compañeros: “Me las van a pagar”.
Aun así, no pretenden que ésa sea su última celebración, pues tienen un firme control del primer puesto del Comodín de la Liga Americana y el título del Este de la Liga Americana todavía está en juego.
“Siempre es bueno cuando puedes celebrar esos momentos durante una temporada”, dijo el manager de los Yankees, Aaron Boone. “Mucha gente dedica mucho tiempo, esfuerzo y sudor. Obviamente, éste es apenas el primer paso de lo que esperamos sean muchos”.
Ahora que aseguraron su pase a la postemporada, ¿qué más les espera a los Yankees?
¿Cómo podría quedar el roster para la postemporada?
C: Austin Wells, Ali Sánchez 
1B: Luis García Jr., Paul Goldschmidt
2B: Jazz Chisholm Jr.
3B: Ryan McMahon, Amed Rosario
SS: George Lombard Jr., José Caballero
OF: Cody Bellinger, Trent Grisham, Spencer Jones, Heliot Ramos
BD: Ben Rice
LA: Gerrit Cole, Cam Schlittler, Max Fried
R: David Bednar, Paul Blackburn, Brent Headrick, Tim Hill, Clarke Schmidt, Michael Fulmer, John Schreiber, Will Warren, Carlos Rodón
Los Yankees utilizaron a 12 lanzadores y a 14 bateadores cuando recibieron a los Medias Rojas en la Serie del Comodín de la Liga Americana del año pasado, así que partiremos de esa misma premisa para el 2026.
Cole está programado para lanzar el miércoles contra Tampa Bay, mientras que Schlittler lo hará el jueves. Mirando hacia adelante, eso sugiere que Cole tendría un día adicional de descanso antes del Juego 1 de la Serie del Comodín de la Liga Americana, mientras que Schlittler estaría con su descanso normal.
Es posible que los Yankees estén alineando a Cole para abrir el Juego 1 y a Schlittler para el Juego 2. Hasta ahora, han preferido no decir mucho al respecto, salvo por la confirmación de Boone de que Cole realizará una apertura en la Serie del Comodín de la Liga Americana.
Rodón podría estar en el bullpen para la serie. En nuestra proyección del roster lo tenemos activo, mientras que el dominicano Luis Gil y Ryan Yarbrough figuran entre quienes quedarían fuera. Ryan Weathers trabaja para regresar como relevista, pero el tiempo juega en su contra. Si está saludable, podría ocupar el lugar de Fulmer o Schreiber.
Chisholm espera regresar esta semana para la serie contra los Rays tras sufrir un esguince en el pulgar derecho, mientras que Grisham ha mostrado mejoría y podría quedarse con un puesto en los jardines. De no ser así, Max Schuemann está entre las alternativas. Otro aspecto para seguir: ¿Podrían los Yankees incluir a Anthony Volpe en lugar de Rosario? Es una posibilidad que vale la pena considerar.
¿Cuándo comenzará la postemporada?
Si los Yankees terminan disputando la Serie del Comodín de la Liga Americana, ésta empezará el 29 de septiembre. La Serie Divisional de la Liga Americana arrancará el 3 de octubre.
¿Contra quién jugarían los Yankees si la temporada terminara hoy?
En estos momentos, sería una revancha de la Serie del Comodín de la Liga Americana del año pasado, con los Yankees recibiendo a los Medias Rojas en el Bronx. Los Yankees ganaron aquella serie dos victorias por una.
Este año, los Yankees tuvieron marca de 7-6 contra Boston.
¿Todavía pueden ganar el Este de la Liga Americana?
Sí, pero tienen un camino cuesta arriba. Los Yankees tienen por delante cuatro enfrentamientos directos con los Rays a partir del martes en el Yankee Stadium, incluyendo una doble-cartelera para abrir la serie. Tampa Bay domina actualmente la serie particular por 6-3, lo que significa que los Yankees necesitarían barrer para quedarse con el criterio de desempate entre ambos.
¿Quién abriría el Juego 1 por los Yankees?
Como se mencionó anteriormente, Cole está programado para lanzar el miércoles frente a Tampa Bay y Schlittler lo hará al día siguiente. Por lo tanto, Cole tendría un día adicional de descanso antes del Juego 1 de la Serie del Comodín de la Liga Americana, mientras que Schlittler estaría con su descanso normal.
Después de permitir siete jonrones en sus dos aperturas anteriores, Cole mermó las dudas externas sobre una posible apertura en los playoffs con una sólida actuación en Arizona. Fried y Rodón han lidiado con lesiones, pero están recuperando su mejor nivel en el momento indicado.
Warren realizará una apertura más durante la serie contra los Orioles, según Boone, pero llegará a los playoffs como una interesante alternativa para el relevo.
¿Será Judge un factor en los playoffs?
Los Yankees han sido poco específicos sobre el estado de Judge. Boone ha evitado ofrecer un plazo estimado para su recuperación e incluso revelar el grado del tirón en la pantorrilla derecha. En términos generales, hasta un tirón de Grado 1, el de menor gravedad, requiere de dos a tres semanas para una recuperación completa.
Es casi seguro que Judge intentará regresar antes. La primera fecha en la que podría ser activado sería para el Juego 162, el 27 de septiembre. Tal como está el panorama ahora mismo, existe una posibilidad muy real de que los Yankees no cuenten con Judge al menos para una potencial Serie del Comodín de la Liga Americana.
Judge dijo que le “gustaría” estar activo para la postemporada y que ése es “el plan”, pero no dijo necesariamente que sería para el 29 de septiembre.
¿Cuáles son las otras preocupaciones en cuanto a lesiones?
Grisham ha avanzado en su programa progresivo de correr y debe de estar disponible para el roster de los playoffs, aunque Boone dijo que no será activado antes de que termine la temporada regular. Chisholm ha estado bateando y realizando tiros, y debe de ser activado durante la serie contra los Rays. Si sufre algún contratiempo, Volpe entraría en consideración.
Y aunque los Yankees no han descartado a Giancarlo Stanton, quien ha estado bateando, han ofrecido pocas novedades sobre su recuperación del más reciente tirón en la pantorrilla.

item.title: [fansided.com] The Yankees just found their unexpected Aaron Judge replacement at the perfect time
item.dc:creator: Jake Elman
item.description: We know what you’re thinking: The New York Yankees cannot realistically replace Aaron Judge. Unfortunately for Aaron Boone and Brian Cashman, they have no choice. Judge landed back on the injured list with a right calf strain, and the earliest that he could return is next Sunday’s regular-season finale against the Orioles. item.content:encoded:
We know what you’re thinking: The New York Yankees cannot realistically replace Aaron Judge.
Unfortunately for Aaron Boone and Brian Cashman, they have no choice. Judge landed back on the injured list with a right calf strain, and the earliest that he could return is next Sunday’s regular-season finale against the Orioles. The Yankees have not committed to the three-time AL MVP potentially being ready for the AL Wild Card Series.
“I usually deal with calf stuff all year long,” Judge told reporters on Saturday. “It usually doesn’t get to [the media], and I usually don’t miss any games. So that was kind of the same thing I was feeling. I was working my way back, and then something kind of grabs you at a strange time.”
So, who will man right field in Judge’s absence? Will it be Spencer Jones, who has flashed as a rookie? What about Cody Bellinger, who could shift over from left field?
As it turns out, the answer might be speedy utilityman José Caballero. Seriously.
José Caballero could start in the Yankees’ outfield following Aaron Judge’s latest injury
The 30-year-old Caballero drew the start in center field on Saturday night, hitting two singles and drawing the walk in a 5-3 loss. He's played 20 of his 130 games in the outfield, with most of that action coming in the corner spots.
For what it’s worth, we’ve always liked Caballero enough that we repeatedly advocated for the Yankees to consider naming him the full-time shortstop and trading Anthony Volpe. So we’re not opposed to the thought of him playing right, with Bellinger starting in center and Heliot Ramos taking over in left field.
The 5-foot-9, 190-pound Caballero's calling card has always been his legs, and he's stolen at least 26 bases in each of his first four seasons. This year has been no exception, with him swiping a team-leading 32 bases in 43 attempts. But to his credit, Caballero has added some power to his game, recording a career-high 14 home runs in nearly 450 plate appearances.
Bellinger has played 118 of his 127 games in left field, though he has extensive experience in both center and right. The reigning All-Star Game MVP is also one of the Yankees' most reliable hitters, even as his OPS has dropped from .813 to .781.
Objectively speaking, the Yankees can afford to have an outfield consisting of Caballero, Bellinger, and either Ramos or Jones. Trent Grisham remains out with a right hamstring problem, though Boone has hinted they’d get the two-time Gold Glove winner back in time for the playoffs. As things stand, the Yankees would host the rival Red Sox in a first-round rematch of last year’s Wild Card Series.
Ideally for the Yankees, they’ll have Judge batting second and playing right field next Tuesday night. But if you’re looking for a dark horse candidate to shine this postseason, you could do far worse than the versatile Caballero.

item.title: [fansided.com] Grading Bleacher Report's latest Paul Skenes trade proposals to the Yankees and Mets

item.content:encoded:
You know that the Pittsburgh Pirates’ offseason has officially arrived when we’re talking about a potential Paul Skenes trade.
It’s been a bit, hasn’t it? The Pirates remained in NL Wild Card contention throughout the second half, which ordinarily would be enough to halt the annual speculation. But Skenes has looked nothing like his Cy Young self, and he could realistically end the year with an ERA above 4.00. This is the same pitcher who had a 1.96 ERA through his first 320.2 innings and looked unhittable most nights.
In the grand scheme of things, nothing has changed. Skenes hasn’t publicly requested a trade, and the Pirates have insisted they won’t trade the three-time All-Star. Objectively, we imagine he’ll be toeing the mound on Opening Day 2027, whenever that might be.
Bleacher Report’s Zachary D. Rymer nonetheless pitched (pun intended) two possible Skenes trades, one involving the Yankees and another featuring Mets. Needless to say, we have plenty of thoughts.
Yankees send Ben Rice, Spencer Jones, and two pitchers to the Pirates for Paul Skenes and Bryan Reynolds
Pirates grade: C+
Yankees grade: C-
Those who spend much of their free time scrolling X/Twitter (hey, we know the feeling all too well) are likely familiar with the meme of Bugs Bunny squinting his eyes and saying “No.” That’s exactly how we felt upon initially seeing this trade offer.
Let’s start with the obvious: the Yankees aren’t trading Rice. At no point did we hear his name floated amid the Tarik Skubal rumors, and his left-handed power makes him a perfect fit for Yankee Stadium’s short porch. He’ll either open next season as the starting first baseman or designated hitter, depending on what Giancarlo Stanton’s future looks like; the 2017 NL MVP has one year left on his deal, and he’s been an injury liability since the start of 2019.
We’re skeptical that Jones would be moved unless the return involves an MVP-caliber outfielder. Trent Grisham is a pending free agent, and we’re genuinely unsure what Jasson Domínguez’s future in New York looks like, especially after his recent demotion to Triple-A. When a team doesn’t want you on the big-league roster ahead of the playoffs, what does that say?
Reynolds has had a fine year, and he entered Sunday leading the league in doubles. But if you’re the Yankees, do you really want to give up Jones and Lagrange for an outfielder who turns 32 in January? Reynolds is under contract through 2030 (with a $20 million team option for 2031), and that’s a significant commitment to someone who, at his best, is a mid-3 bWAR player.
We must also note that Rymer claimed that Rodríguez ranked No. 82 and Lagrange placed No. 100 on MLB Pipeline, which is simply untrue. Shortstop Dax Kilby is the only Yankees player on the most recent MLB Pipeline list, and he placed No. 83. So the Pirates wouldn’t even be landing a top-100 prospect? Hard pass.
That said, we’ll give the Yankees a C- for their return, because an elite Skenes ranks among the game’s best pitchers. But will we see him regain that 2024-25 form? That we’re even asking the question should say enough.
Mets give up Carson Benge and two prospects for Pirates teammates Paul Skenes and Bryan Reynolds
Pirates grade: D
Mets grade: C
At least the proposed Pirates-Yankees trade made some sense. We can’t say the same about Pittsburgh theoretically shipping Skenes and Reynolds to the Mets for Benge, Rojas, and Tong.
First off, why would the Mets only need to give up three players rather than the Yankees’ four? Rymer listed Rojas as the No. 79 prospect and Tong at No. 88, neither of which is accurate; Rojas is No. 73, and MLB Pipeline no longer lists Tong among its top 100 prospects, for reasons we don’t understand. Mariners lefty Kade Anderson has thrown 25.1 big-league innings, and he's still ranked No. 5, but Tong and his 39.2 innings over two seasons no longer qualify. Huh?
Benge has quietly enjoyed a solid rookie season, hitting .276 with 19 home runs, 61 RBIs, 22 steals, and a .760 OPS through his first 149 games. But for him to be the centerpiece of a deal involving both Skenes and Reynolds is absurd. Oh, and Benge turns 24 in January, so he’d be a slightly older second-year starter.
As for the Mets, adding yet another long-term contract isn’t the answer to putting their disastrous 2026 season behind them. As we’ve said before, Bo Bichette would be foolish to exercise his opt-out clause and leave $42 million in guaranteed money on the table. Marcus Semien has two years and $46 million left on his deal, and we’re not even factoring in Francisco Lindor’s contract.
That said, we’ve seen enough positives from Benge thus far to hold off on giving the Pirates’ theoretical return an “F” grade. But both teams should pass on even contemplating such an offer.

September 21 Notes
Falling off: Aaron Judge (ninth), Dylan Cease (40th), Alex Bregman (43rd), Andrés Muñoz (71st), Jesús Luzardo (93rd), Troy Melton (117th), Bryce Eldridge (140th) and 36 other players.
- It’s a fool’s errand, but here’s one last update for the final week of the season. I tried emphasizing two-start starters unless they’re particularly dangerous, but I also tried to take into account that some of the guys currently in line to start twice are going to end up being scratched or making only brief appearances next weekend.
- With no updates yet on Alex Bregman (face) and Andrés Muñoz (knee), I’ve dropped both from the rankings. Pedro Ramírez, who was set to fall off the list with Dansby Swanson back, reclaimed a spot in Bregman’s place. Seranthony Domínguez seems like the likeliest choice for saves in Seattle in Muñoz’s place, so he comes in at No. 166.
- Thank you so much to everyone who has followed along all season. Anyone interested in the full spreadsheet of where players have ranked start to finish, reach out to my gmail at matthewpouliot. I’ll be back in mid-October with the first (or second) go at a 2027 Top 300.
September 14 Notes
Falling off: Shohei Ohtani DH (eighth), Rafael Devers (41st), Jazz Chisholm Jr. (58th), Bryce Miller (177th), Gleyber Torres (183rd), Hayden Wesneski (206th), Royce Lewis (214th), Kyle Bradish (222nd), Michael McGreevy (243rd), Brandon Pfaadt (246th), Braxton Ashcraft (250th) and 21 other players
- I don’t have much of a notes section for you right now, since it’s after 3 am and I’d like to get some sleep. Still, the rankings are updated for the final 14 days of the season. A lot of the pitcher movement this week is elevating guys with three starts remaining and dropping those with only two. I also gave Rockies hitters a nice boost, as they play 10 of their remaining 13 games at home. Padres hitters also got a little lift from that, as they’ll be starting a four-game series in Coors Field on Monday.
September 7 Notes
Falling off: Kyle Harrison (101st), Shane McClanahan (125th), Luis Robert Jr. (163rd), Trent Graham (180th), Joe Musgrove (192nd), Byron Buxton (202nd), Cam Smith (219th), Brendan Donovan (227th), JJ Wetherholt (236th), Eric Lauer (243rd), Jesús Sánchez (247th), Xavier Edwards (254th), Sean Manaea (261st), Samuel Basallo (262nd), Nathan Eovaldi (265th), Connor Norby (268th), Chase Burns (273rd), Shohei Ohtani SP (280th), Tommy White (282nd), Daniel Palencia (285th), Colton Cowser (286th), Taylor Ward (289th), Ezequiel Tovar (290th), Alek Thomas (292nd), Willi Castro (294th), Elvis Alvarado (295th), Brandyn Garcia (299th)
- With three weeks to go, nearly every injured player is off the rankings at this point, with the exception of a few guys hopefully returning before the end of this week. Also, I’m paying a lot more attention to matchups, particularly this week’s. So, some starters with multiple starts this week who wouldn’t normally be in the top 300 make the cut. Also, Athletics hitters have moved up, since they’ll be at home for six games this week. Rockies hitters have dropped off as that team goes back on the road after a week of home games.
- Rafael Devers gets an overdue late bump. There really was good reason for concern early on with his strikeout rate up and his bat speed down, but he bounced back nicely in both categories. Amazing is the consistency in his wOBAs since 2021: .373, .373, .359, .364, .365 and .365. His xwOBAs, on the other hand, still show a little decline: .391, .365, .380, .366, .367, .340. Still, it’s been a really impressive season, and getting to 100 runs scored (maybe) and 100 RBI (almost certainly) on the moribund Giants offense is one heck of an accomplishment.
- The Orioles getting swept by Red Sox over the weekend, dropping their postseason odds at Fangraphs to just three percent, would seem to greatly increase the chances that Kyle Bradish gets shut down with a week or two to go. He’s up to 152 innings in his first full year back from Tommy John, and he’s not exactly doing his best work at the moment.
- Kyle Harrison might have lost his rotation spot with his performance Sunday against the Reds, though I thought about keeping him on the list anyway, since he could be well set up for wins in middle relief if moved to the pen. In the end, he didn’t quite make the cut. It will be really interesting to see how the Brewers play things the rest of the way. I imagine both Jacob Misiorowski and Logan Henderson will make a couple of shorter starts in an attempt to save bullets for October.
- It’ll be nice to see Corbin Burnes back on a major league mound Tuesday, but given that he threw just two innings in his lone rehab start after Tommy John, so I couldn’t see including him here just yet. San Diego’s Nick Pivetta, on the other hand, at least made it up to 4 1/3 innings in his last rehab start as he returns from an elbow injury. That gets him a spot on the bottom of the list, even if he’s a long shot to get a win Monday in his return.

item.content:encoded:
PHOENIX — Los Yankees se fueron del Chase Field con el tipo de derrota que hace que un solo lanzamiento parezca más importante que todo un fin de semana.
Una ventaja de 4-1 se esfumó en la quinta entrada del domingo. La culpa recayó sobre Brent Headrick, el caballo de batalla de los Yankees y cuyo brazo había estado impecable hasta entonces.
Nolan Arenado conectó el golpe que selló la remontada. Su grand slam puso a Arizona por delante y contribuyó a que Nueva York cayera por 8-4 en su último partido fuera de casa de la temporada regular.
La entrada empezó con Will Warren aún defendiendo una ventaja de tres carreras. Arizona llenó las bases con un out antes de que Aaron Boone recurriera al bullpen. Los Yankees ya habían anotado jonrones en la tercera entrada gracias a Heliot Ramos, George Lombard Jr. y Spencer Jones, una racha que sacó del partido a Corbin Burnes y puso el partido brevemente bajo el control de Nueva York.
Headrick entró con las bases llenas. Eliminó a Geraldo Perdomo por strikeout para conseguir el segundo out y, a continuación, concedió una base por bolas a Corbin Carroll, lo que permitió que entrara una carrera. Arenado mandó la siguiente bola fuera por la línea del campo izquierdo. Un lanzamiento después, la bola se quedó dentro del campo.
Ese jonrón de cuatro carreras cambió el marcador de 4-2 a una ventaja de 6-4 para Arizona. Headrick se llevó la derrota y no se le atribuyó ningún salvamento.
La cifra detrás del Grand Slam es motivo de gran preocupación para los Yankees
El problema más grave salió a la luz tras el partido. La bola rápida de Headrick tenía una velocidad notablemente menor que la que había tenido durante la mayor parte de esta temporada en la que ha destacado. El zurdo alcanzó una media de 92,9 mph con ese lanzamiento el domingo, según una publicación del periodista especializado en los Yankees, Brendan Kuty. Baseball Savant sitúa el promedio de la bola de cuatro costuras de Headrick en 94,2 mph para 2026.
Esa diferencia de 1,3 mph no significa que haya una lesión, y no se ha informado de que Headrick esté lesionado. Pero llega al final de una carga de trabajo como ninguna otra que haya tenido que afrontar como relevista de las Grandes Ligas. Headrick ha jugado 79 partidos y ha lanzado 77 entradas. La MLB lo registra con un balance de 7-4, una efectividad de 2,10, 96 strikeouts, 25 bases por bolas y un WHIP de 1,18.
La publicación de Kuty puso en perspectiva el cambio de velocidad tras la salida más desastrosa de Headrick esta temporada.
«La velocidad media de la bola rápida de Headrick esta noche en Arizona contra los Diamondbacks fue de 92,9 mph», escribió Kuty.
Headrick ha lanzado dos días seguidos en Arizona, lanzando dos tercios de entrada el sábado y otra vez el domingo. Ha sumado 10 ponches en 8 1/3 entradas en septiembre, hasta el domingo.
Headrick se acerca a un hito que pocos Yankees han alcanzado
Lo que diferencia esta temporada de una carga de trabajo habitual como relevista es la frecuencia. Headrick ha lanzado en 79 de los 155 partidos de los Yankees, algo más de la mitad del calendario. La MLB informó el domingo de que solo un lanzador de las Grandes Ligas ha salido al campo más veces esta temporada.
La historia del equipo le da aún más peso a esa cifra. Paul Quantrill estableció el récord de la franquicia de los Yankees con 86 apariciones en 2004. Scott Proctor jugó 83 partidos en 2006. Las 79 de Headrick ya igualan el total de Mike Stanton en 2002 y el de Tom Gordon en 2005. A falta de siete partidos, ya está protagonizando una de las temporadas más intensas en el bullpen que ha vivido la franquicia.
El cambio respecto a 2025 es considerable. Según los datos de la MLB, Headrick lanzó 23 entradas con los Yankees y 24 en la Triple A la temporada pasada. Sus 77 entradas en las Grandes Ligas este año ya superan ese total combinado en 30 entradas.
Este bajón de final de temporada es importante, ya que los Yankees necesitan la mejor versión de octubre .
Las estadísticas de Headrick en toda la temporada siguen convirtiéndolo en una de las piezas más sólidas del bullpen de los Yankees. Solo ha cedido cinco jonrones en los 318 bateadores a los que se ha enfrentado. Ha mantenido a los bateadores diestros en un promedio de .205, según los datos actuales de la MLB sobre estadísticas por tipo de bateador, lo que le ha ayudado a evitar quedarse relegado a un papel de relevo específico para determinados enfrentamientos.
Sus últimas actuaciones no han sido tan buenas. En sus últimas siete salidas, Headrick tiene una efectividad de 4,76 en 5 2/3 entradas. Es una muestra pequeña, pero el momento es clave porque Boone va a necesitar opciones fiables en el bullpen para respaldar a la rotación de la postemporada.
Los Yankees prepararon a Headrick para que tuviera una carga de trabajo más intensa durante el invierno. El entrenador de lanzadores, Matt Blake, ya había identificado la recuperación como el principal reto hace meses, cuando Headrick ya se encontraba entre los relevistas más utilizados de la MLB. La pregunta ahora es si los Yankees podrán reducir su tiempo de juego durante la última semana sin que pierda esa precisión que lo ha convertido en indispensable.
Los Yankees tienen ahora que tomar una decisión sobre el descanso en plena lucha por el título de la División Este de la Liga Americana
Para los Yankees, esta derrota ha puesto las cuentas de la División Este de la Liga Americana al límite. Nueva York tiene un balance de 89-66 y está a seis partidos de Tampa Bay, cuando quedan siete partidos por disputar. Los Yankees ya se han asegurado una plaza en la postemporada, pero ahora empiezan una serie de cuatro partidos en casa contra los Rays con muy poco margen en la lucha por el título de la división.
El domingo también se cerró un balance de 47-34 como visitantes, uno de los mejores registros fuera de casa del béisbol.
Nueva York termina con tres partidos contra Baltimore después de enfrentarse a Tampa Bay. Como ya no hay que viajar después de Arizona y el mes de octubre ya está asegurado, la última semana sirve también para decidir qué lanzadores están listos para la postemporada. Por eso, el estado del cuerpo de lanzadores es casi tan importante como la propia clasificación.
La serie contra los Rays complica esa decisión. Mientras la división siga matemáticamente abierta, los Yankees tienen motivos para usar a sus mejores relevos disponibles en partidos reñidos. Si Tampa Bay se asegura el título, la situación cambia rápidamente. Proteger el brazo de Headrick y que recupere su bola rápida habitual podría llegar a ser más importante que otra entrada decisiva para la clasificación.
El grand slam del domingo seguirá siendo el error más evidente porque decidió el partido. Lo que pasa más desapercibido es lo que los Yankees tienen que vigilar ahora. Headrick ha llevado el peso del bullpen durante seis meses, y su bola rápida llegó a Arizona en su momento más flojo, justo cuando octubre está a la vuelta de la esquina.
¿Qué te parece? Deja tu comentario aquí abajo.

item.title: [Empire Sports Media] Spencer Jones just made the Yankees' October call harder
item.dc:creator: Alexander Wilson

item.content:encoded:
Spencer Jones went 1-for-4 with a homer in Saturday’s loss to Arizona, and the hit was not some isolated late-September blip. He has a .279 average, a .343 on-base percentage and a .475 slugging percentage this month.
The catch is sitting right next to it. Jones has struck out 27 times in 68 September plate appearances. That creates a lot of empty trips for a team that may have to win tight games in October, especially with every at-bat getting picked apart.
Still, I do not see how the Yankees can act like the power is optional. Jones has three homers and 14 RBIs this month, and his season line sits at 11 homers with a .759 OPS in 81 games. He is making the hard part of this decision harder, which is a decent place for a young player to be.
The Yankees need to make the power count
Jones gives the lineup something it cannot manufacture with a safer bench piece. The ball comes off his bat differently, and opponents have to respect the damage even when the at-bat is not clean.
That matters because New York does not have the luxury of building an October group around players who merely look tidy. If the games turn into three-run affairs, one Jones homer can change an inning before a manager reaches for a pinch hitter.
The strikeouts will decide the rest
Jones does not get a free pass because he is young or because the homers are fun. The strikeout rate is real, and postseason pitching has a way of exposing loose at-bats quickly.
But there is a useful middle ground here. The Yankees do not need to hand him a permanent everyday role, and they do not need to bury him because the whiffs are ugly. They need to decide whether the power is worth carrying in the spots where it can do the most damage.
The October call is not simple. Jones has made it impossible to treat as a simple yes-or-no question.
More about:New York Yankees

item.title: [Pinstripes Nation] El último Susto Por La Lesión De Clarke Schmidt Podría Obligar A Los Yankees A Replantearse Cuál Será Su Papel En El Futuro
item.dc:creator: Sara Molnick
item.description: NUEVA YORK — Los Yankees se han pasado casi todo septiembre organizando a los lanzadores para la fase de octubre. item.content:encoded:
NUEVA YORK — Los Yankees se han pasado casi todo septiembre organizando a los lanzadores para la fase de octubre.
Gerrit Cole está en la lista para ser el lanzador titular en la Serie de Comodín. Cam Schlittler se ha ganado un sitio en esa misma conversación.
Max Fried vuelve a la rotación, mientras que Carlos Rodón y Will Warren están en la lista para lanzar como relevos una vez que empiece la postemporada. Estas decisiones han dejado poco margen para que algún aspirante de última hora se cuele de nuevo en el grupo de titulares.
Eso limitó las opciones de Clarke Schmidt incluso antes de que volviera a incorporarse a la plantilla. Su regreso tras una segunda operación de Tommy John nunca se planteó con el objetivo de volver a alcanzar el volumen de trabajo de un lanzador titular en las dos últimas semanas.
Los Yankees lo incorporaron al plantilla el 16 de septiembre para aportar duración, lanzamientos certeros y una variedad de lanzamientos propios de un abridor desde el bullpen. No había jugado en las Grandes Ligas desde el 3 de julio de 2025, y solo había lanzado siete entradas en las ligas menores durante su rehabilitación.
Schmidt volvió esa noche en Minnesota y consiguió dos outs, permitiendo dos sencillos de rebote y ponchando a dos. Fue su primera aparición en las Grandes Ligas en 14 meses y medio. Y lo más importante para los Yankees es que supuso el inicio de una prueba para un papel que requiere una rutina diferente.
En lugar de un día fijo de salida y una larga preparación previa al partido, Schmidt ahora tiene que entrar en calor rápidamente, salir al campo en medio de la acción o en una entrada limpia, y recuperarse siguiendo el horario de un relevista.
La situación de la plantilla ya no dejaba margen para que volviera a la rotación. Según las previsiones actuales de la MLB para la postemporada de los Yankees, Cole, Schlittler y Fried figuran como titulares, mientras que Schmidt, Rodon y Warren están entre las opciones de relevo.
Aaron Boone ha confirmado que Cole será el lanzador titular en una posible serie de comodín. Warren tiene prevista una última salida como titular en la temporada regular antes de pasar al bullpen. La posibilidad de que Schmidt volviera a ser titular se había convertido en algo más teórico que práctico para este octubre.
Un problema en el bíceps interrumpe la única prueba que le quedaba a Schmidt
Esa diferencia se hizo aún más evidente el domingo en Arizona. Clarke Schmidt estaba calentando para lo que habría sido su segunda salida desde la operación cuando notó un calambre en el bíceps derecho durante la derrota de los Yankees por 8-4 ante los Diamondbacks en el Chase Field. Dejó de lanzar y no llegó a salir al campo.
Los Yankees dijeron que las pruebas de fuerza no indicaban ningún problema en el hombro ni en el codo. Se espera que Schmidt vea a un médico del equipo en Nueva York, sin que, por el momento, se hayan previsto más pruebas.
Schmidt explicó por qué se negó a seguir adelante a pesar de esa sensación tan pronto después de la operación. Respondía a la pregunta de si ese episodio sugería un contratiempo estructural.
«No es nada estructural, fue más bien por precaución», dijo Schmidt. «Obviamente, dadas las circunstancias, al estar recuperándome de una operación, no quiero forzar nada. Todas las pruebas salieron bien, ni el hombro ni el codo presentan problemas. Era más bien una sensación parecida a un calambre. No he tenido ningún problema al atrapar la pelota hoy por la mañana y en los últimos días me he sentido muy fuerte. Así que fue algo muy, muy leve, solo por precaución».
Boone dijo que Schmidt no pudo terminar su calentamiento a pesar de haber superado las pruebas iniciales.
«Espero que no sea nada grave, pero sí lo suficiente como para que no entre en el partido», dijo Boone. «Ya veremos qué pasa».
En su lugar, Tim Hill lanzó la sexta entrada. Los Yankees habían conseguido una ventaja de 4-1 gracias a los jonrones de Heliot Ramos, George Lombard Jr. y Spencer Jones en la tercera entrada, antes de que Arizona anotara cinco carreras en la quinta, coronadas por el grand slam de Nolan Arenado ante Brent Headrick. Justin Martínez se llevó la victoria, Headrick la derrota y no se acreditó ningún salvamento.
Un historial de 67 partidos como titular se enfrenta a un futuro repleto de jugadores en los Yankees
Schmidt ya ha demostrado que puede ser titular en las Grandes Ligas. Según los registros de la MLB, 67 de sus 97 partidos como profesional han sido como titular. Tiene una efectividad de 3,82 en 393 1/3 entradas y registró una efectividad de 3,32 en 14 partidos como titular en 2025, antes de que un problema en el codo le obligara a dar por terminada la temporada.
La pregunta es si los Yankees todavía tienen un hueco real en la rotación de titulares para él. Según los registros públicos de contratos, Cole y Rodon tienen contrato hasta 2028 y Fried hasta 2032. Schlittler se ha consolidado como lanzador titular de primera línea, mientras que Warren sigue bajo el control del club. Schmidt podrá acogerse al arbitraje en 2027 y podrá convertirse en agente libre tras esa temporada.
Las reacciones en Internet pasaron rápidamente del domingo al invierno. Los aficionados se preguntaban por la resistencia de Schmidt, cómo encajaría junto a Luis Gil y si los Yankees podrán contar con él para lanzar entradas decisivas en octubre.
Ningún responsable de los Yankees ha dicho que Schmidt no vuelva a ser titular en Nueva York. Pero la profundidad de la rotación, su plazo de recuperación y los planes de los Yankees para la postemporada lo han dejado relegado a un segundo plano, con tantas opciones de titulares que ya no puede seguir siendo tu opción predeterminada.
Los Yankees necesitan que Schmidt demuestre que la transición al bullpen funciona
Por eso es tan importante lo del bíceps, aunque las noticias médicas sigan siendo positivas. Schmidt no está intentando llegar a los 90 lanzamientos. Lo que quiere es demostrar que puede calentar rápido, salir al campo cuando lo necesiten y recuperarse para otra salida.
La transición ya ha dado lugar a dos momentos incómodos. Schmidt calentó el sábado por la noche, pero Boone se decantó por Michael Fulmer en la novena entrada de un partido empatado. Fulmer encajó el jonrón de dos carreras de Pavin Smith que decidió el partido. El domingo, Schmidt estuvo a punto de salir al campo, pero unos calambres se lo impidieron.
Los Yankees tienen un balance de 89-66, a seis partidos del Tampa Bay en la División Este de la Liga Americana, cuando quedan siete partidos por disputar, según la clasificación de la MLB. Ya se han asegurado una plaza en la postemporada y ocupan el primer puesto de comodín de la Liga Americana. Su última semana empieza el martes en el Yankee Stadium contra los Rays.
Si Schmidt pasa la prueba, esos partidos supondrán un reto más sencillo. Su objetivo inmediato ya no es volver a ganarse un puesto en la rotación. Se trata de demostrar a los Yankees que pueden confiar en él en el bullpen cuando empiece octubre.
¿Qué te parece? Deja tu comentario aquí abajo.

item.title: [Empire Sports Media] Yankees' three-homer day somehow made the standings uglier
item.dc:creator: Alexander Wilson
item.description: The Yankees hit three homers in Arizona on Saturday and still walked away with an 8-4 loss. Heliot Ramos, Spencer Jones and George Lombard Jr. all went deep, which should have been plenty of oxygen for a club trying to chase Tampa Bay. Instead, Will Warren gave up four earned runs in 4 1/3 innings, John Schreiber gave up two more in the eighth, and the Yankees fell to 89-66.
