item.content:encoded:
The Yankees hit three homers in Arizona on Saturday and still walked away with an 8-4 loss. Heliot Ramos, Spencer Jones and George Lombard Jr. all went deep, which should have been plenty of oxygen for a club trying to chase Tampa Bay.
Instead, Will Warren gave up four earned runs in 4 1/3 innings, John Schreiber gave up two more in the eighth, and the Yankees fell to 89-66. They are six games behind the Rays with a four-game series against Tampa Bay packed into three days starting Tuesday. It is a brutal spot after a game with three home runs on the board.
The Yankees cannot live on solo shots
The frustrating part is not that the Yankees lost a road game in September. It is that they got the type of offensive noise that normally buys a team room to breathe, then gave it all back before the night was over.
Ramos has been a useful part of this group, and Jones brought the kind of power that keeps making the October roster debate complicated. Lombard’s homer was another reminder that the young infield is not going to sit quietly just because the calendar got serious.
None of that changes the larger issue. Three solo shots are not a plan when the pitching staff is handing the other side too many extra chances. The Yankees needed cleaner innings from Warren, and they needed the bullpen to keep the game from turning into a chase.
Tampa Bay is waiting for a mistake
The Rays do not need to make a speech about this series. They have a six-game cushion, while the Yankees have four direct opportunities to cut into it. A six-game gap supplies plenty of urgency on its own.
I am not pretending one series erases everything that came before it. But it can change the temperature fast. A split leaves New York scrambling for help elsewhere, while a big run gives the final week a pulse.
Saturday felt like the kind of game that gets brushed off in July. On September 20, with Tampa Bay next, it landed much harder.
More about:New York Yankees

item.title: [New York Daily News] Yankees playoff roster prediction: Who makes the cut with division dreams dwindling ahead of Rays series?
item.dc:creator: Gary Phillips
item.description: Shortly after getting walked-off by the Diamondbacks on Saturday night, the Yankees acknowledged their reality. “Mathematically, [it’s] probably pretty tough, but you never know,” Cody Bellinger said of winning the American League East. Unable to bounce back with an 8-4 loss in Sunday’s series finale against Arizona, the second-place Yankees are now six games back of the division-leading Rays with seven games left in the regular season. The rivals will play four of those games against each other
item.content:encoded:
Shortly after getting walked-off by the Diamondbacks on Saturday night, the Yankees acknowledged their reality.
“Mathematically, [it’s] probably pretty tough, but you never know,” Cody Bellinger said of winning the American League East.
Unable to bounce back with an 8-4 loss in Sunday’s series finale against Arizona, the second-place Yankees are now six games back of the division-leading Rays with seven games left in the regular season. The rivals will play four of those games against each other at Yankee Stadium this week, starting with a doubleheader on Tuesday.
Aaron Boone acknowledged that his team will probably have to sweep the Rays just for a crack at the division crown, as FanGraphs gave the Yankees a measly 2.7% chance of winning the AL East before Sunday’s game.
“There’s still a chance,” Cam Schlittler said, “but we gotta play our asses off a little bit.”
While the Yankees still technically have a shot to defy the odds, the far likelier scenario is that their postseason begins on Sept. 29 at home against Boston in the Wild Card round for the second straight year.
With that in mind, let’s try to predict what the club’s roster could look like for that series.
Hitters (15): Ben Rice, Heliot Ramos, Spencer Jones, Trent Grisham, Cody Bellinger, Ryan McMahon, George Lombard Jr., Paul Goldschmidt, Luis García Jr., Jazz Chisholm Jr., José Caballero, Austin Wells, Ali Sánchez, Anthony Volpe, Amed Rosario
With the Yankees providing minimal info on Aaron Judge’s calf strain, it can’t be assumed he’ll be available.
Jazz Chisholm Jr. could return from a sprained thumb as soon as Tuesday. Meanwhile, Trent Grisham is still in play as a playoff option as he recovers from a hamstring strain, but Boone said that activating him before the end of the regular season is “complicated,” partly due to roster logistics.
With Max Schuemann presumably the corresponding move for Chisholm, the Yankees would have to option someone else if they activated Grisham before the playoffs. That someone wouldn’t be able to be recalled for 10 days barring a new injury; it seems like Jasson Domínguez is being protected from that window in case he’s needed for the Wild Card roster.
Grisham has been doing baseball activities and is “pretty deep into his running progression,” Boone said. If he is on the Wild Card roster, the Yankees will have an interesting decision to make between him and Spencer Jones in center field.
Third base could also be a conundrum, as Ryan McMahon and José Caballero don’t offer much offensively, and Amed Rosario is a poor defender. He’s only on the roster as an option against lefties, even though he hasn’t been great against them.
Another idea would be to use Volpe, who has been playing second, at third against lefties since he played a few games there in the minors this season. However, he doesn’t have a strong arm, and he hasn’t been working at third base since being recalled. Volpe said that the Yankees have not talked to him about manning the hot corner before the regular season ends.
“We’ll see,” Boone said. “First things first, getting Jazz back, and then we’ll figure out as the week unfolds how I want to play it.”
Volpe can also play second over Chisholm against lefties.
Pitchers (11): Cam Schlittler, Gerrit Cole, Max Fried, Will Warren, David Bednar, Brent Headrick, Paul Blackburn, Clarke Schmidt, John Schreiber, Tim Hill, Ryan Weathers
As things stand, Carlos Rodón, Max Fried, Gerrit Cole and Cam Schlittler are scheduled to pitch against the Rays, in that order. That would give Cole, who has struggled to get swing-and-miss, an extra day of rest if he were to start Game 1 of the Wild Card round. Schlittler, the AL Cy Young frontrunner, would be on regular rest if tabbed for Game 1.
Because the Wild Card round is a best-of-three series, Rodón isn’t needed, especially with Will Warren expected to work out of the bullpen and able to provide length.
Warren, slated to make one more start this season after struggling on Sunday, is one of a few converted starters who could impact the Bombers’ bullpen this postseason. Clarke Schmidt and Ryan Weathers are the others. Schmidt, being cautious in his return from Tommy John surgery, couldn’t come into Sunday’s game due to some bicep cramping, while Weathers isn’t expected to return from a flexor strain before the regular season ends.
Still, neither Boone nor pitching coach Matt Blake ruled out the idea of Weathers’ first game back coming in the playoffs.
“I don’t know if ‘comfortable’ is [the right word],” Blake said, “but it might be the course of action where he’s the best option even though he hasn’t pitched in the last three or four weeks.”
As for the relievers that the Yankees have leaned on all season, David Bednar, Paul Blackburn and Brent Headrick headline the group. All have been used heavily, especially Headrick.
The lefty allowed a grand slam to Nolan Arenado and saw his fastball velocity down an average of 1.3 mph during his major league-leading 79th appearance on Sunday, but he insisted that he feels fine physically. Boone also downplayed concerns over Headrick’s ongoing velocity fluctuations, though he did say that he hopes to get him and other relievers “in a good spot” with some rest ahead of the playoffs.
That said, the Yankees still haven’t been eliminated from the AL East race. They’ll keep trying to take the division from the Rays until they are.
“We’re going to show up Tuesday,” Boone said, “and try and kick their butt.”

item.title: [Pinstripes Nation] Boone Retira Su Controvertida Declaración Sobre Los Yankees Tras La Fea Derrota Ante Arizona Y Lanza Una Advertencia A Los Rays

item.content:encoded:
PHOENIX — Los Yankees se fueron del Chase Field con el tipo de derrota que cambia el panorama de la última semana.
El domingo, Nueva York tuvo a Corbin Burnes contra las cuerdas, remontó un déficit inicial y se puso con una ventaja de 4-1 gracias a tres jonrones en la tercera entrada. Heliot Ramos empató el partido con un jonrón solitario. George Lombard Jr. sumó un jonrón de dos carreras, y Spencer Jones conectó otro justo después de él. Burnes se fue del partido tras 2 2/3 entradas.
La ventaja inicial no duró mucho. Will Warren llenó las bases con un out en la quinta entrada, y el bullpen de los Yankees no pudo evitar que Arizona le diera la vuelta al partido. Brent Headrick ponchó a Geraldo Perdomo y luego concedió una base por bolas a Corbin Carroll con las bases llenas. Nolan Arenado siguió con un grand slam ante una bola rápida de cuatro costuras a 94,2 mph, dando la vuelta a un marcador de 4-2 y poniendo a los Diamondbacks por delante 6-4. Arizona sumó dos carreras más en la séptima y ganó 8-4.
Los Yankees perdieron dos de tres partidos en Arizona y ahora tienen un balance de 89-66. Tampa Bay mejoró su balance a 95-60, lo que deja a Nueva York a seis partidos de distancia en la División Este de la Liga Americana, cuando quedan siete partidos por disputar. Los Rays llegan al Yankee Stadium para una serie de cuatro partidos que empieza el martes con una doble jornada dividida. Una sola victoria de Tampa Bay en la serie dejaría a los Yankees fuera de la lucha por el título de la división.
Ese contexto hizo que las declaraciones del entrenador tras el partido tuvieran más peso que un simple intento de pasar página. Los Yankees ya se han asegurado una plaza en la postemporada, pero el club tiene que encontrar el equilibrio entre una lucha por el título de división que se va desvaneciendo y proteger a un cuerpo de lanzadores muy castigado, además de preparar una plantilla plagada de lesiones para octubre.
La afirmación de Boone choca con la clasificación
A Aaron Boone le preguntaron cómo se enfrentarían los Yankees a Tampa Bay y si el hecho de que la lucha por el título de división se esté desvaneciendo podría cambiar su forma de gestionar los minutos de juego. Su respuesta incluyó una amplia defensa de cómo ha respondido su equipo durante una temporada llena de lesiones y una importante racha negativa este verano.
«Y hemos estado a la altura en casi todas las ocasiones», dijo Boone.
Esa es la parte que llama la atención del mensaje de Boone. Aaron Judge estuvo más de tres meses de baja por una lesión en las costillas, volvió el 8 de septiembre y luego volvió a entrar en la lista de lesionados por una distensión en la pantorrilla derecha. Además, Nueva York sufrió una racha de siete derrotas seguidas durante un tramo de 4 victorias y 14 derrotas, antes de recuperarse y asegurarse una plaza en la postemporada.
El final del partido en Arizona fue el contrapunto. Los Yankees llegaron a la quinta entrada con una ventaja de tres carreras y la terminaron perdiendo por dos. No anotaron nada después de la tercera y encadenaron dos derrotas seguidas tras ganar el primer partido del viernes por 9-2.
Las cifras cuentan dos historias diferentes sobre los Yankees
La clasificación de la MLB a fecha de 21 de septiembre muestra por qué Boone puede hablar de una temporada sólida, mientras que la tabla de la División Este de la Liga Americana presenta un panorama más sombrío.
Los Yankees han marcado 137 carreras más que sus rivales, frente a la diferencia de +83 de Tampa Bay. Según las previsiones de la MLB, Nueva York debería tener un balance de 92-63, tres victorias más que su balance real. Sin embargo, los Rays llevan una ventaja de seis partidos.
Nueva York tiene un balance de 33-32 contra equipos con un porcentaje de victorias igual o superior al 50 %. Tampa Bay tiene un balance de 37-25 en esos partidos. La capacidad de los Yankees para anotar y evitar carreras sugiere que son un equipo más fuerte de lo que indica su segunda posición en la clasificación, pero los Rays han sabido convertir los partidos difíciles en victorias con mayor consistencia.
Ese contraste es lo que le da tensión a la afirmación de Boone. Los Yankees se han recuperado de rachas perjudiciales, pero no con la frecuencia suficiente como para controlar la división de cara a la última semana.
Boone lanza un mensaje contundente a los Rays
Boone también dejó claro que no ve el martes como una puesta a punto inmediata de cara a la postemporada. Dijo que las decisiones sobre el descanso pueden dejarse para más adelante, una vez que los Yankees se enfrenten por primera vez al equipo al que llevan meses persiguiendo.
«Pero lo primero es lo primero: el martes vamos a salir al campo e intentar darles una buena paliza. Así de sencillo. Y lo mantendremos así de sencillo», dijo Boone.
A Tampa Bay le falta una victoria contra los Yankees para asegurarse el título de la División Este de la Liga Americana. Nueva York tiene que ganar los cuatro partidos para mantener vivas sus opciones de cara al último fin de semana.
Eso hace que Boone tenga que gestionar dos frentes a la vez. A los Yankees aún les queda una posibilidad matemática de ganar la división, pero la plantilla para la postemporada, la carga de trabajo del bullpen y los jugadores lesionados se están convirtiendo en las preocupaciones más prácticas de octubre. Nueva York también empieza la semana ocupando el primer puesto de comodín de la Liga Americana.
La carga de trabajo de Headrick añade urgencia a la decisión de Boone
La 79.ª salida de Headrick el domingo fue la segunda más alta de las Grandes Ligas. La velocidad media de su bola rápida fue inferior a la de esta temporada, aunque él lo achacó a la ejecución más que al cansancio.
Los Yankees han confiado en Headrick durante toda la temporada. El domingo quedó claro lo rápido que esa fortaleza puede convertirse en un motivo de preocupación en octubre. Se encontró con las bases llenas, estuvo a un out de salir del apuro, pero luego concedió la base por bolas y encajó el golpe decisivo de Arenado.
Boone dijo tras la derrota que el descanso podría formar parte del plan una vez que se decida el campeón de la división. Eso podría pasar ya el martes.
Hasta entonces, su postura pública está clara. Los Yankees no van a ceder la serie ante Tampa Bay, ni siquiera después de que el colapso de Arizona haya dejado la clasificación prácticamente decidida. La gran afirmación de Boone es ahora lo que los Yankees deben demostrar en el campo: tras decir que han sabido hacer frente a la adversidad en casi todas las ocasiones, su próxima prueba llega con los Rays en posición de celebrar la victoria en el Yankee Stadium.
¿Qué opinas? Deja tu comentario más abajo.

item.content:encoded:
The New York Yankees led 4-1 after three innings on Sunday in Arizona. Three home runs off Corbin Burnes had knocked the Diamondbacks starter out of the game and given the lineup exactly the kind of start it needed.
None of it held. A five-run fifth inning turned a comfortable lead into a deficit, and the Yankees fell 8-4 at Chase Field to drop two of three in the series. New York is 89-66 and now sits six games behind the Rays in the American League East with seven to play.
After the game, manager Aaron Boone met with the media and offered an honest assessment of how it all fell apart.
Boone on Warren’s Start
Will Warren carried a 4-1 lead into the fifth inning before things unraveled. Warren allowed three consecutive baserunners in the fifth, loading the bases with one out, and Boone pulled him for Brent Headrick.
Boone’s evaluation was measured. He saw a pitcher whose stuff was there but whose command slipped at the wrong time.
“Early on he was in the strike zone really well and getting a lot of first pitch strikes ahead,” Boone said. “His stuff was again good. I feel like it’s been in a good place for the last three or four weeks now, but just started falling behind a little bit there in the latter part of the game.”
Warren had retired hitters efficiently through four innings, but back-to-back frames in which he fell behind multiple hitters proved costly. The stuff did not abandon him. The execution did.
The Offense Went Quiet
The Yankees scored all four of their runs in the third inning. Spencer Jones, Heliot Ramos, and George Lombard Jr. all connected off Burnes to build what felt like a comfortable lead.
After that, nothing. The Diamondbacks’ bullpen shut the door, and the lineup could not find a way to respond after the fifth-inning collapse.
“They’ve got a good relief corps. Obviously a lot of big arms,” Boone said. “I thought we had some decent at-bats along the way, but just obviously weren’t able to build on the lead or crawl our way back in.”
A Late Concern Emerges for the Yankees
Boone also provided an update on Clarke Schmidt at the end of his postgame session.
“He felt some cramping in his bicep when he was warming up, so obviously he didn’t want to take any chances there,” Boone said. “He checked out pretty well afterwards and all the strength tests. And so I’m hoping it’s not a big deal. But enough to have him not go into the game.”
Final Word for the Yankees
The Yankees blew a three-run lead and dropped a series they needed. The division is slipping away. The bullpen showed cracks on a day where the workload caught up with one of its most reliable arms.
Boone was honest about all of it. Warren’s stuff was good but the execution faltered. The offense disappeared after the third inning.
The Rays come to the Bronx on Tuesday for a doubleheader. The margin for error is gone.

item.content:encoded:
PHOENIX — Una sola entrada convirtió una serie fuera de casa que los Yankees parecían dispuestos a salvar en una derrota que les acompañó hasta su regreso al Bronx.
El domingo, en el Chase Field, Nueva York llegaba a la parte baja de la quinta con una ventaja de tres carreras. Para cuando terminó la entrada, Nolan Arenado ya había dado la vuelta a las bases, Arizona había anotado cinco veces y los Yankees se habían quedado atrás para siempre, acabando por perder 8-4 ante los Diamondbacks.
Con esta derrota, los Yankees quedan con un balance de 89-66 y a seis partidos de los Tampa Bay Rays, cuando solo quedan siete partidos por jugar. Además, esto puso fin a una gira por Arizona con un balance de 1-2, después de que Nueva York empezara la serie con una victoria por 9-2 y luego perdiera dos veces en partidos que se decidieron en los últimos compases.
Los Yankees ya se han asegurado una plaza en la postemporada y siguen ocupando el primer puesto de comodín de la Liga Americana. Pero la última semana tiene ahora un carácter de urgencia diferente. Tampa Bay puede hacerse con el título de la División Este de la Liga Americana con una sola victoria en la serie de cuatro partidos que empieza el martes en el Yankee Stadium.
El domingo también se prolongó el drástico cambio de rumbo tras el partido inaugural del viernes. El sábado terminó con un jonrón decisivo de Pavin Smith contra Michael Fulmer. El último partido trajo consigo otro fallo del bullpen, pero el mismo perjuicio en la clasificación.
Una entrada de cuatro carreras debería haber cambiado el rumbo de la tarde
Arizona se adelantó en el marcador gracias a un sencillo impulsador de Geraldo Perdomo en la primera entrada. A partir de ahí, Will Warren se asentó en el montículo, impidiendo que los Diamondbacks ampliaran su ventaja hasta la cuarta entrada y dando tiempo a la alineación para atacar a Corbin Burnes.
Ese ataque llegó de repente en la tercera entrada.
Heliot Ramos empató el partido con su decimotercer jonrón. George Lombard Jr. le siguió más adelante en la entrada con un jonrón de dos carreras, el quinto de la temporada.
El batazo de Lombard recorrió, según las estimaciones de Statcast, 424 pies, el jonrón más largo de su carrera en las Grandes Ligas.
Spencer Jones conectó un jonrón justo después, su undécimo. A continuación, lanzó una bola que se calculó que recorrió 448 pies. Los dos jonrones de los novatos sumaron un total de 872 pies.
Los Yankees habían pasado de ir perdiendo 1-0 a ponerse 4-1 por delante y habían obligado a Burnes a abandonar el partido tras solo 2 2/3 entradas. Parecía el tipo de remontada de los jóvenes que podría sacar adelante a una alineación en la que faltaban los titulares lesionados.
En cambio, esas cuatro carreras fueron toda la producción ofensiva de los Yankees.
Diecinueve outs demuestran lo mucho que ha dado un giro el partido
Cinco relevos de los Diamondbacks sumaron entre todos 6 1/3 entradas sin encajar carreras tras la salida de Burnes. Los Yankees solo consiguieron tres hits contra ese grupo y no anotaron en las últimas 19 eliminaciones.
Justin Martínez lanzó una quinta entrada sin permitir carreras y se llevó la victoria, mejorando su balance a 3-0. Brent Headrick cargó con la derrota, quedando con un balance de 7-4. No se concedió ningún salvamento.
Los Yankees terminaron el día con 216 jonrones, liderando la Liga Americana, pero su poderío no pudo compensar el colapso que vino después.
Warren y Headrick pierden el quinto
Warren llegó a la quinta entrada defendiendo la ventaja de 4-1. Lars Nootbaar conectó un doble, Ketel Marte un sencillo y Gabriel Moreno recibió una base por bolas, llenando las bases con un out. Aaron Boone recurrió a Brent Headrick, uno de los lanzadores del bullpen más utilizados por los Yankees.
Headrick ponchó a Perdomo y luego concedió una base por bolas a Corbin Carroll con las bases llenas, dejando el marcador en 4-2. Arenado mandó una bola rápida justo fuera por la línea del jardín izquierdo antes de conectar con fuerza el siguiente lanzamiento para un grand slam, dando a Arizona una ventaja de 6-4.
Headrick disputaba su 79.ª salida, la segunda cifra más alta de las Grandes Ligas, y, según se informó, la velocidad media de su bola rápida estaba aproximadamente 1,3 mph por debajo de su media de la temporada.
Headrick dijo que el problema era la precisión, no el cansancio.
«Me sentí bien, pero me faltó precisión y me quedé atrás respecto a los bateadores», dijo Headrick.
Warren se fue del partido con cuatro carreras encajadas, seis hits y tres bases por bolas en 4 1/3 entradas. Boone ha dicho que Warren hará una salida más como titular en la temporada regular contra Baltimore antes de pasar al bullpen en octubre.
Warren apoyó al relevo que se hizo cargo de la situación complicada que él había dejado.
«Nos ha dado un montón de problemas todo el año», dijo Warren. «Es un rollo, pero está claro que contamos con él, y nos ha ido muy bien con él todo el año, y va a seguir haciéndolo bien».
Arizona sigue sumando mientras el bullpen de los Yankees flaquea
Perdomo impulsó una carrera con un triple ante John Schreiber en la séptima entrada, y Carroll le siguió con un sencillo impulsor que dejó el marcador final en 8-4. Arizona terminó con siete carreras sin respuesta y se aseguró su 47.ª victoria tras remontada, la mejor marca de la MLB.
Los Yankees también se quedaron sin poder ver a Clarke Schmidt en el bullpen, como tenían previsto. El lanzador diestro tuvo que dejar de calentar por unos calambres cerca del brazo que se le había operado. Las primeras pruebas de fuerza fueron alentadoras, y se esperaba que Schmidt fuera examinado una vez que el equipo volviera a Nueva York.
Por qué esta podría ser la derrota más cara de los Yankees en 2026
Tras dos derrotas seguidas en Arizona, los Yankees vuelven al Yankee Stadium con Tampa Bay en condiciones de zanjar la lucha por el título de la División Este de la Liga Americana en el campo de Nueva York.
El daño va más allá de haber desperdiciado una ventaja. El Tampa Bay llega ahora al Bronx y solo necesita una victoria en la doble jornada del martes para asegurarse el título de la División Este de la Liga Americana, ya que esa victoria también le garantizaría el desempate en la serie de la temporada.
Eso da lugar a la consecuencia más incómoda del colapso de Arizona: los Yankees podrían verse obligados a ver cómo los Rays celebran el título de división en el Yankee Stadium, en el mismo campo donde Nueva York esperaba mantener viva la lucha hasta la última semana.
¿Qué le parece? Deje su comentario a continuación.

item.content:encoded:
Field Level Media

21 Sep 2026, 11:49 GMT+10

(Photo credit: Erik Williams)
Mike Yastrzemski capped a four-run sixth inning with a three-run homer, and the visiting Atlanta Braves clinched the National League East with a 4-2 victory over the Houston Astros on Sunday.
The Braves swept the three-game interleague series and claimed their seventh division pennant over the last nine seasons. Yastrzemski was the last of four batters to reach safely against Astros left-handed reliever Bryan King (3-6), who didn't record a single out and exited after allowing Yastrzemski's 12th homer of the season.
Jose Altuve and Yainer Diaz homered for the spiraling Astros, who will enter the final week of the regular season one game behind the Texas Rangers in the American League West.
Astros starter Hunter Brown allowed just three singles and two walks over five shutout innings. Braves starter Martin Perez navigated traffic, allowing just one run on six hits and two walks in 4 1/3 innings.
Rays 5, Red Sox 1
Tampa Bay's Jonny DeLuca and Chandler Simpson drove in two runs apiece during a four-run first inning, Victor Mesa Jr. homered and the Rays defeated visiting Boston in St. Petersburg, Fla.
With the win, the Rays completed their final regular-season homestand with an 8-1 record and wrapped their home schedule with a major league-best 55-26 mark.
Trevor Story homered, and Roman Anthony and Caleb Durbin each went 2-for-4 for the Red Sox, who managed just six hits while losing their second straight game.
Pirates 4, Royals 3
Rafael Flores Jr. belted a go-ahead two-run homer in the eighth inning to cap Pittsburgh's three-game sweep over visiting Kansas City. With the win, the Pirates improved to 14-6 in their last 20 games.
Oneil Cruz went deep to lead off the fourth inning and Spencer Horwitz had an RBI single in the sixth for Pittsburgh. Carmen Mlodzinski earned the win after allowing two runs on three hits in three innings.
Vinnie Pasquantino had a pinch-hit two-run homer for the Royals, who have lost four in a row and seven of their past eight games.
Phillies 7, Mets 2
Cristopher Sanchez tossed 6 1/3 solid innings and earned the victory for visiting Philadelphia, which earned a much-needed win over New York.
Luis Arraez was 1-for-4 with two RBIs for the Phillies. Justin Crawford provided insurance in the eighth with a bases-clearing triple off Kodai Senga. Sanchez (18-6) gave up two runs on six hits. Philadelphia sits four games ahead of the Arizona Diamondbacks in the race for the final National League wild card.
Bo Bichette homered for the Mets, who dropped their home finale for the third time in four years, while Brett Baty had a pinch-hit run-scoring single in the seventh. Francisco Alvarez and A.J. Ewing each singled twice.
Cubs 9, Reds 1
Pete Crow-Armstrong tied the major league lead with his 45th home run, and David Peterson held host Cincinnati to one run on three hits in six innings in Chicago's win.
Crow-Armstrong was 3-for-5 with two RBIs, three runs, his 30th double and his 38th stolen base. He matched Philadelphia's Kyle Schwarber at 45 homers, and he became the first center fielder in history with 40 home runs, 30 doubles and 30 steals in a season.
Michael Conforto and Seiya Suzuki also homered for the Cubs. JJ Bleday hit a home run for the Reds, who have dropped three of four.
Cardinals 5, Nationals 3
Leo Bernal's two-run home run capped a three-run eighth inning, and St. Louis rallied for a win against visiting Washington to salvage the finale of the three-game series.
Ivan Herrera tied it 3-3 with one out when he hit his second solo homer of the day. Luis Gastelum (5-3) pitched a scoreless inning for the win. Jose Fermin had two hits for the Cardinals, who had lost four straight.
CJ Abrams homered, and Daylen Lile had a double and a single for Washington, which had won six of seven.
Mariners 2, Rockies 1
Kade Anderson threw seven scoreless innings, allowing just three hits in the longest outing of his rookie season, and visiting Seattle stayed alive in the postseason race with a win over Colorado in Denver.
Dominic Canzone had two hits and two RBIs for Seattle, which gained a game on the Texas Rangers in the AL West. Closer Andres Munoz left the game in the ninth with an apparent right arm injury.
Hunter Goodman's 39th home run of the season couldn't prevent Colorado from moving within one loss of its fourth consecutive 100-loss season.
Blue Jays 7, Rangers 2
Nathan Lukes and Charles McAdoo each had two RBIs to lead Toronto to a win over Texas in Arlington, Texas.
Kazuma Okamoto broke a 2-2 deadlock with an RBI single in the fifth and gave the Blue Jays a lead they would never relinquish as they remained three games back of the final AL wild-card spot. Spencer Arrighetti (9-9) picked up the win, allowing two runs in 2 1/3 innings during a bullpen game.
Jake Burger delivered the Rangers' lone runs on a game-tying two-run homer in the fourth. Jacob deGrom (11-10) had a shaky outing, giving up three runs with five hits in 4 1/3 innings for Texas, which maintained its one-game lead in the AL West despite the defeat.
Brewers 3, Orioles 0
Jacob Misiorowski set the tone with three shutout innings and Milwaukee blanked host Baltimore for the second game in a row to complete a three-game sweep and set a franchise record for regular-season victories.
William Contreras homered, and Cooper Pratt provided two run-scoring singles with two outs. Milwaukee is two games ahead of the Los Angeles Dodgers for the best record in the National League. Misiorowski's ERA dipped to 1.86.
The Orioles further damaged their fading playoff hopes, losing the first three games of the homestand to fall five games back of the Chicago White Sox for the final American League wild-card spot. Colton Cowser had two of Baltimore's four hits. Orioles starter Brandon Young (9-5) was charged with two runs in six innings.
Diamondbacks 8, Yankees 4
Nolan Arenado hit his third grand slam of the season to cap a five-run fifth and Arizona kept its slim National League wild-card chances alive with a victory over New York in Phoenix.
Geraldo Perdomo had two hits and two RBIs and five Arizona relievers limited the Yankees to three hits in 6 1/3 scoreless innings. The D-backs remained five games behind NL wild-card leaders Chicago Cubs and San Diego Padres and four behind the Philadelphia Phillies with six to play.
Heliot Ramos, George Lombard Jr. and Spencer Jones homered for the Yankees, who fell six games behind Tampa Bay in the AL East. The Yankees lead the American League with 216 homers. Lombard had two hits.
Twins 8, Angels 0
Dean Kremer allowed one hit over six innings and Alan Roden went 3-for-5 with a home run and four RBIs as Minnesota earned a split of its four-game series with Los Angeles in Anaheim, Calif.
Josh Bell had three hits, a walk, two RBIs and a run while Brooks Lee also had three hits and scored three times for Minnesota, which finished with 13 hits. Kremer (4-5) allowed just a fourth-inning leadoff single to Vaughn Grissom.
Ryan Johnson (5-9) suffered the loss for Los Angeles, which finished the 2026 season with a 34-47 home record.
Guardians 1, Athletics 0
Gavin Williams threw seven shutout innings to lift Cleveland past the visiting Athletics.
Williams (14-8) gave up only three hits while throwing 63 of 89 pitches for strikes. Steven Kwan had three hits and Cade Smith earned his 39th save as the Guardians swept the series and remain atop the American League Central.
A's starter Jack Perkins (3-12) gave up five hits and one run in six innings. Zack Gelof had two of the team's six hits as the Athletics suffered their sixth straight loss
Dodgers 3, Giants 1
Emmet Sheehan pitched brilliantly in long relief, Enrique Hernandez broke a seventh-inning tie with a run-scoring double and Los Angeles completed a three-game sweep of visiting San Francisco.
Tommy Edman homered for the Dodgers, who trailed 1-0 after one inning before Sheehan took over to start the second and held the Giants to just one hit with nine strikeouts over the next 5 1/3 scoreless innings.
Jung Hoo Lee and Victor Bericoto singled for the only hits for the Giants, who completed their road schedule with a 28-53 record. Sam Hentges (1-7) allowed a pair of one-out singles in the seventh before Hernandez's double for a 2-1 edge.
Padres 7, Marlins 3
Jake Cronenworth homered twice and knocked in a season-high five runs while Fernando Tatis Jr. also homered as host San Diego polished off a three-game sweep and finished 6-0 against Miami this season.
The Padres won their fifth straight game and are 13-1 in their last 14 games. Walker Buehler (9-6) worked 6 2/3 innings, allowing three hits and three runs.
Sandy Alcantara (13-11) absorbed the loss for the Marlins after permitting eight hits and four runs over six innings. Alcantara is winless in his last eight starts.
White Sox 8, Tigers 1
Chase Meidroth hit a two-run homer for Chicago and Sam Antonacci's two-run double highlighted a 2-for-4 performance as the White Sox waited through a rain delay of nearly four hours and played in wet, blustery conditions to beat Detroit.
Five pitchers held the Tigers to six hits and five walks as Detroit was limited to a single run for the third time in the series. Huascar Brazoban (6-2), reinstated prior to the game from the 15-day injured list (left lat strain), pitched for the first time since Aug. 24. He allowed a hit in one inning to get his first victory with the White Sox.
Tigers starter Troy Melton (8-5) allowed four runs in 3 2/3 innings, giving up four hits before exiting with a trainer. Detroit pitchers allowed eight walks, with White Sox third baseman Miguel Vargas (1-for-2) drawing three of them. Eduardo Valencia went 3-for-4 for the Tigers, who were eliminated from postseason contention.
--Field Level Media

Geraldo Perdomo had two hits and two RBIs and five Arizona relievers limited the Yankees to three hits in 6 1-3 scoreless innings as the D-backs scored the final se
item.content:encoded:
Field Level Media

21 Sep 2026, 04:55 GMT+10

(Photo credit: Arianna Grainey)
Nolan Arenado hit his third grand slam of the season to cap a five-run fifth and the Arizona Diamondbacks kept their slim National League wild card chances alive with an 8-4 victory over the New York Yankees on Sunday in Phoenix.
Geraldo Perdomo had two hits and two RBIs and five Arizona relievers limited the Yankees to three hits in 6 1-3 scoreless innings as the D-backs scored the final seven runs for their major league-leading 47th comeback win.
Heliot Ramos, George Lombard Jr. and Spencer Jones homered for the Yankees, who fell six games behind Tampa Bay in the AL East. The Yankees lead the American League with 216 homers. Lombard had two hits.
Lars Nootbaar and Gabriel Moreno had two hits and scored twice and Ketel Marte had two hits for the Diamondbacks, who have won two straight games.
The D-backs (82-74) remained five games behind NL wild-card leaders Chicago Cubs and San Diego Padres (both 87-69) and four behind the Philadelphia Phillies (86-70) with six to play.
The D-backs would lose a tiebreaker to the Cubs, and tiebreakers against the Padres and Phillies have yet to be determined. The D-backs end the season with three games at Colorado and the final three at San Diego.
Justin Martinez (3-0), the second Arizona reliever to follow Corbin Burnes, struck out two in the fifth for the victory.
The Yankees lost their second straight after winning four of five.
Nootbaar started the D-backs' five-run fifth with a one-out double off Yankees starter Will Warren. Marte singled and Moreno walked to load the bases. Brent Headrick (7-4) entered and struck out Perdomo before walking Corbin Carroll to force in a run.
Arenado followed with his 381-foot homer into the Arizona bullpen for a 6-4 edge. He has five homers in his last 10 games and is tied with Houston's Yordan Alvarez for the major league lead in grand slams.
Perdomo tripled in a run and scored on Carroll's single in a two-run seventh.
The D-backs took a 1-0 lead in the first on singles by Nootbaar, Marte and Perdomo. Warren gave up six hits and four runs in 4 1/3 innings, with three walks and four strikeouts.
Ramos, Lombard and Jones homered four batters apart in a four-run third off Burnes for a 4-1 lead. Ramos homered with two outs before Luis Garcia Jr. singled and Lombard and Jones hit back-to-back shots. Lombard's went an estimated 424 feet. Jones' went 448.Burnes gave up four runs and five hits, with two walks and two strikeouts in 2 2/3 innings. He has given up nine runs and five homers in 10 1-3 innings of three starts since returning after a 15-month absence after Tommy John surgery.
--Field Level Media

The New York Yankees' bid for the AL East crown may be all but lost, as they sit six games behind division-leader Tampa Bay Rays in the standings with seven games remaining in the regular season, but the important thing is that they have secured a spot in the Wild Card round — marking their 27th postseason berth in 34 seasons (they are curre
item.content:encoded:
Yankees news: Clarke Schmidt to see doctor amid new injury concerns appeared first on ClutchPoints. Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here.
The New York Yankees' bid for the AL East crown may be all but lost, as they sit six games behind division-leader Tampa Bay Rays in the standings with seven games remaining in the regular season, but the important thing is that they have secured a spot in the Wild Card round — marking their 27th postseason berth in 34 seasons (they are currently in the middle of a 34-year winning season streak).
The key now for the Yankees is keeping their key players healthy. While the Yankees have been mostly healthy on the pitching side of things, reliever Clarke Schmidt, who returned to big-league action on September 16 after a lengthy layoff, suffered some bicep cramping on Sunday, which then prevented him from suiting up in their 8-4 loss to the Arizona Diamondbacks.
While Bob Nightengale of USA Today reported that Schmidt's inability to show up on the mound was merely precautionary, he will be meeting with a doctor back in New York to ascertain that he's not suffering from any underlying serious injury that could keep him out for an extended period once more.
Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)
Schmidt didn't make his 2026 season debut until September after he underwent elbow surgery (internal brace procedure), so at least he's not suffering any setbacks in that regard.
The 30-year-old righty struck out two in 0.2 innings of work in his only appearance of 2026 in a 5-4 loss for the Yankees against the Minnesota Twins.
The Yankees have already been dealt a huge injury blow, with Aaron Judge, who only recently returned to action, suffering a calf strain that sent him back to the injured list. They already have Jazz Chisholm Jr. and Trent Grisham among lineup regulars already on the IL.
While New York has enough depth to make up for the absences of a few players, they would want to enter the postseason as close to full strength as they can get. With the Wild Card round set to begin in nine days, they have some time to get it together from a health standpoint.
Related: Yankees' Spencer Jones shuts down injury concern ahead of postseason

Jones went 1-for-4 with a solo home run in Sunday's 8-4 loss to the Diamondbacks.
Jones sat out due to foot soreness Saturday, but he was back in the lineup Sunday. He had gone 1-for-19 with nine strikeouts over his previous four games. The outfielder is batting .248 with a .759 OPS, 11 homers, 39 RBI, 33 runs scored, 12 doubles, one triple and nine stolen bases over 81 contests this season. With Trent Grisham (hamstring) sidelined for the rest of the regular season, Jones has a clear path to starting in center field until the postseason.

item.content:encoded:
PHOENIX — The Yankees’ chances of winning the AL East are on life support.




Access the Yankees beat like never before


Join Post Sports+ for exciting subscriber-only features, including real-time texting with Greg Joyce about the inside buzz on the Yankees.
Try it free
Of greater concern is whether their bullpen meltdown Sunday was just a bad day or represents cracks emerging in a heavily worked unit.
Brent Headrick served up a grand slam to Nolan Arenado in the fifth inning, flipping the game on its head and all but wrapping up the Yankees’ spot in the AL wild-card series next week after an 8-4 loss to the Diamondbacks at Chase Field.
By dropping the series finale, a game they once led 4-1, the Yankees (89-66) fell to six games back of the Rays with seven to play.
They will welcome the Rays to Yankee Stadium on Tuesday for a four-game showdown, needing a sweep to stay alive in the division race. One win by the Rays in The Bronx will secure them the AL East title.
The Yankees would then turn their attention to securing the top AL wild card, ending Sunday leading the Red Sox by 5 ¹/₂ games, though Aaron Judge’s questionable status for that series because of a calf strain looms over everything.
In the meantime, Sunday’s loss — on the heels of Saturday’s walk-off win by the Diamondbacks (82-74) — was another regrettable one after third-inning home runs by Heliot Ramos, George Lombard Jr. and Spencer Jones had staked them to a 4-1 lead.
In the bottom of the fifth, Will Warren loaded the bases with one out, at which point Aaron Boone called on reliable lefty Headrick for his 79th appearance of the season — the second most in the majors.
Before Sunday, Headrick had inherited 50 runners this season and allowed only five of them to score.
But after striking out the first batter he faced, Headrick walked Corbin Carroll to force in a run, which brought Arenado to the plate.
Shop Yankees Merch
Arenado crushed Headrick’s 2-0 fastball just to the left of the left field foul pole, but then straightened it out on the very next pitch (another fastball), clobbering a grand slam to put the Diamondbacks ahead 6-4.
The Diamondbacks later added a pair of insurance runs off John Schreiber in the seventh inning, the first earned runs Schreiber has allowed as a Yankee.

item.content:encoded:
Instead, they face the very real prospect that Tampa Bay will soon celebrate a division crown in the Bronx, sending the Yankees into their second consecutive assignment to host the Red Sox in the AL Wild Card Series.
Nolan Arenado hit a fifth-inning grand slam off Brent Headrick as the Yankees absorbed an 8-4 loss on Sunday afternoon at Chase Field. With seven games remaining, New York trails Tampa Bay by six games in the division race.
Heliot Ramos, George Lombard Jr. and Spencer Jones all hit third-inning homers to chase Corbin Burnes early, with Lombard and Jones going back to back.
The rookies’ blasts traveled a combined Statcast-projected 872 feet; Lombard’s 424-footer was the longest of his career, which Jones followed with a 448-foot drive.
Will Warren allowed four runs on six hits and three walks over 4 1/3 innings. Yankees manager Aaron Boone confirmed that Warren will draw one more start during the regular season, set to face the Orioles, before transitioning to a bullpen role during the playoffs.
Headrick issued a bases-loaded walk to Corbin Carroll, then saw Arenado crush a drive just foul down the left-field line before pouncing on the next pitch for a grand slam that put Arizona ahead.

item.content:encoded:
In the final game and rubber match of their three-game road series against the Arizona Diamondbacks (82-74), the Yankees (89-66) coughed up an early lead to lose 8-4.
Here are the takeaways...
-- Will Warren got the nod to start the game, and delivered a solid outing... until the fifth inning. Up to that point, Warren had allowed one earned run - an RBI single in the first inning by Diamondbacks shortstop Geraldo Perdomo - and struck out four batters through four full innings. The Yankees entered the fifth inning leading 4-1 (thanks to home runs from Heliot Ramos, George Lombard Jr., and Spencer Jones), but after Warren surrendered two hits and a walk to load the bases with just one man out, he was pulled in favor of left-handed reliever Brent Headrick.
-- Headrick struck out Perdomo to record the second out, but he couldn't close the door on the frame, issuing a free pass to Corbin Carroll to bring in one run before surrendering a grand slam to Nolan Arenado which gave Arizona a 6-4 lead.
-- Of those five earned runs surrendered in the fifth, three were attributed to Warren, and two to Headrick.
-- New York's right-handed reliever John Schreiber allowed two more runs in the seventh inning, surrendering a triple to Perdomo and a single to Carroll which brought the shortstop home. For Arizona, former Yankee Jonathan Loáisiga recorded the final six outs, facing the minimum six batters without allowing a run to wrap up the 8-4 loss.
Game MVP: Nolan Arenado
Arenado's grand slam flipped the game on its head, and the massive momentum-shifting blast gave the Snakes a lead they wouldn't relinquish.
Highlights
What's next
The Yankees travel back home on Monday and will kick off a pivotal three game series against the AL East divisional leading Tampa Bay Rays on Tuesday at 1:05 p.m.
Of course, now 6.0 games back of Tampa Bay for first place in the AL East with just seven regular season games remaining, the Yankees need a miracle to win the division.
Carlos Rodón (2.95 ERA, 1.13 WHIP in 76.1 IP) is set to take the mound for the Yankees.
The Rays will send out Nick Martinez (2.94 ERA, 1.07 WHIP in 171.1 IP).

item.content:encoded:
Yankees news: Why Cam Schlittler was pissed at himself after NY's loss to Diamondbacks appeared first on ClutchPoints. Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here.
Cam Schlittler wasn't happy with his performance on the mound after the New York Yankees' 5-3 loss to the Arizona Diamondbacks on Saturday night.
Schlittler is going through the second season of his career in the majors with the Yankees. He has quickly broken out as one of the best young pitchers, helping New York be firm in the playoff picture this year.
Schlittler started on the mound as he lasted six innings, striking out six batters while conceding three hits and one earned run. New York lost on Pavin Smith's pinch-hit, two-run homer in the ninth inning, resulting in Arizona's victory. He blamed himself for those mistakes after the game.
Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)
"I mean, I wouldn't say I really gave them a chance,'' Schlittler said. "That one's kind of on me, so I'll take the blame for that. Made an error there, let up two runs."
"I mean, there's still a chance,'' Schlittler said, "but we got to play our (butts) off a little bit.'
How Cam Schlittler, Yankees played against Diamondbacks
Cam Schlittler and the Yankees have preparation for the postseason. These last games of the regular season will decide their place in the AL bracket, needing every win they can get.
The game was scoreless throughout the first four innings, seeing both teams finally get on the board in the fifth frame. However, Arizona dealt more blows as New York was unable to muster up more big plays to rally back against the hosts.
New York fell to an 89-65 record on the season, sitting at second place in the AL East Division standings. They are above the Boston Red Sox and the Toronto Blue Jays while trailing the Tampa Bay Rays.
The Yankees will look to bounce back in their series finale against the Diamondbacks. That contest commences on Sept. 20 at 4:10 p.m. ET.

item.content:encoded:
The final road game of the 2026 regular season is upon us, as the Yankees will conclude it with a seven-game homestand before likely hosting the Red Sox for the Wild Card Series. If the season ends there, this is the end of the line for the gray uniforms for 2026, but obviously, we all hope we'll see them next in Tampa (and more) in early October.
Looking to end a road slate that has been very generous to the Yankees on a high note is Will Warren, who's finishing his sophomore season strong after his great start to the campaign unraveled into a bit of a mess over the summer. Rotation reinforcements that threatened to throw him in the bullpen never came with the recurring injuries, so he'll finish 2026 with 30 starts for the second straight season. This is No. 29, as he enters with a 3.89 ERA (108 ERA+) and 4.07 FIP in 148 innings. No matter what happens from here, Warren has had a successful year in solidifying himself as a true MLB-caliber rotation arm.
Opposing him will be a former Cy Young winner trying to round into form off Tommy John surgery in Corbin Burnes, whom Yankees fans remember well from his lone season in Baltimore in 2024. Returning from a 16-month absence on September 8 to help with the playoff push, Burnes has allowed five runs across 7.2 innings with six strikeouts to two walks against the Royals and Marlins. He isn't totally built up, having thrown 75 pitches in his last start, so expect him to settle around 80-85 today. He's always befuddled the Yankees, pitching to a 1.93 ERA across 23.1 innings in his career, but he doesn't have a win in any of those four starts.
Ben Rice will once again lead off, followed by Cody Bellinger, Heliot Ramos, and Luis García Jr. We've seen better ABs and swings from George Lombard Jr. lately, who'll bat fifth. Spencer Jones is back after a one-day absence due to a sore foot and will bat in front of Anthony Volpe, Austin Wells, and José Caballero.
Lars Nootbaar will also be a repeat leadoff hitter for the D-backs, followed by Ketel Marte, Gabriel Moreno, and Geraldo Perdomo. Corbin Carroll is batting fifth, Nolan Arenado will bat sixth, and former Blue Jay Jesús Sánchez bats seventh ahead of last night's hero Pavin Smith and Tim Tawa.

item.dc:creator: Cole Shelton
item.description: The New York Yankees avoided a major injury to star outfielder Spencer Jones. New York is already without Aaron Judge, so losing Jones before the playof
item.content:encoded:
The New York Yankees avoided a major injury to star outfielder Spencer Jones.
Jones didn't play on Saturday due to an injury; it isn't considered long-term
New York is coming off a 5-3 loss to the Arizona Diamondbacks on Saturday, as the Yankees will look for the series win on Sunday.
New York Yankees Get Injury Update on Spencer Jones
After Jones didn't play on Saturday due to an injury, there was some concern about him. New York is already without Aaron Judge, so losing Jones before the playoffs begin would be a blow.
Yet, the injury to Jones doesn't seem serious, according to the MLB.com injury report, as he was available off the bench.
"Jammed his heel during Twins series earlier in the week, Jones said Sept. 19. Could be available off the bench," the injury report read.
The hope for the Yankees is Jones could return to the lineup on Sunday, or Tuesday when they begin a series against the Tampa Bay Rays. They could opt to give Jones another day off on Sunday to give him three full days off to make sure his jammed heel is fully healthy.
Yankees manager Aaron Boone, meanwhile, confirmed Jones was available off the bench on Saturday if needed.
"He was available, like I would've… if a spot came up to hit or we needed to do something I would've gone to him," Boone said.
Jones also said the injury was no big deal and doesn't need an IL stint.
Jones is hitting .248 with 10 home runs and 38 RBIs with the Yankees this season in 80 games in his first MLB season.
New York Right Now
The Yankees will be a Wild Card team again this year but could be without star slugger Aaron Judge.
Judge is back on the IL due to a right calf strain and he said he hopes he can return for the playoffs.
"I'd like to be back by the postseason," Judge said. "That's definitely the plan. [It's the] 10-day IL, so the 10th day is probably the last game of the season. So we'll see. I've got really no answers for you on any timeline or anything like that."
Judge doesn't know the grade of the strain, but is confident he can return for the playoffs.
"I've dealt with strains before and kind of played through them, but this was kind of in a different spot where it made it a little bit more difficult," Judge said.
The Yankees are 89-65 and 5 games back of the Rays for the top spot in the AL East.

Yahoo Sports | Tate Mosher: Headed into what
item.content:encoded:
New York Post | Greg Joyce: The Yankees cannot afford any more additions to their M*A*S*H unit. Unfortunately, at least for Saturday, there is another. Spencer Jones, who’s been outstanding at the plate lately, was out of the starting lineup Saturday with a sore foot. For his part, Jones did not seem worried and attributed the soreness to playing in Arizona Friday after jamming his heel earlier in the week against the Twins. Here’s hoping he’s right.
Yahoo Sports | Tate Mosher: Headed into what was likely his penultimate regular season start of 2026, Cam Schlittler’s incredible campaign has the attention of people all over baseball. Cam’s been so sensational that he’s earned MVP chatter, an award that pitchers rarely hoist. The last to do it? Future Hall of Famer Clayton Kershaw. Earlier on Saturday, MLB’s official X account made sure everyone is tracking the similarities between the latter’s 2014 season and Cam’s 2026 campaign. Whether Schlittler can take home AL MVP or not, it’s been a heck of a ride. And you know you’ve had a brilliant season when you’re getting comped to Peak Kershaw.
MLB | Bryan Hoch: All Cam, all the time. The burgeoning ace has been so spectacular that it has become difficult for those closest to him to express just how good he has been. Through 31 starts, his 1.95 ERA trails only Ron Guidry’s 1.71 ERA in 1978. His 21 starts of one run or fewer are the most in franchise history. And in the past 11o years, only three pitchers his age or younger have matched him, including Babe Ruth in 1916.
CBSSports | Mike Axisa: Meanwhile, if you hadn’t heard, Aaron Judge is headed back to the IL, this time with a calf injury. In the aftermath of the Captain’s injury, Axisa takes a look at a few questions for Judge, and for the Yankees at large. For Judge, if he can return in time for a playoff run, how much has the injury set him back? Will he be able to find his timing at the dish? For the Yankees, if Judge is out or ineffective, where does that leave the offense against southpaws? It sure would be nice if Judge returns in good order and quickly finds his footing.
The Athletic | Brendan Kuty ($): Speaking of Judge’s calf injury, there’s a little bit of clarification on its nature, if not its severity or a timeline. The injury is in Judge’s inner, lower calf. That part of the calf is important for “sustained activities such as standing or walking uphill.” Judge has previously played through calf injuries. This time, however, it’s in a spot that makes doing so more difficult. So here we are, with the best hitter in the world back on the IL as the Yanks approach the postseason.

item.title: [Pinstripes Nation] Spencer Jones Da Un Buen Susto A Los Yankees Por Una Lesión, Ya Que El Césped Del Chase Field Le Ha Hecho Daño En El Talón

item.content:encoded:
PHOENIX — Los Yankees llegaron a Arizona con el objetivo de mantener su puesto en la postemporada, sin dejar de luchar por una oportunidad cada vez más lejana de ganar la División Este de la Liga Americana. Para el sábado por la noche, la clasificación ya no era más que una parte del problema.
El propio Chase Field se había convertido en algo con lo que Aaron Boone tenía que lidiar.
Nueva York llegaba al domingo con un balance de 89-65 tras perder por 5-3 en la última entrada ante los Diamondbacks, a cinco partidos de Tampa Bay cuando solo quedan ocho partidos por disputar. Los Yankees seguían ocupando el primer puesto de comodín de la Liga Americana, pero su margen para hacer frente a otra lesión se había reducido después de que Aaron Judge volviera a la lista de lesionados de 10 días por una distensión en la pantorrilla derecha.
Las decisiones de Boone del sábado reflejaron esa realidad. José Caballero fue titular en el centro del campo por segunda vez esta temporada. Cody Bellinger se quedó en la izquierda en lugar de cambiar de posición, a pesar de que tiene mucha experiencia jugando en el centro del campo. Boone explicó más tarde que Bellinger también estaba notando el estrés acumulado por la superficie sintética y que no quería aumentar la carga sobre él.
Esa cautela se mantuvo durante todo el partido, que los Yankees acabaron perdiendo por un jonrón de dos carreras de Pavin Smith en la novena entrada. También fue importante porque Nueva York está a punto de marcharse de Arizona para afrontar una serie crucial de cuatro partidos contra Tampa Bay en el Yankee Stadium, que empieza el martes con una doble jornada en la que se repartirán las victorias. Los Yankees ya se han asegurado una plaza en la postemporada, pero el equipo sigue buscando el equilibrio entre la lucha por el título de división y mantener intacta su plantilla para octubre.
La preocupación por el estado del césped dejó de ser un simple detalle de gestión de la alineación en cuanto Boone explicó por qué faltaba otro titular. Los Yankees habían llegado a un punto en el que un pie lesionado más podía complicar tanto su alineación en los jardines como la profundidad de plantilla que podrían necesitar durante la última semana.
Ese cálculo es especialmente importante en el centro del campo, donde Boone tiene menos combinaciones con las que está acostumbrado a trabajar una vez que empieza a proteger a los jugadores de las lesiones. Un ajuste de una sola noche puede convertirse rápidamente en un problema para la plantilla si las molestias persisten de cara a la recta final de la temporada.
Jones se queda fuera tras un repunte del dolor en el talón al jugar sobre césped artificial
Spencer Jones no jugó el sábado por unas molestias en el pie izquierdo y el talón, después de haberse dado un golpe en el talón a principios de semana en Minnesota. Jones dijo que las molestias se agravaron por el desgaste de haber jugado el viernes por la noche en el césped del Chase Field.
El novato restó importancia al tema antes del partido y dijo que esperaba que la baja durara solo un día.
«No es nada grave», dijo Jones.
Jones describió el problema como una molestia más que como una nueva lesión aguda. También lo relacionó directamente con la superficie y con los impactos que habían absorbido sus pies.
«Solo estoy un poco magullado», dijo Jones. «Jugar sobre césped artificial es diferente, es duro para los pies».
Boone dijo que la situación de Jones se evaluaría día a día y que estuvo a punto de dejarlo en la alineación. También dejó claro que los Yankees no consideraban que Jones estuviera fuera de combate.
«Simplemente me pareció que, sobre todo al estar aquí en el césped artificial, se había dado un golpe en el talón en Minnesota y, al volver a jugar en césped [el viernes], creo que es algo que hay que valorar día a día», dijo Boone. «Incluso creo que podría jugar esta noche».
Las declaraciones de Boone tras el partido son lo que más tranquilidad dan
Jones no llegó a salir en el partido del sábado, pero Boone dijo después que la decisión se debió más a la situación del partido que a motivos médicos. El entrenador dijo que habría sacado a Jones si los Yankees hubieran tenido el enfrentamiento adecuado o lo hubieran necesitado al final del partido.
«Estaba disponible, igual que yo lo habría estado… si hubiera surgido una oportunidad de batear o hubiéramos tenido que hacer algo, habría recurrido a él», dijo Boone.
Esa distinción es importante. A Jones no le han dado de baja, ni lo han puesto en la lista de lesionados, ni le han prohibido hacer nada relacionado con el béisbol. El domingo por la mañana, los Yankees seguían considerando el problema como una molestia pasajera.
La profundidad en el centro del campo hace que un día de descanso cobre más importancia
Los Yankees pueden permitirse que se pierda un solo partido. La situación de la plantilla se complica si Jones necesita más tiempo.
Jones ha jugado 80 partidos esta temporada y tiene un promedio de bateo de .248, con un porcentaje de embasado de .318 y un porcentaje de slugging de .433. Lleva 10 jonrones, 12 dobles, un triple, 38 carreras impulsadas y nueve bases robadas en 265 turnos al bate. Baseball Savant le atribuye 23 hits de más de una base, es decir, uno cada 11,5 turnos al bate.
Su valía también se nota en cómo los Yankees pueden colocar al resto del equipo. Caballero puede jugar de central, pero el sábado fue solo su segunda titularidad en esa posición esta temporada. Boone decidió expresamente no cambiar a Bellinger al centro por culpa del césped artificial y de la propia carga de trabajo de Bellinger.
Los Yankees también llamaron a Max Schuemann cuando Judge entró en la lista de lesionados, dando prioridad a la versatilidad defensiva. Esa decisión le da a Boone otra opción en todas las posiciones del campo y en los jardines, pero no sustituye la potencia de Jones como bateador zurdo ni su papel habitual en el centro del campo.
Los Yankees llegan a la última jornada de la serie con una duda sobre su estado físico
Los Yankees cierran la serie contra Arizona el domingo, antes del día de descanso del lunes. Ese descanso le da a Jones un poco más de tiempo para recuperarse antes de los cuatro partidos contra los Rays en tres días en el Yankee Stadium.
Por ahora, el último informe médico sigue siendo alentador. Jones espera que las molestias sean pasajeras, Boone lo consideraba apto para jugar el sábado y el club no ha dado a entender que se esté planteando incluirlo en la lista de lesionados.
La pregunta que queda es si un día de descanso del césped del Chase Field será suficiente para que el talón se recupere antes de que los Yankees empiecen la serie más importante que les queda en el calendario de la temporada regular.
¿Qué opinas? Deja tu comentario más abajo.

item.content:encoded:
Aaron Judge's regular season may be over, but that doesn't mean the Yankees' has to be.
A mystery calf ailment popped up suddenly on Wednesday and has resulted in the Yankees captain being placed on the injured list. It's unclear whether he will return in 2026, even if he's eligible to return next weekend. Aaron Boone did not give any information on the severity of the calf issue, but the timeline is likely not good due to how tricky those injuries prove to be.
A scenario is now potentially unfolding that would have only appeared in Boone's nightmares: a postseason without the best hitter in baseball, with a lineup that struggled mightily without him. Even if they seemed to gradually improve as time went on, particularly in August, it would be a massive blow if he cannot return.
You can't replace a guy like Judge midseason; you can merely do your best to make up for his absence. Fortunately, on a platoon-heavy team like this, they should have plenty of options to build a lineup without him for the playoffs.
What the playoff lineup should look like against right-handed pitching
- Ben Rice (DH)
- Cody Bellinger (LF)
- Luis García Jr. (1B)
- Heliot Ramos (RF)
- Spencer Jones (CF)
- Jazz Chisholm Jr. (2B)
- George Lombard Jr. (SS)
- Austin Wells (C)
- Ryan McMahon (3B)
This lineup simultaneously features the easiest decisions, but also the roughest circumstances. Having a guy like Judge as the ultimate lineup balancer who mashed both lefties and righties allowed you to use plenty of left-handed hitters at the top of the order, something that the team has in abundance.
The best right-handed hitter on the roster without Judge is hard to pinpoint, especially since all of them are significantly worse against same-handed pitching. Heliot Ramos might just be the best option to bat highest among them, which would be cleanup in this scenario.
It's not an ideal situation in the slightest. Even if you don't think it makes sense to bat Ramos that high because of his struggles against righties, there is some merit to breaking up the team's many left-handed bats. In a lineup that will likely only feature one other righty, it has to be considered.
The fate of this lineup when they're out there, which would likely be mostly after a potential Wild Card Series with the Red Sox, would hinge on the middle. Spencer Jones and Jazz Chisholm Jr. got hot in August and helped the offensive turnaround begin, but both are heavily streaky bats with contact issues. If they go cold, this lineup might limp through games like they did in July.
What the playoff lineup should look like against left-handed pitching
- Paul Goldschmidt (1B)
- Cody Bellinger (LF)
- Heliot Ramos (RF)
- Ben Rice (DH)
- George Lombard Jr. (SS)
- Spencer Jones (CF)
- Jazz Chisholm Jr. (2B)
- Anthony Volpe/José Caballero (3B)
- Austin Wells (C)
Here's where it gets interesting. How far do you lean into the platoons on a team with several players designated to specifically hit lefties, especially against a team that will likely lean heavily on those types of pitchers in Boston?
Many Yankees fans believe that it would be improper to take a guy like García, who is likely the team's second-best pound-for-pound hitter with Judge injured, out of the lineup, but you don't really have a choice here. He's slashing just .238/.274/.363 against lefties, while Goldschmidt has been among the team's best hitters against them for the last two seasons. Add in Rice's improvements against same-handed pitching, and it just needs to be done.
Using him in a different position is also just not happening. He has not played second base, where he was extremely poor, since 2025. The only position he's played this season is first base. If he wasn't so dreadful out there, maybe he could replace Chisholm, a mediocre hitter against lefties in his own right.
Speaking of defense, you might notice the lack of Amed Rosario, and that's intentional. Rosario's use on this roster was almost exclusively predicated on his ability to hit left-handed pitching, but he's been significantly worse at it this season. Add in his truly dreadful defense, and you have a conundrum.
Anthony Volpe is a better hitter than José Caballero, but there are questions about how his arm strength would play at third, where he's also very inexperienced with just three games played in Triple-A. Caballero would probably get the nod here, but he's someone who just plays better off the bench with his speed and versatility.
It's also an aggressive placement for Lombard, batting fifth in his first career playoff game. The results haven't quite been there yet for him, but he's always been significantly better against lefties and should be slid up the lineup and be treated as one of those platoon bats who are there to hit that handedness, even if it might lead to consequences in the bullpen.
Boston is loaded with left-handed pitching from the rotation to the bullpen, so there will be few opportunities to get to a guy like García on the bench. The rest of the bench would be situational with pinch runners and pinch hitters.
Things ultimately look particularly shallow, but is there a chance that some last-minute reinforcements could help out?
Could Trent Grisham or Giancarlo Stanton return to provide relief?
It seems unlikely, especially early in the postseason, but the Yankees are refusing to shut the door on either Trent Grisham's or Giancarlo Stanton's return.
Grisham, who suffered a Grade 2 hamstring strain earlier this month, was revealed to be "pretty far along" in his running program, and Boone said it's not out of the question that he returns in the season's final days, although an exact timeline for that has not been spelled out. If Grisham is physically ready to get back on the field, it would provide a boost, even if he might not be starting over Jones at this point.
Stanton, who's been out since April due to two separate calf strains and a re-aggravation, has continued to hit through his rehab, but hasn't resumed running as of last Sunday. Considering how it took several weeks for him to even get close to back from injury with his running program last time, this likely doesn't put him in play until the ALCS at the earliest.
While Stanton seems significantly less likely to get into a game again this season, there is a path for Grisham. The team could use him and Ramos in a platoon situation to add yet another lefty to the lineup against right-handed pitching. They could also utilize him as a pinch hitter on a larger bench than usual, due to the team's propensity to carry fewer than 13 pitchers in the Wild Card Series.
The real question for Grisham is defensive. While Jones has absolutely looked shaky in center field, the struggles of Grisham out there are well documented. Add in his diminished athleticism and likely balky hamstring straight off an injury, would it be better if the team just chanced it by throwing him in right field when he plays?
He hasn't played the position since a disastrous error lost the Brewers the 2019 Wild Card Game against the Nationals, but playing it at Yankee Stadium is significantly easier than dealing with the spacious center field. Of course, this is something the Yankees would have to determine their willingness to do beforehand and have him practice the position, so what plans they have will be determined by that.
As for Stanton if he's ever medically able to get back? There just might not be any room for him with Rice as the permanent DH. You don't want to take the bat out of either of their hands, and with the team seemingly having to juggle multiple guys coming off soft-tissue injuries, can they afford to use a roster spot for a designated pinch hitter as they did with 2022 Matt Carpenter?

item.content:encoded:
The New York Yankees fell in heartbreaking fashion on Saturday night against the Los Angeles Dodgers, losing on a walk-off two-run shot from Pavin Smith.
New York is now 89-65 on the season and still sits firmly in the top Wild Card spot but trails the Tampa Bay Rays by five games for the AL East division.
Currently, the biggest concern for the Yankees stems from injuries, as Aaron Judge, Giancarlo Stanton, and Jazz Chisholm Jr. are all sidelined. Even rookie slugger Spencer Jones seems to be dealing with some type of foot injury.
Aaron Boone Makes Statement on Jones’ Decision
Fortunately, Jones’ injury does not seem serious as he said pregame it was “no big deal.”
In fact, Boone said that he was available off the bench during Saturday night’s game and ultimately explained why he didn’t use him as a pinch-hitter.
After a reporter asked Boone if Jones was available or if he was trying to stay away from him because of the injury, Boone made it clear that he would’ve gone to him if the right spot emerged.
“He was available, like I would’ve… if a spot came up to hit or we needed to do something I would’ve gone to him,” Boone said.
Aaron Boone speaks to the media following the Yankees 5-3 loss tonight in Arizona. pic.twitter.com/aeBBxybvHN
— YES Network (@YESNetwork) September 20, 2026
Looking at the Yankees
New York will play the Diamondbacks one more time on Sunday and then, after a day off Monday, will begin a massive four-game set with the Rays. If they can sweep the series, they could get back into the race over the final three games of the regular season.
On Tuesday, the two teams will play a doubleheader and then wrap it up across Wednesday and Thursday, with the Yankees likely throwing their top four guys in Max Fried, Carlos Rodon, Gerrit Cole, and Cam Schlittler.

item.content:encoded:
The New York Yankees secured a 9-2 series-opening victory over the Arizona Diamondbacks on Friday night.
Now, they're once again back in action on Saturday evening with right-handed ace and AL Cy Young favorite Cam Schlittler on the mound for the Yankees, while the Diamondbacks will have righty Brandon Pfaadt pitching.
Ahead of the matchup, manager Aaron Boone didn't make any major changes to his starting lineup, but he did make some notable changes to his batting order.
Yankees Announce George Lombard Jr. Move
With outfielder Spencer Jones getting the day off and veteran Paul Goldschmidt out of the lineup after leading off on Friday, rookie shortstop George Lombard Jr. is moving up in the batting order.
After hitting seventh in the series opener, Boone is placing Lombard Jr. in the five-hole Saturday, while Heliot Ramos bats cleanup and Ben Rice moves back into the leadoff role.
Cody Bellinger and Luis Garcia Jr. will remain in their normal roles, hitting second and third.
Here's the full Yankees lineup:
Via Underdog MLB: "Yankees 9/19 B. Rice DH C. Bellinger LF L. García Jr. 1B H. Ramos RF G. Lombard Jr. SS A. Wells C A. Volpe 2B R. McMahon 3B J. Caballero CF C. Schlittler SP."
Yankees 9/19
B. Rice DH
C. Bellinger LF
L. García Jr. 1B
H. Ramos RF
G. Lombard Jr. SS
A. Wells C
A. Volpe 2B
R. McMahon 3B
J. Caballero CF
C. Schlittler SP
— Underdog MLB (@UnderdogMLB) September 19, 2026
Lombard Jr.'s 2026 Season
Since the Yankees called him up on Aug. 4, Lombard Jr. has exceeded expectations and made an immediate impact for New York.
He's appeared in 35 games and has gone 29-for-124 with 19 runs, four home runs, and 15 RBIs while hitting .234 with a .371 slugging percentage and a .663 OPS.
Looking at the Yankees
New York enters Saturday with an 89-64 overall record and currently holds the top Wild Card spot, which would set them up to host a Wild Card series at home in the Bronx.
That said, they're just 4.0 games back of the Tampa Bay Rays for first place in the AL East and the No. 1 overall seed in the AL, with an upcoming four-game set against the Rays this week.

The post New York Yankees Announce George Lombard Jr. Move During Diamondbacks Series appeared first on HEAVY.

item.content:encoded:
PHOENIX — In case the Yankees weren’t dealing with enough injury headaches for a 6-foot-7 slugger, Spencer Jones was out of the lineup Saturday with a sore left foot/heel.
The rookie outfielder claimed it was “no big deal” and chalked it up to the wear and tear of playing on Chase Field’s turf Friday night after jamming his heel in Minnesota earlier this week.




Access the Yankees beat like never before


Join Post Sports+ for exciting subscriber-only features, including real-time texting with Greg Joyce about the inside buzz on the Yankees.
Try it free
But after the Yankees just lost Aaron Judge to the injured list again with a right calf strain, the last thing they needed was Jones nursing an injury of his own.
“Just a little banged up,” Jones said before Saturday’s game against the Diamondbacks. “Playing on turf is different, hard on the feet.”
Aaron Boone also downplayed it, adding that he still almost kept Jones in the lineup before sitting him in favor of José Caballero, who started in center field for the second time this season.
“Just felt like especially being on the turf here, he kind of jammed that heel in Minnesota and being on the turf [Friday], so I think it’s just a day-to-day kind of thing,” Boone said. “I even view him as available tonight.”
Boone said he preferred to keep Cody Bellinger in left field instead of shifting him to center.
“I considered moving him to center, but Belli’s grinding too and the turf here kind of beats you up,” he said. “There’s some scenarios where I would move him to center. Tonight, just being on the turf and as much as he’s been through this year, I didn’t want to move him.”
When the Yankees officially placed Judge on the 10-day injured list Saturday, they opted for defensive versatility over offensive upside in his replacement.
That meant calling up Max Schuemann instead of Jasson Domínguez, giving the former another shot in the big leagues for at least a few days beginning this weekend against the Diamondbacks.
“Adding his versatility to our bench makes some sense,” Boone said. “And then obviously some different roster complications moving forward with the playoffs around the corner.”
Schuemann’s stay may be brief, with Jazz Chisholm Jr. potentially returning from the IL as soon as the upcoming series against the Rays at Yankee Stadium that begins Tuesday.
If Schuemann goes back to Triple-A to make room, he would not be available to be recalled for 10 days (unless he was replacing an injured player again), essentially ruling him out as an option for the AL wild-card series.
That may have played a part in Domínguez not getting the call this time, in case the Yankees wanted to use him as a pinch-running threat on their playoff roster.
The 23-year-old also offers value as a switch-hitter, but he has proven to be a defensive liability in the outfield.
The Yankees’ trip to Chase Field gave them a chance to reunite with former teammate Jonathan Loáisiga, who has finally stayed healthy for a full season in the Diamondbacks bullpen.
Shop Yankees Merch
The right-hander often flashed his talent during his eight-year tenure with the Yankees, but injuries too often got in the way.
This season, though, after signing a minor league deal with the Diamondbacks, Loáisiga has avoided the IL and pitched in a career-high 64 games with a 2.32 ERA entering Saturday.
“Been through a lot of battles over the years with Jonny,” Boone said. “It’ll be great to see him. Hopefully we can ding him a little bit here. I know he’s had a really strong year, which I’m excited about for him. He’s such a talented guy that for him, it’s always been about just being healthy. So the fact that he’s gone out there and had a largely healthy season, I’m not surprised at the success he’s had.”
The Diamondbacks held a 25th-anniversary celebration Saturday of their 2001 World Series team that beat the Yankees in seven games.
